before_page.title: Registers, Tensor Products, and Partial Trace

items.title: Finite registers and their ordered computational bases
items.statement:
For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

items.title: The trace pairing on a finite endomorphism space is nondegenerate
items.statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space. If $D:V\to V$ is linear
and $\operatorname{tr}(D\circ A)=0$ for every linear map $A:V\to V$, then $D=0$.
Equivalently, the trace pairing $(D,A)\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(D\circ A)$
has the property that its only first input pairing to zero with every second
input is $D=0$. This includes the zero space.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.7

items.title: Big-endian encoding of ordered bit strings
items.statement:
For $n\ge0$ and a binary word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})\in\{0,1\}^n$, define its
**big-endian index**

$$\operatorname{enc}_n(x):=\sum_{k<n}x_k\,2^{\,n-1-k}.$$

Thus the first wire is the most significant bit. For $n=0$, the domain
$\{0,1\}^0$ consists only of the empty word $()$, and the empty sum gives
$\operatorname{enc}_0(())=0$. In an ordered $n$-qubit
computational basis, the word $x$ occupies the slot numbered
$\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

items.title: Ordered tensor registers, their inner product, and wire permutations
items.statement:
An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

items.title: The computational basis is orthonormal
items.statement:
For every $d\ge1$, the ordered computational basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of
the register $Q_d$ from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] is an
orthonormal basis for its declared inner product. Separately, the one-dimensional
zero-qubit register has the basis $\{1\}$ by definition.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

items.title: Partial trace over a finite tensor factor
items.statement:
For a complex vector space $H$, write $\operatorname{End}(H)$ for the set of
linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-linear-map]]).

Let $H_A,H_B$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with fixed
ordered orthonormal bases $(e_i)_{i<a}$ and $(f_j)_{j<b}$, respectively. The
ordered product basis of $H_A\otimes H_B$ has the $A$ index first. For
$R\in\operatorname{End}(H_A\otimes H_B)$ define
$\operatorname{Tr}_B(R)\in\operatorname{End}(H_A)$ by

$$\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_B(R)\bigr)_{i i'}:=\sum_{j<b}R_{(i,j),(i',j)}.$$

Rows are output coordinates and columns are input coordinates, as in
[[def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map]]. If $b=0$, the sum is
empty and equals $0$. The notation $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ means that the second
factor is contracted; the first factor and its order are retained.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles

items.title: Tensor products of finitely many linear maps
items.statement:
For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

items.title: The product basis is orthonormal and tensor dimensions multiply
items.statement:
Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered list of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces with specified ordered orthonormal bases of
sizes $d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1}$, allowing $d_k=0$. The elementary tensors of the
factor bases, ordered lexicographically, form an orthonormal basis of the
tensor register, and

$$\dim(H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1})=\prod_{k<n}d_k.$$

For the empty list the product is $1$ and the tensor space is $\mathbb C$; if
any $d_k=0$, the tensor space is zero and the product basis is empty.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

items.title: Big-endian bit-string indices are bijective
items.statement:
For every $n\ge0$, the map
$\operatorname{enc}_n:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,\ldots,2^n-1\}$ of
[[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]] is a bijection. Any permutation of the
$n$ bit positions therefore induces a permutation of the corresponding
computational basis.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

items.title: The partial trace is characterized by the trace pairing and is basis-independent
items.statement:
For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_A,H_B$, the partial
trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B:\operatorname{End}(H_A\otimes H_B)\to
\operatorname{End}(H_A)$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_B R)\circ T\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(R\circ(T\otimes I_{H_B})\bigr)\quad\text{for every }R\in\operatorname{End}(H_A\otimes H_B)\text{ and }T\in\operatorname{End}(H_A).$$

Here $I_{H_B}$ is the identity map $y\mapsto y$ on $H_B$; $\operatorname{End}$
is the notation defined in [[def-qc-partial-trace]].

Its coordinate formula is independent of the chosen ordered orthonormal basis
of $H_B$. The assertion includes zero-dimensional factors.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles

items.title: Tensor maps preserve composition, identities, and adjoints
items.statement:
Let $(T_k:H_k\to K_k)_{k<n}$ and $(S_k:K_k\to L_k)_{k<n}$ be finite ordered
families of linear maps between finite-dimensional complex inner-product
spaces. Then

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}S_k\right)\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)=\bigotimes_{k<n}(S_kT_k),\qquad \bigotimes_{k<n}I_{H_k}=I_{\otimes_{k<n}H_k},\qquad \left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)^*=\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k^*.$$

In the first formula, $S_kT_k$ means $S_k\circ T_k$. Here $I_{H_k}$ denotes
the identity map $x\mapsto x$. All adjoints use the
repository pairing, linear in the first argument. The empty tensor-map
identity is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on $\mathbb C$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

items.title: Finite wire permutations are unitary basis permutations
items.statement:
Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces, with the product bases of
[[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For a permutation $\sigma$ of the
factor positions, the map $P_\sigma$ that reorders the factors is a bijective
linear isometry from $H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$ to
$H_{\sigma(0)}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{\sigma(n-1)}$. When source and target
are identified as the same register, $P_\sigma$ is a unitary operator in the
sense of [[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]].

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

items.title: The partial trace preserves non-negativity and total trace
items.statement:
For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_A,H_B$ and a
non-negative operator $R\in\operatorname{End}(H_A\otimes H_B)$,
$\operatorname{Tr}_B(R)$ is non-negative and

$$\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Tr}_B(R))=\operatorname{tr}(R).$$

Here $\operatorname{End}(H)$ is the set of linear maps $H\to H$ as in
[[def-qc-partial-trace]], $I_H$ denotes the identity map $x\mapsto x$, and both
conclusions include zero-dimensional factors.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles

significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

proposed_after_items.title: The trace pairing on a finite endomorphism space is nondegenerate
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space. If $D:V\to V$ is linear
and $\operatorname{tr}(D\circ A)=0$ for every linear map $A:V\to V$, then $D=0$.
Equivalently, the trace pairing $(D,A)\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(D\circ A)$
has the property that its only first input pairing to zero with every second
input is $D=0$. This includes the zero space.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.7

proposed_after_items.title: Big-endian encoding of ordered bit strings
proposed_after_items.statement:
For $n\ge0$ and a binary word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})\in\{0,1\}^n$, define its
**big-endian index**

$$\operatorname{enc}_n(x):=\sum_{k<n}x_k\,2^{\,n-1-k}.$$

Thus the first wire is the most significant bit. For $n=0$, the domain
$\{0,1\}^0$ consists only of the empty word $()$, and the empty sum gives
$\operatorname{enc}_0(())=0$. In an ordered $n$-qubit
computational basis, the word $x$ occupies the slot numbered
$\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

proposed_after_items.title: Ordered tensor registers, their inner product, and wire permutations
proposed_after_items.statement:
An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

proposed_after_items.title: The computational basis is orthonormal
proposed_after_items.statement:
For every $d\ge1$, the ordered computational basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of
the register $Q_d$ from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] is an
orthonormal basis for its declared inner product. Separately, the one-dimensional
zero-qubit register has the basis $\{1\}$ by definition.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

proposed_after_items.title: Partial trace over a finite tensor factor
proposed_after_items.statement:
For a complex vector space $H$, write $\operatorname{End}(H)$ for the set of
linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-linear-map]]).

Let $H_A,H_B$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with fixed
ordered orthonormal bases $(e_i)_{i<a}$ and $(f_j)_{j<b}$, respectively. The
ordered product basis of $H_A\otimes H_B$ has the $A$ index first. For
$R\in\operatorname{End}(H_A\otimes H_B)$ define
$\operatorname{Tr}_B(R)\in\operatorname{End}(H_A)$ by

$$\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_B(R)\bigr)_{i i'}:=\sum_{j<b}R_{(i,j),(i',j)}.$$

Rows are output coordinates and columns are input coordinates, as in
[[def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map]]. If $b=0$, the sum is
empty and equals $0$. The notation $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ means that the second
factor is contracted; the first factor and its order are retained.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles

proposed_after_items.title: Tensor products of finitely many linear maps
proposed_after_items.statement:
For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

proposed_after_items.title: The product basis is orthonormal and tensor dimensions multiply
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered list of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces with specified ordered orthonormal bases of
sizes $d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1}$, allowing $d_k=0$. The elementary tensors of the
factor bases, ordered lexicographically, form an orthonormal basis of the
tensor register, and

$$\dim(H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1})=\prod_{k<n}d_k.$$

For the empty list the product is $1$ and the tensor space is $\mathbb C$; if
any $d_k=0$, the tensor space is zero and the product basis is empty.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

proposed_after_items.title: Big-endian bit-string indices are bijective
proposed_after_items.statement:
For every $n\ge0$, the map
$\operatorname{enc}_n:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,\ldots,2^n-1\}$ of
[[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]] is a bijection. Any permutation of the
$n$ bit positions therefore induces a permutation of the corresponding
computational basis.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

proposed_after_items.title: The partial trace is characterized by the trace pairing and is basis-independent
proposed_after_items.statement:
For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_A,H_B$, the partial
trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B:\operatorname{End}(H_A\otimes H_B)\to
\operatorname{End}(H_A)$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_B R)\circ T\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(R\circ(T\otimes I_{H_B})\bigr)\quad\text{for every }R\in\operatorname{End}(H_A\otimes H_B)\text{ and }T\in\operatorname{End}(H_A).$$

Here $I_{H_B}$ is the identity map $y\mapsto y$ on $H_B$; $\operatorname{End}$
is the notation defined in [[def-qc-partial-trace]].

Its coordinate formula is independent of the chosen ordered orthonormal basis
of $H_B$. The assertion includes zero-dimensional factors.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles

proposed_after_items.title: Tensor maps preserve composition, identities, and adjoints
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $(T_k:H_k\to K_k)_{k<n}$ and $(S_k:K_k\to L_k)_{k<n}$ be finite ordered
families of linear maps between finite-dimensional complex inner-product
spaces. Then

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}S_k\right)\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)=\bigotimes_{k<n}(S_kT_k),\qquad \bigotimes_{k<n}I_{H_k}=I_{\otimes_{k<n}H_k},\qquad \left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)^*=\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k^*.$$

In the first formula, $S_kT_k$ means $S_k\circ T_k$. Here $I_{H_k}$ denotes
the identity map $x\mapsto x$. All adjoints use the
repository pairing, linear in the first argument. The empty tensor-map
identity is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on $\mathbb C$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

proposed_after_items.title: Finite wire permutations are unitary basis permutations
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces, with the product bases of
[[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For a permutation $\sigma$ of the
factor positions, the map $P_\sigma$ that reorders the factors is a bijective
linear isometry from $H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$ to
$H_{\sigma(0)}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{\sigma(n-1)}$. When source and target
are identified as the same register, $P_\sigma$ is a unitary operator in the
sense of [[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]].

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Appendix A.6

proposed_after_items.title: The partial trace preserves non-negativity and total trace
proposed_after_items.statement:
For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_A,H_B$ and a
non-negative operator $R\in\operatorname{End}(H_A\otimes H_B)$,
$\operatorname{Tr}_B(R)$ is non-negative and

$$\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Tr}_B(R))=\operatorname{tr}(R).$$

Here $\operatorname{End}(H)$ is the set of linear maps $H\to H$ as in
[[def-qc-partial-trace]], $I_H$ denotes the identity map $x\mapsto x$, and both
conclusions include zero-dimensional factors.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles

statement.before:
Let $\Phi_0,\Psi_0:\mathcal L(H_0)\to\mathcal L(H_1)$ and $\Phi_1,\Psi_1:\mathcal L(H_1)\to\mathcal L(H_2)$ be finite-dimensional channels. Then
$$\|\Psi_1\circ\Psi_0-\Phi_1\circ\Phi_0\|_\diamond\le\|\Psi_0-\Phi_0\|_\diamond+\|\Psi_1-\Phi_1\|_\diamond.$$
statement.after:
Let $H_0,H_1,H_2$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, and let $\Phi_0,\Psi_0:\mathcal L(H_0)\to\mathcal L(H_1)$ and $\Phi_1,\Psi_1:\mathcal L(H_1)\to\mathcal L(H_2)$ be finite-dimensional channels. Then
$$\|\Psi_1\circ\Psi_0-\Phi_1\circ\Phi_0\|_\diamond\le\|\Psi_0-\Phi_0\|_\diamond+\|\Psi_1-\Phi_1\|_\diamond.$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §3.3.2–3.3.4, tensor-product and composition properties.

before_page.title: Trace Distance, Fidelity, and Information Limits

items.title: Unitary Group Compact
items.statement:
For every positive integer $d$, the unitary group
$$U(d):=\{U\in M_d(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_d\}$$
is a compact Hausdorff topological group in the Euclidean topology inherited from the real and imaginary parts of its matrix entries.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §7.2, PDF pp.408–434; finite-dimensional unitary-group context; compactness is proved locally.

items.title: Diamond Norm
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces and let $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be complex-linear. For each finite $r\ge1$, the induced trace norm of the amplification is
$$\|\Phi\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb C^r}\|_{1\to1}:=\sup_{X\ne0}\frac{\| (\Phi\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb C^r})(X)\|_1}{\|X\|_1},$$
where $X\in\mathcal L(H\otimes\mathbb C^r)$ and $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the finite-dimensional trace norm ([[def-qc-trace-norm]]). The **diamond norm** (the completely bounded trace norm) is
$$\|\Phi\|_\diamond:=\sup_{r\ge1}\|\Phi\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb C^r}\|_{1\to1}.$$
There is no factor $1/2$ in this map norm. The finite-dimensional ancilla theorem [[thm-qc-diamond-norm-ancilla-dimension-bound]] proves the supremum is finite, is attained, and can be capped at $r=\dim H$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

items.title: Fidelity
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on $H$ (nonnegative operators of trace one; [[def-qc-density-operator]]). Their **root fidelity** is
$$F(\rho,\sigma):=\|\sqrt\rho\,\sqrt\sigma\|_1,$$
where $\sqrt\rho$ and $\sqrt\sigma$ are the unique non-negative square roots and $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the finite-dimensional trace norm ([[def-qc-trace-norm]]). This library uses root fidelity; the squared quantity $F(\rho,\sigma)^2$ is called squared fidelity.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.1–2, PDF pp.36–40; complete cross-read qc_r2 ledger, summary/corroboration only

items.title: Trace Distance
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on $H$ (nonnegative operators of trace one; [[def-qc-density-operator]]). Their **trace distance** is
$$D(\rho,\sigma):=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1,$$
where $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the trace norm ([[def-qc-trace-norm]]). The factor $1/2$ is part of this state-distance convention. The diamond norm below is an unhalved norm on maps.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.2, PDF pp.39–41; raw trace norm and optimal-measurement discussion

items.title: Faithful State Dominates Positive Operator
items.statement: Let $H$ be finite-dimensional, let $\sigma$ be a density operator that is positive definite on $H$, and let $X$ be a non-negative endomorphism of $H$. Then there is a finite real $c\ge0$ such that $X\le c\sigma$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §2.1.2–2.1.3, PDF pp.69–83; positive-operator and support conventions. The finite domination/support arguments are proved locally.

items.title: Symmetric Subspace Projector
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let $k\ge1$, and let $H^{\otimes k}$ use the ordered tensor product register and factor permutation convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For $\pi\in S_k$, let $U_\pi$ be the resulting unitary that permutes the $k$ tensor factors according to $\pi$. Define
$$\Pi_{\mathrm{sym},k}:=\frac1{k!}\sum_{\pi\in S_k}U_\pi.$$
The **symmetric subspace** is $\operatorname{Sym}^k(H):=\{v\in H^{\otimes k}:U_\tau v=v\text{ for every }\tau\in S_k\}$. For $k=0$, the tensor unit is one-dimensional and $\Pi_{\mathrm{sym},0}:=I$.

The permutation average is the orthogonal projector onto $\operatorname{Sym}^k(H)$ by [[lem-qc-symmetric-subspace-average-is-projector]].

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §7.1.1 Proposition 7.1, PDF pp.392–393

items.title: The two root-fidelity trace expressions agree
items.statement:
For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space,
$$\|\sqrt\rho\,\sqrt\sigma\|_1=\operatorname{tr}\sqrt{\sqrt\rho\,\sigma\,\sqrt\rho}.$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

items.title: Trace norm of a tensor product
items.statement:
For finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces $H_1,K_1,H_2,K_2$ and linear maps $A:H_1\to K_1$, $B:H_2\to K_2$,
$$\|A\otimes B\|_1=\|A\|_1\,\|B\|_1.$$
The equality includes zero maps and zero-dimensional factors.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §1.1.3, trace norm and singular-value decomposition; the tensor-product formula is proved locally.

items.title: Positive Marginals Imply Joint Support
items.statement: Let $H$ be finite-dimensional, let $Y\ge0$ act on $H\otimes H$, and let $S\subseteq H$ be a subspace. If both partial-trace marginals of $Y$ are supported on $S$, then $\operatorname{supp}Y\subseteq S\otimes S$; equivalently, $Y=(P_S\otimes P_S)Y(P_S\otimes P_S)$, where $P_S$ is the orthogonal projection onto $S$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §2.1.2–2.1.3, PDF pp.69–83; positive-operator and support conventions. The finite domination/support arguments are proved locally.

items.title: Pure state trace distance
items.statement:
For unit vectors $u,v$ in a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let $P_u=|u\rangle\langle u|$ and $P_v=|v\rangle\langle v|$. Then
$$D(P_u,P_v)=\sqrt{1-|\langle u|v\rangle_D|^2},$$
where $\langle\cdot|\cdot\rangle_D$ is the Dirac pairing converted from the root library's first-argument-linear inner product.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: Chapters 1–3; finite-dimensional adaptation specified in this contract

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.2, PDF pp.39–41; pure-state trace-norm calculation (2.155)–(2.158)

items.title: The permutation average is the symmetric-subspace projector
items.statement: Let $H$ be finite-dimensional and let $k\ge1$. The average $\Pi_{\mathrm{sym},k}=\frac1{k!}\sum_{\pi\in S_k}U_\pi$ is self-adjoint and idempotent, with range exactly $\operatorname{Sym}^k(H)=\{v:U_\tau v=v\ \forall\tau\in S_k\}$. For $k=0$ on the tensor unit, $\Pi_{\mathrm{sym},0}=I$ and its range is the full tensor unit.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

items.title: Diamond Norm Ancilla Dimension Bound
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, $d=\dim H$, and let $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be linear. Then
$$\|\Phi\|_\diamond=\|\Phi\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb C^d}\|_{1\to1},$$
and the latter induced norm is attained on some rank-one operator $R_{x,y}:z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{\rm root}x$ with unit vectors $x,y\in H\otimes\mathbb C^d$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

items.title: Helstrom Binary Discrimination
items.statement:
Let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. If they are presented with equal prior probability, the greatest success probability of any binary measurement for identifying the state is
$$\frac12(1+D(\rho,\sigma)).$$
The binary projective measurement whose first effect is the spectral projection of $\Delta=\rho-\sigma$ onto its strictly positive eigenspaces attains this value.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.2, PDF pp.39–41; raw trace norm and optimal-measurement discussion

items.title: Trace Distance Range And Equality
items.statement:
For finite-dimensional density operators $\rho,\sigma$,
$$0\le D(\rho,\sigma)\le1.$$
Moreover, $D(\rho,\sigma)=0$ iff $\rho=\sigma$, and $D(\rho,\sigma)=1$ iff their supports are orthogonal.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.2, PDF pp.39–41; raw trace norm and optimal-measurement discussion

items.title: Symmetric Power Irreducible
items.statement: For every positive integer $d$ and integer $k\ge0$, the natural unitary action of $U(d)$ on $\operatorname{Sym}^k(\mathbb C^d)$ is irreducible.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §7.2 proof of Theorem 7.28, PDF pp.423–434; local weight-space proof supplied here.

items.title: Measurement Variation At Most Trace Distance
items.statement:
Let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $\{E_a\}_{a\in\mathcal A}$ be any finite POVM. If $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a)$ and $q_a=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma E_a)$, then
$$\frac12\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}|p_a-q_a|\le D(\rho,\sigma).$$
The two-effect projective measurement from the Holevo–Helstrom theorem attains equality.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.2, PDF pp.39–41; raw trace norm and optimal-measurement discussion

items.title: Broadcasting Family
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $\mathcal D(H)$ be its density operators (nonnegative operators of trace one; [[def-qc-density-operator]]), and let $S\subseteq\mathcal D(H)$ be any set, finite or infinite. A **broadcaster** for $S$ is one quantum channel $B:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(H\otimes H)$ (completely positive and trace-preserving; [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]) such that for every $\rho\in S$,
$$\operatorname{Tr}_1(B(\rho))=\rho\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{Tr}_2(B(\rho))=\rho.$$
Here $\operatorname{Tr}_1$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_2$ are the partial traces over the indicated output factors ([[def-qc-partial-trace]]). The joint output may be correlated; this definition does not require $B(\rho)=\rho\otimes\rho$.

references.title: Howard Barnum, Carlton M. Caves, Christopher A. Fuchs, Richard Jozsa, and Benjamin Schumacher, Noncommuting Mixed States Cannot Be Broadcast
references.locator: Complete paper, PDF pp.2–10; pair statement/construction p.3, fidelity and invertible-state proof Eqs.(4)–(31), pp.4–10

items.title: Fidelity Purification Characterization
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\rho,\sigma\in\mathcal D(H)$. For every auxiliary space $R$ with $\dim R\ge\dim H$, a **purification** of $\rho$ on $H\otimes R$ means a unit vector $x$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R(|x\rangle\langle x|)=\rho$. Then
$$F(\rho,\sigma)=\max\{|\langle x,y\rangle|:x,y\in H\otimes R,\ \|x\|=\|y\|=1,\ \operatorname{Tr}_R|x\rangle\langle x|=\rho,\ \operatorname{Tr}_R|y\rangle\langle y|=\sigma\}.$$
In particular, the maximum is attained with $R\cong H$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.1–2, PDF pp.36–40; complete cross-read qc_r2 ledger, summary/corroboration only

items.title: Symmetric Subspace Dimension And Haar Moment
items.statement:
Assume the axiom-of-choice branch used by [[cor-normalized-haar-probability-on-a-compact-group]]. For integers $d\ge1$ and $k\ge0$, put $N_k=\binom{k+d-1}{d-1}$. Then $\dim\operatorname{Sym}^k(\mathbb C^d)=N_k$, and if $\mu$ is the probability measure on the unit sphere obtained by pushing normalized Haar probability on $U(d)$ through $U\mapsto Ue_1$, then
$$\int |u\rangle\langle u|^{\otimes k}\,d\mu(u)=\frac{1}{N_k}\Pi_{\mathrm{sym},k}.$$
For $k=0$, the tensor power and projector are the identity on the one-dimensional tensor unit.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §§7.1.1–7.2, PDF pp.392–434; symmetric-subspace dimension and Haar/spherical-moment route.

items.title: Trace Distance Channel Contractivity
items.statement:
For every finite-dimensional quantum channel $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ and every pair of density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on $H$,
$$D(\Phi(\rho),\Phi(\sigma))\le D(\rho,\sigma).$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

items.title: Fidelity classical measurement minimum
items.statement:
For states $\rho,\sigma$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $H$, let a finite POVM be a finite family $(E_a)_{a=1}^n$ of nonnegative operators summing to $I_H$. Then
$$F(\rho,\sigma)=\min_{(E_a)}\sum_{a=1}^n\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a)\operatorname{tr}(\sigma E_a)}.$$
The minimum is attained by a projective measurement with $d=\dim H$ rank-one outcomes.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: Chapter 3 fidelity: measurement characterization and Fuchs–van de Graaf inequalities

items.title: Optimal Cloner Attains Bound
items.statement:
Assume the choice branch in [[thm-qc-symmetric-subspace-dimension-and-haar-moment]]. Let $d\ge1$ and $1\le n\le m$. Write $N_r=\binom{r+d-1}{d-1}$ and let $\Pi_{\rm sym,r}$ project onto $\operatorname{Sym}^r(\mathbb C^d)$. For any fixed output density operator $\omega$ on $(\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes m}$, the map
$$\Phi(X)=\frac{N_n}{N_m}\Pi_{\rm sym,m}(X\otimes I^{\otimes(m-n)})\Pi_{\rm sym,m}+\operatorname{tr}((I-\Pi_{\rm sym,n})X)\,\omega$$
is a channel and satisfies $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(|u\rangle\langle u|^{\otimes n})|u\rangle\langle u|^{\otimes m})=N_n/N_m$ for every unit $u\in\mathbb C^d$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

items.title: Optimal Cloning Worst Case Upper Bound
items.statement:
Assume the choice branch in [[thm-qc-symmetric-subspace-dimension-and-haar-moment]]. Let $d\ge1$ and $1\le n\le m$. Every channel $\Phi:\mathcal L((\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes n})\to\mathcal L((\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes m})$ has
$$\inf_{\|u\|=1}F\!\left(\Phi(|u\rangle\langle u|^{\otimes n}),|u\rangle\langle u|^{\otimes m}\right)^2\le\frac{N_n}{N_m},\qquad N_r=\binom{r+d-1}{d-1}.$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: Thm.7.28 proof, PDF pp.433–434

items.title: Channel Diamond Norm One
items.statement: Every quantum channel $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ between nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces has $\|\Phi\|_\diamond=1$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

items.title: Fidelity range equality and products
items.statement:
For finite-dimensional density operators $\rho,\sigma$,
$$0\le F(\rho,\sigma)\le1,\qquad F(\rho,\sigma)=1\iff\rho=\sigma,\qquad F(\rho,\sigma)=0\iff\operatorname{supp}\rho\perp\operatorname{supp}\sigma.$$
For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on $H$ and $\tau,\omega$ on $K$,
$$F(\rho\otimes\tau,\sigma\otimes\omega)=F(\rho,\sigma)F(\tau,\omega).$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: Chapters 1–3; finite-dimensional adaptation specified in this contract

items.title: Channel Composition Hybrid Bound
items.statement:
Let $\Phi_0,\Psi_0:\mathcal L(H_0)\to\mathcal L(H_1)$ and $\Phi_1,\Psi_1:\mathcal L(H_1)\to\mathcal L(H_2)$ be finite-dimensional channels. Then
$$\|\Psi_1\circ\Psi_0-\Phi_1\circ\Phi_0\|_\diamond\le\|\Psi_0-\Phi_0\|_\diamond+\|\Psi_1-\Phi_1\|_\diamond.$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

items.title: Fidelity Data Processing
items.statement:
For every finite-dimensional channel $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ and states $\rho,\sigma\in\mathcal D(H)$,
$$F(\rho,\sigma)\le F(\Phi(\rho),\Phi(\sigma)).$$
No general equality characterization is asserted.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

items.title: Fuchs Van De Graaf
items.statement:
For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space,
$$1-F(\rho,\sigma)\le D(\rho,\sigma)\le\sqrt{1-F(\rho,\sigma)^2},$$
where $F$ is root fidelity and $D(\rho,\sigma)=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.1–2, PDF pp.36–40; complete cross-read qc_r2 ledger, summary/corroboration only

items.title: Optimal Universal Pure State Cloning Bound
items.statement:
Assume the choice branch used by the normalized Haar moment theorem. For $d\ge1$ and $1\le n\le m$, the largest possible worst-case squared root fidelity of a channel from $n$ identical $d$-dimensional input registers to $m$ output registers is
$$\frac{N_n}{N_m},\qquad N_r=\binom{r+d-1}{d-1}.$$
For $n=1,m=2$ this value is $2/(d+1)$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: Thm.7.28 and proof, PDF pp.432–434

items.title: Pure State No Cloning
items.statement: Let $S$ be a set of pure-state rays in a nonzero finite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$. If one channel maps every pure-state projector $P_\psi$ with ray $\psi\in S$ to $P_\psi\otimes P_\psi$, then every pair of rays in $S$ is identical or orthogonal. Consequently no channel exactly clones all pure states when $\dim H\ge2$; when $\dim H=1$, the unique ray is cloned by the one-dimensional isometry.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: Thm.7.28 and proof, §7.2, PDF pp.432–434

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415v6
references.locator: Ch.1 Exercise 12, PDF pp.23–24; Appendix C hint 12, PDF p.203, pure-state no-cloning context only

items.title: Channel Tensor Error Bound
items.statement:
For nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces $H_i,K_i$ and linear maps $\Phi_i:\mathcal L(H_i)\to\mathcal L(K_i)$, $i=1,2$,
$$\|\Phi_1\otimes\Phi_2\|_\diamond=\|\Phi_1\|_\diamond\|\Phi_2\|_\diamond.$$
Consequently, if $\Phi_i,\Psi_i:\mathcal L(H_i)\to\mathcal L(K_i)$ are channels, then
$$\|\Phi_1\otimes\Phi_2-\Psi_1\otimes\Psi_2\|_\diamond\le\|\Phi_1-\Psi_1\|_\diamond+\|\Phi_2-\Psi_2\|_\diamond.$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

items.title: Exact Mixed State Cloning Fidelity Criterion
items.statement: Let $\rho_0,\rho_1$ be finite-dimensional density operators. If one channel $\Phi$ satisfies $\Phi(\rho_i)=\rho_i\otimes\rho_i$ for $i=0,1$, then $F(\rho_0,\rho_1)\in\{0,1\}$. Therefore the inputs are identical or have orthogonal supports.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
Howard Barnum, Carlton M. Caves, Christopher A. Fuchs, Richard Jozsa, and Benjamin Schumacher, Noncommuting Mixed States Cannot Be Broadcast
references.locator: Complete paper, PDF pp.2–10; pair statement/construction p.3, fidelity and invertible-state proof Eqs.(4)–(31), pp.4–10

items.title: Full Rank Pair No Broadcasting
items.statement: Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $\rho_0,\rho_1$ be positive-definite density operators on $H$. One channel $B:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(H\otimes H)$ broadcasts both states if and only if $\rho_0\rho_1=\rho_1\rho_0$.

references.title: Howard Barnum, Carlton M. Caves, Christopher A. Fuchs, Richard Jozsa, and Benjamin Schumacher, Noncommuting Mixed States Cannot Be Broadcast
references.locator: Complete paper, PDF pp.2–10; pair statement/construction p.3, fidelity and invertible-state proof Eqs.(4)–(31), pp.4–10

items.title: Singular Pair No Broadcasting
items.statement: For any two density operators $\rho_0,\rho_1$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional $H$, one channel broadcasts both if and only if $[\rho_0,\rho_1]=0$.

references.title: Howard Barnum, Carlton M. Caves, Christopher A. Fuchs, Richard Jozsa, and Benjamin Schumacher, Noncommuting Mixed States Cannot Be Broadcast
references.locator: Complete paper, PDF pp.2–10; pair statement/construction p.3, fidelity and invertible-state proof Eqs.(4)–(31), pp.4–10

items.title: State Family No Broadcasting Iff Commuting
items.statement: Let $S$ be any family, finite or infinite, of density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $H$. One common channel broadcasts every member of $S$ if and only if every pair of members commutes.

references.title: Howard Barnum, Carlton M. Caves, Christopher A. Fuchs, Richard Jozsa, and Benjamin Schumacher, Noncommuting Mixed States Cannot Be Broadcast
references.locator: Complete paper, PDF pp.2–10; pair statement/construction p.3, fidelity and invertible-state proof Eqs.(4)–(31), pp.4–10

proposed_after_items.title: Unitary Group Compact
proposed_after_items.statement:
For every positive integer $d$, the unitary group
$$U(d):=\{U\in M_d(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_d\}$$
is a compact Hausdorff topological group in the Euclidean topology inherited from the real and imaginary parts of its matrix entries.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §7.2, PDF pp.408–434; finite-dimensional unitary-group context; compactness is proved locally.

proposed_after_items.title: Diamond Norm
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces and let $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be complex-linear. For each finite $r\ge1$, the induced trace norm of the amplification is
$$\|\Phi\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb C^r}\|_{1\to1}:=\sup_{X\ne0}\frac{\| (\Phi\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb C^r})(X)\|_1}{\|X\|_1},$$
where $X\in\mathcal L(H\otimes\mathbb C^r)$ and $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the finite-dimensional trace norm ([[def-qc-trace-norm]]). The **diamond norm** (the completely bounded trace norm) is
$$\|\Phi\|_\diamond:=\sup_{r\ge1}\|\Phi\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb C^r}\|_{1\to1}.$$
There is no factor $1/2$ in this map norm. The finite-dimensional ancilla theorem [[thm-qc-diamond-norm-ancilla-dimension-bound]] proves the supremum is finite, is attained, and can be capped at $r=\dim H$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

proposed_after_items.title: Fidelity
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on $H$ (nonnegative operators of trace one; [[def-qc-density-operator]]). Their **root fidelity** is
$$F(\rho,\sigma):=\|\sqrt\rho\,\sqrt\sigma\|_1,$$
where $\sqrt\rho$ and $\sqrt\sigma$ are the unique non-negative square roots and $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the finite-dimensional trace norm ([[def-qc-trace-norm]]). This library uses root fidelity; the squared quantity $F(\rho,\sigma)^2$ is called squared fidelity.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.1–2, PDF pp.36–40; complete cross-read qc_r2 ledger, summary/corroboration only

proposed_after_items.title: Trace Distance
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on $H$ (nonnegative operators of trace one; [[def-qc-density-operator]]). Their **trace distance** is
$$D(\rho,\sigma):=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1,$$
where $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the trace norm ([[def-qc-trace-norm]]). The factor $1/2$ is part of this state-distance convention. The diamond norm below is an unhalved norm on maps.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.2, PDF pp.39–41; raw trace norm and optimal-measurement discussion

proposed_after_items.title: Faithful State Dominates Positive Operator
proposed_after_items.statement: Let $H$ be finite-dimensional, let $\sigma$ be a density operator that is positive definite on $H$, and let $X$ be a non-negative endomorphism of $H$. Then there is a finite real $c\ge0$ such that $X\le c\sigma$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §2.1.2–2.1.3, PDF pp.69–83; positive-operator and support conventions. The finite domination/support arguments are proved locally.

proposed_after_items.title: Symmetric Subspace Projector
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let $k\ge1$, and let $H^{\otimes k}$ use the ordered tensor product register and factor permutation convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For $\pi\in S_k$, let $U_\pi$ be the resulting unitary that permutes the $k$ tensor factors according to $\pi$. Define
$$\Pi_{\mathrm{sym},k}:=\frac1{k!}\sum_{\pi\in S_k}U_\pi.$$
The **symmetric subspace** is $\operatorname{Sym}^k(H):=\{v\in H^{\otimes k}:U_\tau v=v\text{ for every }\tau\in S_k\}$. For $k=0$, the tensor unit is one-dimensional and $\Pi_{\mathrm{sym},0}:=I$.

The permutation average is the orthogonal projector onto $\operatorname{Sym}^k(H)$ by [[lem-qc-symmetric-subspace-average-is-projector]].

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §7.1.1 Proposition 7.1, PDF pp.392–393

proposed_after_items.title: The two root-fidelity trace expressions agree
proposed_after_items.statement:
For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space,
$$\|\sqrt\rho\,\sqrt\sigma\|_1=\operatorname{tr}\sqrt{\sqrt\rho\,\sigma\,\sqrt\rho}.$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

proposed_after_items.title: Trace norm of a tensor product
proposed_after_items.statement:
For finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces $H_1,K_1,H_2,K_2$ and linear maps $A:H_1\to K_1$, $B:H_2\to K_2$,
$$\|A\otimes B\|_1=\|A\|_1\,\|B\|_1.$$
The equality includes zero maps and zero-dimensional factors.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §1.1.3, trace norm and singular-value decomposition; the tensor-product formula is proved locally.

proposed_after_items.title: Positive Marginals Imply Joint Support
proposed_after_items.statement: Let $H$ be finite-dimensional, let $Y\ge0$ act on $H\otimes H$, and let $S\subseteq H$ be a subspace. If both partial-trace marginals of $Y$ are supported on $S$, then $\operatorname{supp}Y\subseteq S\otimes S$; equivalently, $Y=(P_S\otimes P_S)Y(P_S\otimes P_S)$, where $P_S$ is the orthogonal projection onto $S$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §2.1.2–2.1.3, PDF pp.69–83; positive-operator and support conventions. The finite domination/support arguments are proved locally.

proposed_after_items.title: Pure state trace distance
proposed_after_items.statement:
For unit vectors $u,v$ in a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let $P_u=|u\rangle\langle u|$ and $P_v=|v\rangle\langle v|$. Then
$$D(P_u,P_v)=\sqrt{1-|\langle u|v\rangle_D|^2},$$
where $\langle\cdot|\cdot\rangle_D$ is the Dirac pairing converted from the root library's first-argument-linear inner product.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: Chapters 1–3; finite-dimensional adaptation specified in this contract

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.2, PDF pp.39–41; pure-state trace-norm calculation (2.155)–(2.158)

proposed_after_items.title: The permutation average is the symmetric-subspace projector
proposed_after_items.statement: Let $H$ be finite-dimensional and let $k\ge1$. The average $\Pi_{\mathrm{sym},k}=\frac1{k!}\sum_{\pi\in S_k}U_\pi$ is self-adjoint and idempotent, with range exactly $\operatorname{Sym}^k(H)=\{v:U_\tau v=v\ \forall\tau\in S_k\}$. For $k=0$ on the tensor unit, $\Pi_{\mathrm{sym},0}=I$ and its range is the full tensor unit.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

proposed_after_items.title: Diamond Norm Ancilla Dimension Bound
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, $d=\dim H$, and let $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be linear. Then
$$\|\Phi\|_\diamond=\|\Phi\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb C^d}\|_{1\to1},$$
and the latter induced norm is attained on some rank-one operator $R_{x,y}:z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{\rm root}x$ with unit vectors $x,y\in H\otimes\mathbb C^d$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

proposed_after_items.title: Helstrom Binary Discrimination
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. If they are presented with equal prior probability, the greatest success probability of any binary measurement for identifying the state is
$$\frac12(1+D(\rho,\sigma)).$$
The binary projective measurement whose first effect is the spectral projection of $\Delta=\rho-\sigma$ onto its strictly positive eigenspaces attains this value.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.2, PDF pp.39–41; raw trace norm and optimal-measurement discussion

proposed_after_items.title: Trace Distance Range And Equality
proposed_after_items.statement:
For finite-dimensional density operators $\rho,\sigma$,
$$0\le D(\rho,\sigma)\le1.$$
Moreover, $D(\rho,\sigma)=0$ iff $\rho=\sigma$, and $D(\rho,\sigma)=1$ iff their supports are orthogonal.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.2, PDF pp.39–41; raw trace norm and optimal-measurement discussion

proposed_after_items.title: Symmetric Power Irreducible
proposed_after_items.statement: For every positive integer $d$ and integer $k\ge0$, the natural unitary action of $U(d)$ on $\operatorname{Sym}^k(\mathbb C^d)$ is irreducible.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §7.2 proof of Theorem 7.28, PDF pp.423–434; local weight-space proof supplied here.

proposed_after_items.title: Measurement Variation At Most Trace Distance
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $\{E_a\}_{a\in\mathcal A}$ be any finite POVM. If $p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a)$ and $q_a=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma E_a)$, then
$$\frac12\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}|p_a-q_a|\le D(\rho,\sigma).$$
The two-effect projective measurement from the Holevo–Helstrom theorem attains equality.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.2, PDF pp.39–41; raw trace norm and optimal-measurement discussion

proposed_after_items.title: Broadcasting Family
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $\mathcal D(H)$ be its density operators (nonnegative operators of trace one; [[def-qc-density-operator]]), and let $S\subseteq\mathcal D(H)$ be any set, finite or infinite. A **broadcaster** for $S$ is one quantum channel $B:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(H\otimes H)$ (completely positive and trace-preserving; [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]) such that for every $\rho\in S$,
$$\operatorname{Tr}_1(B(\rho))=\rho\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{Tr}_2(B(\rho))=\rho.$$
Here $\operatorname{Tr}_1$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_2$ are the partial traces over the indicated output factors ([[def-qc-partial-trace]]). The joint output may be correlated; this definition does not require $B(\rho)=\rho\otimes\rho$.

references.title: Howard Barnum, Carlton M. Caves, Christopher A. Fuchs, Richard Jozsa, and Benjamin Schumacher, Noncommuting Mixed States Cannot Be Broadcast
references.locator: Complete paper, PDF pp.2–10; pair statement/construction p.3, fidelity and invertible-state proof Eqs.(4)–(31), pp.4–10

proposed_after_items.title: Fidelity Purification Characterization
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\rho,\sigma\in\mathcal D(H)$. For every auxiliary space $R$ with $\dim R\ge\dim H$, a **purification** of $\rho$ on $H\otimes R$ means a unit vector $x$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R(|x\rangle\langle x|)=\rho$. Then
$$F(\rho,\sigma)=\max\{|\langle x,y\rangle|:x,y\in H\otimes R,\ \|x\|=\|y\|=1,\ \operatorname{Tr}_R|x\rangle\langle x|=\rho,\ \operatorname{Tr}_R|y\rangle\langle y|=\sigma\}.$$
In particular, the maximum is attained with $R\cong H$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)
references.locator: §2.6.1–2, PDF pp.36–40; complete cross-read qc_r2 ledger, summary/corroboration only

proposed_after_items.title: Symmetric Subspace Dimension And Haar Moment
proposed_after_items.statement:
Assume the axiom-of-choice branch used by [[cor-normalized-haar-probability-on-a-compact-group]]. For integers $d\ge1$ and $k\ge0$, put $N_k=\binom{k+d-1}{d-1}$. Then $\dim\operatorname{Sym}^k(\mathbb C^d)=N_k$, and if $\mu$ is the probability measure on the unit sphere obtained by pushing normalized Haar probability on $U(d)$ through $U\mapsto Ue_1$, then
$$\int |u\rangle\langle u|^{\otimes k}\,d\mu(u)=\frac{1}{N_k}\Pi_{\mathrm{sym},k}.$$
For $k=0$, the tensor power and projector are the identity on the one-dimensional tensor unit.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §§7.1.1–7.2, PDF pp.392–434; symmetric-subspace dimension and Haar/spherical-moment route.

proposed_after_items.title: Trace Distance Channel Contractivity
proposed_after_items.statement:
For every finite-dimensional quantum channel $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ and every pair of density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on $H$,
$$D(\Phi(\rho),\Phi(\sigma))\le D(\rho,\sigma).$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

proposed_after_items.title: Fidelity classical measurement minimum
proposed_after_items.statement:
For states $\rho,\sigma$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $H$, let a finite POVM be a finite family $(E_a)_{a=1}^n$ of nonnegative operators summing to $I_H$. Then
$$F(\rho,\sigma)=\min_{(E_a)}\sum_{a=1}^n\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a)\operatorname{tr}(\sigma E_a)}.$$
The minimum is attained by a projective measurement with $d=\dim H$ rank-one outcomes.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: Chapter 3 fidelity: measurement characterization and Fuchs–van de Graaf inequalities

proposed_after_items.title: Optimal Cloner Attains Bound
proposed_after_items.statement:
Assume the choice branch in [[thm-qc-symmetric-subspace-dimension-and-haar-moment]]. Let $d\ge1$ and $1\le n\le m$. Write $N_r=\binom{r+d-1}{d-1}$ and let $\Pi_{\rm sym,r}$ project onto $\operatorname{Sym}^r(\mathbb C^d)$. For any fixed output density operator $\omega$ on $(\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes m}$, the map
$$\Phi(X)=\frac{N_n}{N_m}\Pi_{\rm sym,m}(X\otimes I^{\otimes(m-n)})\Pi_{\rm sym,m}+\operatorname{tr}((I-\Pi_{\rm sym,n})X)\,\omega$$
is a channel and satisfies $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(|u\rangle\langle u|^{\otimes n})|u\rangle\langle u|^{\otimes m})=N_n/N_m$ for every unit $u\in\mathbb C^d$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

proposed_after_items.title: Optimal Cloning Worst Case Upper Bound
proposed_after_items.statement:
Assume the choice branch in [[thm-qc-symmetric-subspace-dimension-and-haar-moment]]. Let $d\ge1$ and $1\le n\le m$. Every channel $\Phi:\mathcal L((\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes n})\to\mathcal L((\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes m})$ has
$$\inf_{\|u\|=1}F\!\left(\Phi(|u\rangle\langle u|^{\otimes n}),|u\rangle\langle u|^{\otimes m}\right)^2\le\frac{N_n}{N_m},\qquad N_r=\binom{r+d-1}{d-1}.$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: Thm.7.28 proof, PDF pp.433–434

proposed_after_items.title: Channel Diamond Norm One
proposed_after_items.statement: Every quantum channel $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ between nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces has $\|\Phi\|_\diamond=1$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

proposed_after_items.title: Fidelity range equality and products
proposed_after_items.statement:
For finite-dimensional density operators $\rho,\sigma$,
$$0\le F(\rho,\sigma)\le1,\qquad F(\rho,\sigma)=1\iff\rho=\sigma,\qquad F(\rho,\sigma)=0\iff\operatorname{supp}\rho\perp\operatorname{supp}\sigma.$$
For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on $H$ and $\tau,\omega$ on $K$,
$$F(\rho\otimes\tau,\sigma\otimes\omega)=F(\rho,\sigma)F(\tau,\omega).$$

references.locator: Chapters 1–3; finite-dimensional adaptation specified in this contract

proposed_after_items.title: Channel Composition Hybrid Bound
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H_0,H_1,H_2$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, and let $\Phi_0,\Psi_0:\mathcal L(H_0)\to\mathcal L(H_1)$ and $\Phi_1,\Psi_1:\mathcal L(H_1)\to\mathcal L(H_2)$ be finite-dimensional channels. Then
$$\|\Psi_1\circ\Psi_0-\Phi_1\circ\Phi_0\|_\diamond\le\|\Psi_0-\Phi_0\|_\diamond+\|\Psi_1-\Phi_1\|_\diamond.$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

proposed_after_items.title: Fidelity Data Processing
proposed_after_items.statement:
For every finite-dimensional channel $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ and states $\rho,\sigma\in\mathcal D(H)$,
$$F(\rho,\sigma)\le F(\Phi(\rho),\Phi(\sigma)).$$
No general equality characterization is asserted.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information

proposed_after_items.statement:
For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space,
$$1-F(\rho,\sigma)\le D(\rho,\sigma)\le\sqrt{1-F(\rho,\sigma)^2},$$
where $F$ is root fidelity and $D(\rho,\sigma)=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$.

proposed_after_items.title: Channel Tensor Error Bound
proposed_after_items.statement:
For nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces $H_i,K_i$ and linear maps $\Phi_i:\mathcal L(H_i)\to\mathcal L(K_i)$, $i=1,2$,
$$\|\Phi_1\otimes\Phi_2\|_\diamond=\|\Phi_1\|_\diamond\|\Phi_2\|_\diamond.$$
Consequently, if $\Phi_i,\Psi_i:\mathcal L(H_i)\to\mathcal L(K_i)$ are channels, then
$$\|\Phi_1\otimes\Phi_2-\Psi_1\otimes\Psi_2\|_\diamond\le\|\Phi_1-\Psi_1\|_\diamond+\|\Phi_2-\Psi_2\|_\diamond.$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information
references.locator: §3.3.2–3.3.4, tensor-product and composition properties.

proposed_after_items.title: Exact Mixed State Cloning Fidelity Criterion
proposed_after_items.statement: Let $\rho_0,\rho_1$ be finite-dimensional density operators. If one channel $\Phi$ satisfies $\Phi(\rho_i)=\rho_i\otimes\rho_i$ for $i=0,1$, then $F(\rho_0,\rho_1)\in\{0,1\}$. Therefore the inputs are identical or have orthogonal supports.

proposed_after_items.title: Full Rank Pair No Broadcasting
proposed_after_items.statement: Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let $\rho_0,\rho_1$ be positive-definite density operators on $H$. One channel $B:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(H\otimes H)$ broadcasts both states if and only if $\rho_0\rho_1=\rho_1\rho_0$.

proposed_after_items.title: Singular Pair No Broadcasting
proposed_after_items.statement: For any two density operators $\rho_0,\rho_1$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional $H$, one channel broadcasts both if and only if $[\rho_0,\rho_1]=0$.

proposed_after_items.title: State Family No Broadcasting Iff Commuting
proposed_after_items.statement: Let $S$ be any family, finite or infinite, of density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $H$. One common channel broadcasts every member of $S$ if and only if every pair of members commutes.

Input distinct $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$, $n\ge1$, exact $V\in U(2)$, and for each controlled call a choice between the no-workspace and clean-bit constructions of [[thm-qc-multicontrolled-ancilla-resource-tradeoff]]. If any call selects the clean-bit construction, supply one clean bit initialized to $0$. Output: the chronological elementary-gate list on the $n$ data wires and, if selected, that one clean work wire.

Let $g_0=x,\ldots,g_d=y$ be the path that flips the differing bit positions once in increasing order, where $d$ is the Hamming distance. For $j=0,\ldots,d-2$, swap $g_j$ and $g_{j+1}$ by an $X$ on their differing bit controlled on the other $n-1$ bits matching their common pattern. Apply $V$ to the final pair $g_{d-1},y$ by a one-qubit target gate controlled on their common other bits, reversing the ordered $2\times2$ block if $g_{d-1}$ has target bit $1$. Undo the swaps in reverse order. Expand every multi-control using its selected construction; implement negative controls by conjugating that control wire with $X$.

Use the selected literal elementary gate list for each call without deleting identity gates or cancelling neighboring gates. In the one-control base use the three target matrices and one control phase as four arbitrary one-qubit gates. Use the same choices and reversed adjoint gate lists for the return swaps. Reuse the supplied clean bit sequentially; each selected clean-bit construction returns it to $0$.
statement.after:
Input distinct $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$, $n\ge1$, exact $V\in U(2)$, and for each controlled call a choice between the no-workspace and clean-bit constructions of [[thm-qc-multicontrolled-ancilla-resource-tradeoff]]. If any call selects the clean-bit construction, supply one clean bit initialized to $0$. Output: the chronological elementary-gate list on the $n$ data wires and, if selected, that one clean work wire.

Let $g_0=x,\ldots,g_d=y$ be the path that flips the differing bit positions once in increasing order, where $d$ is the Hamming distance. For $j=0,\ldots,d-2$, swap $g_j$ and $g_{j+1}$ by an $X$ on their differing bit controlled on the other $n-1$ bits matching their common pattern. Apply $V$ to the final pair $g_{d-1},y$ by a one-qubit target gate controlled on their common other bits, reversing the ordered $2\times2$ block if $g_{d-1}$ has target bit $1$. Undo the swaps in reverse order. Expand every multi-control using its selected construction; implement negative controls by conjugating that control wire with $X$.

Expand the calls by the following procedures. Every list below is chronological; concatenation means execute the left list first. Order control wires and available spare wires by their register positions. All parameter selections are exact mathematical operations: use exact matrix arithmetic, a finite-dimensional unitary eigendecomposition, polar arguments and the Euler parameter selection of [[thm-qc-one-qubit-euler-decomposition]]. The input representation must support these selections and exact zero tests; no finite-precision bit-time claim is made. Fix each selection when its call is first expanded and retain the resulting list for an inverse call.

For one control $c$, target $t$ and matrix $W$, choose $W=e^{i\delta}R_z(\alpha)R_y(\theta)R_z(\beta)$ as in [[thm-qc-one-qubit-euler-decomposition]]. Form the three matrices $A=R_z(\alpha)R_y(\theta/2)$, $B=R_y(-\theta/2)R_z(- (\alpha+\beta)/2)$ and $C=R_z((\beta-\alpha)/2)$. Define $S(c,t;W)$ to be the list $C_t$, $\mathrm{CNOT}_{c\to t}$, $B_t$, $\mathrm{CNOT}_{c\to t}$, $A_t$, $\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\delta})_c$. Each of $A,B,C$ is one arbitrary one-qubit gate, as in [[thm-qc-one-control-unitary-two-cnot]]. Define $T(a,b;t)$ by setting $J=((1+i)I+(1-i)X)/2$ and concatenating $S(b,t;J)$, $\mathrm{CNOT}_{a\to b}$, $S(b,t;J^*)$, $\mathrm{CNOT}_{a\to b}$, $S(a,t;J)$.

Define the ladder list $L(c_1,\ldots,c_s;t)$ with an ordered supply of at least $\max\{s-2,0\}$ distinct spare wires. For $s=1$ emit one CNOT; for $s=2$ emit $T(c_1,c_2;t)$. For $s\ge3$, use the first $s-2$ spares $a_1,\ldots,a_{s-2}$. Set $T_1=T(c_1,c_2;a_1)$, $T_j=T(c_{j+1},a_{j-1};a_j)$ for $2\le j\le s-2$, and $H=T(c_s,a_{s-2};t)$. Concatenate $T_1,\ldots,T_{s-2},H,T_{s-2},\ldots,T_1$ and then $T_2,\ldots,T_{s-2},H,T_{s-2},\ldots,T_2$; the latter list is just $H$ when $s=3$. This is the borrowed ladder used in [[lem-qc-borrowed-bit-multicontrolled-x-linear]].

Define $D(C;t;z)$ for an ordered nonempty control set $C$ and a distinct borrowed wire $z$. With one or two controls use the corresponding ladder base case and leave $z$ unused. With $r\ge3$ controls split $C$ into its first $p=\lceil r/2\rceil$ controls $A$ and the remaining $q=\lfloor r/2\rfloor$ controls $B$. Let $F=L(A;z)$ use spares from $B\cup\{t\}$, and let $G=L(B\cup\{z\};t)$ use spares from $A$. Emit $F,G,F,G$, using the same parameter choices for repeated lists. The stated spare supplies have at least $p-2$ and $q-1$ wires, respectively.

Define the positive-control no-workspace expansion $N(C;t;W)$ recursively. If $C$ is empty, emit $W_t$. If it has one wire $c$, emit $S(c,t;W)$. Otherwise write $C=A\cup\{b\}$, with $b$ its last control. Choose an orthonormal eigendecomposition $W=R\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)R^*$ by [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]], choose polar angles $\lambda_j=\cos u_j+i\sin u_j$ by [[thm-polar-form-with-unique-principal-argument]], and set $Z=R\operatorname{diag}(\cos(u_1/2)+i\sin(u_1/2),\cos(u_2/2)+i\sin(u_2/2))R^*$. The addition formulas of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]] specify these half-angle roots. Emit $S(b,t;Z)$, $D(A;b;t)$, $S(b,t;Z^*)$, $D(A;b;t)$, $N(A;t;Z)$. The last call has one fewer control and uses only its indicated wires.

For the positive-control clean-bit expansion with nonempty $C$ and clean wire $w$, emit $D(C;w;t)$, $S(w,t;W)$, and the reversed adjoint of that same $D$ list. With no controls emit $W_t$ and leave $w$ unused. These are the two constructions analyzed in [[thm-qc-multicontrolled-ancilla-resource-tradeoff]]. For a pattern control, conjugate the selected whole positive-control list by one $X$ on each zero-valued control, ordering each set of these $X$ gates by wire position. Reverse the ordered middle block by using $XVX$ as its single matrix parameter, not by adding target $X$ occurrences.

Use the selected literal elementary gate list for each call without deleting identity gates or cancelling neighboring gates. In the one-control base use the three target matrices and one control phase as four arbitrary one-qubit gates. Use the same choices and reversed adjoint gate lists for the return swaps. Reuse the supplied clean bit sequentially; each selected clean-bit construction returns it to $0$.
