For $N\ge1$, define $U(N)=\{Q\in M_N(\mathbb C):Q^*Q=QQ^*=I\}$ and $\mathfrak u(N)=\{X\in M_N(\mathbb C):X^*=-X\}$, both regarded as real spaces where appropriate. Then $U(N)$ is a compact smooth real manifold of dimension $N^2$. Near $I$, the Cayley map
$$X\longmapsto (I+X)(I-X)^{-1}$$
is a smooth chart from $\mathfrak u(N)$; left translates give a finite atlas. The Frobenius inner product induces a smooth Riemannian metric and a normalized volume probability $\mu_F$. Its null sets are exactly the sets that are Lebesgue-null in these charts. Under AC, $\mu_F$ is the normalized Haar probability, so this also gives the Haar-null criterion in that branch.
statement.after:
For $N\ge1$, define $U(N)=\{Q\in M_N(\mathbb C):Q^*Q=QQ^*=I\}$ and $\mathfrak u(N)=\{X\in M_N(\mathbb C):X^*=-X\}$, both regarded as real spaces where appropriate. Then $U(N)$ is a compact smooth real manifold of dimension $N^2$. Near $I$, the Cayley map
$$X\longmapsto (I+X)(I-X)^{-1}$$
is a smooth chart from $\mathfrak u(N)$; left translates give a finite atlas. The Frobenius inner product induces a smooth Riemannian metric. Under AC$_\omega$, its volume density defines a normalized Borel volume probability $\mu_F$; a Borel subset is $\mu_F$-null exactly when its intersection with every chart has Lebesgue-null coordinate image. Under AC, $\mu_F$ is the normalized Haar probability, so this also gives the Haar-null criterion in that branch.

before_page.title: Continuous-Gate Universality and Exact Synthesis

items.title: Global Phase Equivalence
items.statement: For square matrices $U,V$ of the same size, write $U\sim_{\mathrm{phase}}V$ when $U=\lambda V$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ with $|\lambda|=1$. This relation is kept distinct from exact matrix equality.

items.title: Demultiplexing a Two-Block Unitary
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $U_0,U_1$ be unitary endomorphisms of $H$. On the control-first direct sum $H\oplus H$, the block unitary $\operatorname{diag}(U_0,U_1)$ factors as
$$\operatorname{diag}(U_0,U_1)=(I\otimes V)\operatorname{diag}(D,D^*)(I\otimes W)$$
for unitary $V,W$ on $H$ and a diagonal unitary $D$ in an orthonormal eigenbasis; $I\otimes V$ denotes $\operatorname{diag}(V,V)$ under $\mathbb C^2\otimes H\cong H\oplus H$.

items.title: Cayley Charts on the Unitary Matrix Group
items.statement:
For $N\ge1$, define $U(N)=\{Q\in M_N(\mathbb C):Q^*Q=QQ^*=I\}$ and $\mathfrak u(N)=\{X\in M_N(\mathbb C):X^*=-X\}$, both regarded as real spaces where appropriate. Then $U(N)$ is a compact smooth real manifold of dimension $N^2$. Near $I$, the Cayley map
$$X\longmapsto (I+X)(I-X)^{-1}$$
is a smooth chart from $\mathfrak u(N)$; left translates give a finite atlas. The Frobenius inner product induces a smooth Riemannian metric and a normalized volume probability $\mu_F$. Its null sets are exactly the sets that are Lebesgue-null in these charts. Under AC, $\mu_F$ is the normalized Haar probability, so this also gives the Haar-null criterion in that branch.
items.axiom_use: Assume AC_omega for the Radon volume measure; assume full AC only for the optional identification with normalized Haar probability.

items.title: Cosine-Sine Block Decomposition
items.statement:
Let $k\ge1$ and let $U\in U(2k)$ be partitioned into $k\times k$ blocks
$$U=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\ C&D\end{pmatrix}.$$
There are block-diagonal unitaries $L=\operatorname{diag}(L_0,L_1)$ and $R=\operatorname{diag}(R_0,R_1)$ and nonnegative real diagonal matrices $C_0,S_0$ such that
$$U=L\begin{pmatrix}C_0&-S_0\\S_0&C_0\end{pmatrix}R,\qquad C_0^2+S_0^2=I,\quad 0\le C_0,S_0\le I.$$
The singular values at $0$ and $1$ are allowed, with no nondegeneracy assumption.

items.title: Two-Level Unitary
items.statement: Let a finite ordered register have an orthonormal computational basis $(|z\rangle)_{z\in\mathcal X}$, using the root convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. For distinct labels $x,y\in\mathcal X$, choose $V\in U(2)$, where $U(2)=\{M\in M_2(\mathbb C):M^*M=MM^*=I_2\}$. The **two-level unitary** $T_{x,y}(V)$ acts by the matrix $V$ in the ordered basis $(|x\rangle,|y\rangle)$ and acts as the identity on $\operatorname{span}\{|x\rangle,|y\rangle\}^{\perp}$. Its action is exact matrix equality: any scalar phase contained in $V$ is retained.

items.title: Exact Two-Level Elimination of a Unitary
items.statement:
Input: an exact-arithmetic representation of $U\in U(N)$, $N\ge1$, supporting addition, multiplication, conjugation, nonnegative square roots, exact zero tests, and exact division by nonzero positive real scalars. Output: a finite ordered factorization into two-level unitaries and a diagonal unitary. This is an exact algebraic procedure; no claim of a bit-time algorithm for arbitrary real input is made.

Initialize $M:=U$ and an empty chronological list. For each column $j=0,\ldots,N-2$, and for $r=N-1,N-2,\ldots,j+1$, set $a=M_{r-1,j}$ and $b=M_{r,j}$. If $b=0$, do nothing. Otherwise set $h=\sqrt{|a|^2+|b|^2}>0$ and left-multiply rows $(r-1,r)$ by
$$G=\frac1h\begin{pmatrix}\overline a&\overline b\\-b&a\end{pmatrix},$$
recording this two-level unitary in the order applied. Let the resulting matrix be $D$. Return the factorization $U=G_1^*\cdots G_s^*D$. In chronological circuit order, apply $D$ first and then $G_s^*,\ldots,G_1^*$.

items.title: Correctness and Termination of Two-Level Elimination
items.statement: For $U\in U(N)$, the elimination procedure of [[alg-qc-two-level-unitary-elimination]] terminates after at most $N(N-1)/2$ Givens steps and returns an exact factorization of $U$ into the recorded two-level adjoints followed by a diagonal unitary. The number of diagonal entries is $N$; entries equal to $1$ need no phase gate.

items.title: One-Qubit Euler Decomposition
items.statement:
Use the rotation convention of [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]] and define $R_y(\theta):=R_{(0,1,0)}(\theta)$:
$$R_z(\alpha)=\begin{pmatrix}e^{-i\alpha/2}&0\\0&e^{i\alpha/2}\end{pmatrix},\qquad R_y(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta/2)&-\sin(\theta/2)\\\sin(\theta/2)&\cos(\theta/2)\end{pmatrix}.$$
For every $U\in U(2)$ there are real $\delta,\alpha,\theta,\beta$ with
$$U=e^{i\delta}R_z(\alpha)R_y(\theta)R_z(\beta).$$
If $\det U=1$, the scalar factor is unnecessary and $U=R_z(\alpha)R_y(\theta)R_z(\beta)$.

items.title: Exact Two-Qubit Cartan Decomposition
items.statement:
For every $U\in U(4)$ there are $A,B,C,D\in SU(2)$, real $a,b,c,\delta$, and the matrices
$$X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$
such that
$$U=e^{i\delta}(A\otimes B)\exp\!\bigl(i(aX\otimes X+bY\otimes Y+cZ\otimes Z)\bigr)(C\otimes D).$$
The equality is exact; the scalar $e^{i\delta}$ is displayed.

items.title: Global Phase Under Control
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional target space, let $U$ be unitary on $H$, and let $|\lambda|=1$. In control-first order put
$$C(U)=\begin{pmatrix}I_H&0\\0&U\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_\lambda=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\lambda\end{pmatrix}.$$
Then $C(\lambda U)=(P_\lambda\otimes I_H)C(U)$. A scalar multiplying an entire output leaves every defined finite-POVM outcome law unchanged, whereas a scalar attached to a target matrix inside a control gives a phase on only the active control block; applying $P_{\overline\lambda}$ on the control restores the exact controlled matrix.

items.title: Parameter Count for a Fixed CNOT Skeleton
items.statement: Assume AC$_\omega$ to form normalized Frobenius volume on $U(2^n)$. For fixed $n\ge1$ and a fixed ordered CNOT skeleton with $m$ CNOTs, arbitrary exact one-qubit gates, and no ancillas, the set of exact circuit matrices is contained in a finite union of smooth images of real parameter spaces of dimension at most $3n+4m+1$. If $3n+4m+1<4^n$, this fixed skeleton has measure zero. Under full AC, it is Haar-null.
items.axiom_use: AC_omega is assumed for the normalized smooth volume measure; full AC is needed only for the optional Haar identification.

items.title: Gray-Code Synthesis of a Multiplexed Axis Rotation
items.statement:
Let $k\ge0$ controls have computational labels $x\in\{0,1\}^k$, and let $\theta_x\in\mathbb R$. Fix $a\in\{x,y,z\}$. On one target qubit define
$$M=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^k}|x\rangle\langle x|\otimes R_a(\theta_x),\qquad R_a(t)=\exp(-it\sigma_a/2).$$
Then $M$ is exactly synthesized with $2^k$ CNOTs for $k>0$ (the final CNOT restores the parity network). For $a=y,z$ it uses $2^k$ target rotations $R_a(\beta_j)$; for $a=x$ it uses $2^k$ $R_y$ rotations in the fixed target basis described below; for $k=0$ it is one rotation and no CNOT. For $a=x$ and $k>0$ the implementation also uses two fixed target basis-change gates; the $y,z$ implementations need none. One may replace the cyclic Gray traversal by a traversal that omits the final restoration and absorb that final parity into the next block only when that block is explicitly specified.

items.title: Exact Controlled One-Qubit Unitary with Two CNOTs
items.statement: For every $U\in U(2)$, the exact controlled matrix $C(U)=\operatorname{diag}(I_2,U)$ is realized with two CNOTs and one-qubit gates only. The scalar phase of $U$ is implemented as a phase gate on the control and is not discarded.

items.title: Exact Three-CNOT Synthesis of Two-Qubit Unitaries
items.statement: Every $U\in U(4)$ has an exact circuit with no ancillas, at most three CNOT gates, and arbitrary one-qubit gates. The scalar phase is implemented as a one-qubit scalar gate and is not discarded.

items.title: Two-CNOT Synthesis up to a Migrating Terminal Diagonal
items.statement: Every $U\in U(4)$ factors exactly as $U=\Delta V$, where $\Delta$ is diagonal in the ordered two-qubit computational basis and $V$ has a no-ancilla circuit with at most two CNOTs and arbitrary one-qubit gates. Scalar phases are retained. Consequently, if a chronological circuit has $N\ge1$ arbitrary two-qubit slots all on the same two wires and each separator preserves every computational label on those two wires, the slots can be synthesized using at most $2(N-1)+3$ CNOTs in total, leaving the separator operations unchanged. This counts only the slots' CNOTs.

items.title: Exact Central Controlled-Z Absorption at a QSD Node
items.statement: Let $k\ge1$, let the first of $k+1$ wires be the target, and let $L=\operatorname{diag}(L_0,L_1)$ and $R=\operatorname{diag}(R_0,R_1)$ be generic block-diagonal unitaries in that target's basis. Let $M$ be a multiplexed $R_y$ on that target, selected by the other $k$ wires. The exact matrix $LMR$ can be represented by four generic $k$-qubit slots, two multiplexed $R_z$ factors and a central network with only $2^k-1$ controlled-$Z$ gates and arbitrary one-qubit rotations. Each controlled-$Z$ costs one CNOT. Thus one CNOT is saved relative to demultiplexing $L,R$ and using a full $2^k$-CNOT central rotation. The exact rewritten factors add no workspace, preserve scalar phases, and keep every non-target wire a select wire within the central network.

items.title: Generic No-Ancilla CNOT Lower Bound
items.statement:
Assume AC$_\omega$ to form normalized Frobenius volume. For $n\ge1$, almost every $n$-qubit unitary with respect to that measure requires at least
$$\left\lceil\frac{4^n-3n-1}{4}\right\rceil$$
CNOT gates in an exact circuit with arbitrary one-qubit gates and no ancillas. Under full AC, normalized Frobenius volume is normalized Haar measure, so the same is a Haar-almost-everywhere bound. This is a generic lower bound and is not a per-unitary assertion.
items.axiom_use: Assume AC_omega for normalized Frobenius volume; assume full AC only for the optional identification with normalized Haar measure.

items.title: Linear Multicontrolled X with One Borrowed Wire
items.statement: For every integer $r\ge1$, an $r$-controlled $X$ on $r$ control wires and one target has an exact circuit of $O(r)$ arbitrary one-qubit gates and CNOTs when one additional borrowed wire is available. The circuit equals $C^r(X)\otimes I$ on the entire register: the borrowed wire is returned unchanged for every state, including states entangled with the controls, target, or an external register. No wire is initialized or measured.

items.title: Exact QSD CNOT Upper Bound
items.statement:
For $n\ge2$, every $n$-qubit unitary has an exact no-ancilla circuit with arbitrary one-qubit gates and at most
$$\frac{23}{48}4^n-\frac32 2^n+\frac43$$
CNOTs. For $n=1$, no CNOT is needed. For $n=0$, a circuit on the empty register realizes a scalar unitary exactly if and only if it is $1$; the empty circuit realizes this identity with no gates. This is a gate-count bound; it makes no numerical decomposition-time or finite-precision bit-complexity claim.

items.title: Multicontrolled Unitaries with and without a Clean Work Bit
items.statement:
For $m\ge1$ controls and exact $U\in U(2)$, define
$$C^m(U)=\sum_{x\ne1^m}|x\rangle\langle x|\otimes I_2+|1^m\rangle\langle1^m|\otimes U.$$
This controlled operation has (i) a no-workspace exact construction with $O(m^2)$ one-qubit and CNOT gates, and (ii) an exact construction using one clean work bit, initially $0$ and returned to $0$, with $O(m)$ such gates. For nonscalar $U$, every exact circuit needs at least $m$ two-qubit gates, also when auxiliary wires are allowed with data-independent initial state and exact clean or dirty return. Clean auxiliary wires start at $0$ and return to $0$ for every data input; dirty auxiliary wires may start in any state and the full operation is $C^m(U)\otimes I$ on them, including correlated inputs. A fixed auxiliary state may be internally entangled but is initially independent of the data. These are upper/lower bounds; the quadratic no-work construction is not asserted optimal.

items.title: Gray-Path Synthesis of a Two-Level Gate
items.statement:
Input distinct $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$, $n\ge1$, exact $V\in U(2)$, and for each controlled call a choice between the no-workspace and clean-bit constructions of [[thm-qc-multicontrolled-ancilla-resource-tradeoff]]. If any call selects the clean-bit construction, supply one clean bit initialized to $0$. Output: the chronological elementary-gate list on the $n$ data wires and, if selected, that one clean work wire.

Let $g_0=x,\ldots,g_d=y$ be the path that flips the differing bit positions once in increasing order, where $d$ is the Hamming distance. For $j=0,\ldots,d-2$, swap $g_j$ and $g_{j+1}$ by an $X$ on their differing bit controlled on the other $n-1$ bits matching their common pattern. Apply $V$ to the final pair $g_{d-1},y$ by a one-qubit target gate controlled on their common other bits, reversing the ordered $2\times2$ block if $g_{d-1}$ has target bit $1$. Undo the swaps in reverse order. Expand every multi-control using its selected construction; implement negative controls by conjugating that control wire with $X$.

Use the selected literal elementary gate list for each call without deleting identity gates or cancelling neighboring gates. In the one-control base use the three target matrices and one control phase as four arbitrary one-qubit gates. Use the same choices and reversed adjoint gate lists for the return swaps. Reuse the supplied clean bit sequentially; each selected clean-bit construction returns it to $0$.

items.title: Correctness of Gray-Path Two-Level Synthesis
items.statement:
The algorithm of [[alg-qc-two-level-gate-to-elementary-gates]] realizes the exact two-level unitary on the ordered selected pair $(x,y)$ and fixes every other computational-basis vector. Write $d$ for their Hamming distance and $m=n-1$. Before expansion there are $2(d-1)$ pattern-controlled swaps and one pattern-controlled target block.

Here are exact post-expansion counts for its literal circuits. A cost pair $(c,q)$ counts CNOTs and arbitrary one-qubit gates, respectively; pairs are added componentwise and identity gate occurrences are retained. Define
$$E_1=(1,0),\quad E_2=(8,12),\quad E_s=(4s-8)(8,12)\quad(s\ge3),$$
$$B_1=(1,0),\quad B_2=(8,12),\quad B_r=2E_{\lceil r/2\rceil}+2E_{\lfloor r/2\rfloor+1}\quad(r\ge3).$$
For a positive $m$-controlled one-qubit call the no-workspace cost is
$$Q_0=(0,1),\quad Q_1=(2,4),\quad Q_m=Q_{m-1}+2B_{m-1}+(4,8)\quad(m\ge2),$$
and the selected one-clean-bit cost is $K_m=2B_m+(2,4)$ for $m\ge1$ (use $K_0=Q_0$ with no work bit). For each forward swap $j$, choose $S_j\in\{Q_m,K_m\}$, and for the middle block choose $T\in\{Q_m,K_m\}$. If $z_j$ and $z_V$ are the numbers of zero-valued controls in their patterns, the exact total pair is
$$2\sum_{j=0}^{d-2}\bigl(S_j+(0,2z_j)\bigr)+T+(0,2z_V).$$
Its sum of coordinates is the exact elementary gate count. All-no-workspace selection uses $n$ wires and $O(dn^2)$ gates; all-clean selection uses at most $n+1$ wires and $O(dn)$ gates. For mixed selections one clean bit suffices and is reused sequentially, returned to zero after each call. When $n=1$, the circuit is one arbitrary one-qubit gate with cost $(0,1)$ and no work bit.

proposed_after_items.title: Global Phase Equivalence
proposed_after_items.statement: For square matrices $U,V$ of the same size, write $U\sim_{\mathrm{phase}}V$ when $U=\lambda V$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ with $|\lambda|=1$. This relation is kept distinct from exact matrix equality.

proposed_after_items.title: Demultiplexing a Two-Block Unitary
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $U_0,U_1$ be unitary endomorphisms of $H$. On the control-first direct sum $H\oplus H$, the block unitary $\operatorname{diag}(U_0,U_1)$ factors as
$$\operatorname{diag}(U_0,U_1)=(I\otimes V)\operatorname{diag}(D,D^*)(I\otimes W)$$
for unitary $V,W$ on $H$ and a diagonal unitary $D$ in an orthonormal eigenbasis; $I\otimes V$ denotes $\operatorname{diag}(V,V)$ under $\mathbb C^2\otimes H\cong H\oplus H$.

proposed_after_items.title: Cayley Charts on the Unitary Matrix Group
proposed_after_items.statement:
For $N\ge1$, define $U(N)=\{Q\in M_N(\mathbb C):Q^*Q=QQ^*=I\}$ and $\mathfrak u(N)=\{X\in M_N(\mathbb C):X^*=-X\}$, both regarded as real spaces where appropriate. Then $U(N)$ is a compact smooth real manifold of dimension $N^2$. Near $I$, the Cayley map
$$X\longmapsto (I+X)(I-X)^{-1}$$
is a smooth chart from $\mathfrak u(N)$; left translates give a finite atlas. The Frobenius inner product induces a smooth Riemannian metric. Under AC$_\omega$, its volume density defines a normalized Borel volume probability $\mu_F$; a Borel subset is $\mu_F$-null exactly when its intersection with every chart has Lebesgue-null coordinate image. Under AC, $\mu_F$ is the normalized Haar probability, so this also gives the Haar-null criterion in that branch.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: Assume AC_omega for the Radon volume measure; assume full AC only for the optional identification with normalized Haar probability.

proposed_after_items.title: Cosine-Sine Block Decomposition
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $k\ge1$ and let $U\in U(2k)$ be partitioned into $k\times k$ blocks
$$U=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\ C&D\end{pmatrix}.$$
There are block-diagonal unitaries $L=\operatorname{diag}(L_0,L_1)$ and $R=\operatorname{diag}(R_0,R_1)$ and nonnegative real diagonal matrices $C_0,S_0$ such that
$$U=L\begin{pmatrix}C_0&-S_0\\S_0&C_0\end{pmatrix}R,\qquad C_0^2+S_0^2=I,\quad 0\le C_0,S_0\le I.$$
The singular values at $0$ and $1$ are allowed, with no nondegeneracy assumption.

proposed_after_items.title: Two-Level Unitary
proposed_after_items.statement: Let a finite ordered register have an orthonormal computational basis $(|z\rangle)_{z\in\mathcal X}$, using the root convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. For distinct labels $x,y\in\mathcal X$, choose $V\in U(2)$, where $U(2)=\{M\in M_2(\mathbb C):M^*M=MM^*=I_2\}$. The **two-level unitary** $T_{x,y}(V)$ acts by the matrix $V$ in the ordered basis $(|x\rangle,|y\rangle)$ and acts as the identity on $\operatorname{span}\{|x\rangle,|y\rangle\}^{\perp}$. Its action is exact matrix equality: any scalar phase contained in $V$ is retained.

proposed_after_items.title: Exact Two-Level Elimination of a Unitary
proposed_after_items.statement:
Input: an exact-arithmetic representation of $U\in U(N)$, $N\ge1$, supporting addition, multiplication, conjugation, nonnegative square roots, exact zero tests, and exact division by nonzero positive real scalars. Output: a finite ordered factorization into two-level unitaries and a diagonal unitary. This is an exact algebraic procedure; no claim of a bit-time algorithm for arbitrary real input is made.

Initialize $M:=U$ and an empty chronological list. For each column $j=0,\ldots,N-2$, and for $r=N-1,N-2,\ldots,j+1$, set $a=M_{r-1,j}$ and $b=M_{r,j}$. If $b=0$, do nothing. Otherwise set $h=\sqrt{|a|^2+|b|^2}>0$ and left-multiply rows $(r-1,r)$ by
$$G=\frac1h\begin{pmatrix}\overline a&\overline b\\-b&a\end{pmatrix},$$
recording this two-level unitary in the order applied. Let the resulting matrix be $D$. Return the factorization $U=G_1^*\cdots G_s^*D$. In chronological circuit order, apply $D$ first and then $G_s^*,\ldots,G_1^*$.

proposed_after_items.title: Correctness and Termination of Two-Level Elimination
proposed_after_items.statement: For $U\in U(N)$, the elimination procedure of [[alg-qc-two-level-unitary-elimination]] terminates after at most $N(N-1)/2$ Givens steps and returns an exact factorization of $U$ into the recorded two-level adjoints followed by a diagonal unitary. The number of diagonal entries is $N$; entries equal to $1$ need no phase gate.

proposed_after_items.title: One-Qubit Euler Decomposition
proposed_after_items.statement:
Use the rotation convention of [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]] and define $R_y(\theta):=R_{(0,1,0)}(\theta)$:
$$R_z(\alpha)=\begin{pmatrix}e^{-i\alpha/2}&0\\0&e^{i\alpha/2}\end{pmatrix},\qquad R_y(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta/2)&-\sin(\theta/2)\\\sin(\theta/2)&\cos(\theta/2)\end{pmatrix}.$$
For every $U\in U(2)$ there are real $\delta,\alpha,\theta,\beta$ with
$$U=e^{i\delta}R_z(\alpha)R_y(\theta)R_z(\beta).$$
If $\det U=1$, the scalar factor is unnecessary and $U=R_z(\alpha)R_y(\theta)R_z(\beta)$.

proposed_after_items.title: Exact Two-Qubit Cartan Decomposition
proposed_after_items.statement:
For every $U\in U(4)$ there are $A,B,C,D\in SU(2)$, real $a,b,c,\delta$, and the matrices
$$X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$
such that
$$U=e^{i\delta}(A\otimes B)\exp\!\bigl(i(aX\otimes X+bY\otimes Y+cZ\otimes Z)\bigr)(C\otimes D).$$
The equality is exact; the scalar $e^{i\delta}$ is displayed.

proposed_after_items.title: Global Phase Under Control
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional target space, let $U$ be unitary on $H$, and let $|\lambda|=1$. In control-first order put
$$C(U)=\begin{pmatrix}I_H&0\\0&U\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_\lambda=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\lambda\end{pmatrix}.$$
Then $C(\lambda U)=(P_\lambda\otimes I_H)C(U)$. A scalar multiplying an entire output leaves every defined finite-POVM outcome law unchanged, whereas a scalar attached to a target matrix inside a control gives a phase on only the active control block; applying $P_{\overline\lambda}$ on the control restores the exact controlled matrix.

proposed_after_items.title: Parameter Count for a Fixed CNOT Skeleton
proposed_after_items.statement: Assume AC$_\omega$ to form normalized Frobenius volume on $U(2^n)$. For fixed $n\ge1$ and a fixed ordered CNOT skeleton with $m$ CNOTs, arbitrary exact one-qubit gates, and no ancillas, the set of exact circuit matrices is contained in a finite union of smooth images of real parameter spaces of dimension at most $3n+4m+1$. If $3n+4m+1<4^n$, this fixed skeleton has measure zero. Under full AC, it is Haar-null.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: AC_omega is assumed for the normalized smooth volume measure; full AC is needed only for the optional Haar identification.

proposed_after_items.title: Gray-Code Synthesis of a Multiplexed Axis Rotation
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $k\ge0$ controls have computational labels $x\in\{0,1\}^k$, and let $\theta_x\in\mathbb R$. Fix $a\in\{x,y,z\}$. On one target qubit define
$$M=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^k}|x\rangle\langle x|\otimes R_a(\theta_x),\qquad R_a(t)=\exp(-it\sigma_a/2).$$
Then $M$ is exactly synthesized with $2^k$ CNOTs for $k>0$ (the final CNOT restores the parity network). For $a=y,z$ it uses $2^k$ target rotations $R_a(\beta_j)$; for $a=x$ it uses $2^k$ $R_y$ rotations in the fixed target basis described below; for $k=0$ it is one rotation and no CNOT. For $a=x$ and $k>0$ the implementation also uses two fixed target basis-change gates; the $y,z$ implementations need none. One may replace the cyclic Gray traversal by a traversal that omits the final restoration and absorb that final parity into the next block only when that block is explicitly specified.

proposed_after_items.title: Exact Controlled One-Qubit Unitary with Two CNOTs
proposed_after_items.statement: For every $U\in U(2)$, the exact controlled matrix $C(U)=\operatorname{diag}(I_2,U)$ is realized with two CNOTs and one-qubit gates only. The scalar phase of $U$ is implemented as a phase gate on the control and is not discarded.

proposed_after_items.title: Exact Three-CNOT Synthesis of Two-Qubit Unitaries
proposed_after_items.statement: Every $U\in U(4)$ has an exact circuit with no ancillas, at most three CNOT gates, and arbitrary one-qubit gates. The scalar phase is implemented as a one-qubit scalar gate and is not discarded.

proposed_after_items.title: Two-CNOT Synthesis up to a Migrating Terminal Diagonal
proposed_after_items.statement: Every $U\in U(4)$ factors exactly as $U=\Delta V$, where $\Delta$ is diagonal in the ordered two-qubit computational basis and $V$ has a no-ancilla circuit with at most two CNOTs and arbitrary one-qubit gates. Scalar phases are retained. Consequently, if a chronological circuit has $N\ge1$ arbitrary two-qubit slots all on the same two wires and each separator preserves every computational label on those two wires, the slots can be synthesized using at most $2(N-1)+3$ CNOTs in total, leaving the separator operations unchanged. This counts only the slots' CNOTs.

proposed_after_items.title: Exact Central Controlled-Z Absorption at a QSD Node
proposed_after_items.statement: Let $k\ge1$, let the first of $k+1$ wires be the target, and let $L=\operatorname{diag}(L_0,L_1)$ and $R=\operatorname{diag}(R_0,R_1)$ be generic block-diagonal unitaries in that target's basis. Let $M$ be a multiplexed $R_y$ on that target, selected by the other $k$ wires. The exact matrix $LMR$ can be represented by four generic $k$-qubit slots, two multiplexed $R_z$ factors and a central network with only $2^k-1$ controlled-$Z$ gates and arbitrary one-qubit rotations. Each controlled-$Z$ costs one CNOT. Thus one CNOT is saved relative to demultiplexing $L,R$ and using a full $2^k$-CNOT central rotation. The exact rewritten factors add no workspace, preserve scalar phases, and keep every non-target wire a select wire within the central network.

proposed_after_items.title: Generic No-Ancilla CNOT Lower Bound
proposed_after_items.statement:
Assume AC$_\omega$ to form normalized Frobenius volume. For $n\ge1$, almost every $n$-qubit unitary with respect to that measure requires at least
$$\left\lceil\frac{4^n-3n-1}{4}\right\rceil$$
CNOT gates in an exact circuit with arbitrary one-qubit gates and no ancillas. Under full AC, normalized Frobenius volume is normalized Haar measure, so the same is a Haar-almost-everywhere bound. This is a generic lower bound and is not a per-unitary assertion.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: Assume AC_omega for normalized Frobenius volume; assume full AC only for the optional identification with normalized Haar measure.

proposed_after_items.title: Linear Multicontrolled X with One Borrowed Wire
proposed_after_items.statement: For every integer $r\ge1$, an $r$-controlled $X$ on $r$ control wires and one target has an exact circuit of $O(r)$ arbitrary one-qubit gates and CNOTs when one additional borrowed wire is available. The circuit equals $C^r(X)\otimes I$ on the entire register: the borrowed wire is returned unchanged for every state, including states entangled with the controls, target, or an external register. No wire is initialized or measured.

proposed_after_items.title: Exact QSD CNOT Upper Bound
proposed_after_items.statement:
For $n\ge2$, every $n$-qubit unitary has an exact no-ancilla circuit with arbitrary one-qubit gates and at most
$$\frac{23}{48}4^n-\frac32 2^n+\frac43$$
CNOTs. For $n=1$, no CNOT is needed. For $n=0$, a circuit on the empty register realizes a scalar unitary exactly if and only if it is $1$; the empty circuit realizes this identity with no gates. This is a gate-count bound; it makes no numerical decomposition-time or finite-precision bit-complexity claim.

proposed_after_items.title: Multicontrolled Unitaries with and without a Clean Work Bit
proposed_after_items.statement:
For $m\ge1$ controls and exact $U\in U(2)$, define
$$C^m(U)=\sum_{x\ne1^m}|x\rangle\langle x|\otimes I_2+|1^m\rangle\langle1^m|\otimes U.$$
This controlled operation has (i) a no-workspace exact construction with $O(m^2)$ one-qubit and CNOT gates, and (ii) an exact construction using one clean work bit, initially $0$ and returned to $0$, with $O(m)$ such gates. For nonscalar $U$, every exact circuit needs at least $m$ two-qubit gates, also when auxiliary wires are allowed with data-independent initial state and exact clean or dirty return. Clean auxiliary wires start at $0$ and return to $0$ for every data input; dirty auxiliary wires may start in any state and the full operation is $C^m(U)\otimes I$ on them, including correlated inputs. A fixed auxiliary state may be internally entangled but is initially independent of the data. These are upper/lower bounds; the quadratic no-work construction is not asserted optimal.

proposed_after_items.title: Gray-Path Synthesis of a Two-Level Gate
proposed_after_items.statement:
Input distinct $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$, $n\ge1$, exact $V\in U(2)$, and for each controlled call a choice between the no-workspace and clean-bit constructions of [[thm-qc-multicontrolled-ancilla-resource-tradeoff]]. If any call selects the clean-bit construction, supply one clean bit initialized to $0$. Output: the chronological elementary-gate list on the $n$ data wires and, if selected, that one clean work wire.

Let $g_0=x,\ldots,g_d=y$ be the path that flips the differing bit positions once in increasing order, where $d$ is the Hamming distance. For $j=0,\ldots,d-2$, swap $g_j$ and $g_{j+1}$ by an $X$ on their differing bit controlled on the other $n-1$ bits matching their common pattern. Apply $V$ to the final pair $g_{d-1},y$ by a one-qubit target gate controlled on their common other bits, reversing the ordered $2\times2$ block if $g_{d-1}$ has target bit $1$. Undo the swaps in reverse order. Expand every multi-control using its selected construction; implement negative controls by conjugating that control wire with $X$.

Expand the calls by the following procedures. Every list below is chronological; concatenation means execute the left list first. Order control wires and available spare wires by their register positions. All parameter selections are exact mathematical operations: use exact matrix arithmetic, a finite-dimensional unitary eigendecomposition, polar arguments and the Euler parameter selection of [[thm-qc-one-qubit-euler-decomposition]]. The input representation must support these selections and exact zero tests; no finite-precision bit-time claim is made. Fix each selection when its call is first expanded and retain the resulting list for an inverse call.

For one control $c$, target $t$ and matrix $W$, choose $W=e^{i\delta}R_z(\alpha)R_y(\theta)R_z(\beta)$ as in [[thm-qc-one-qubit-euler-decomposition]]. Form the three matrices $A=R_z(\alpha)R_y(\theta/2)$, $B=R_y(-\theta/2)R_z(- (\alpha+\beta)/2)$ and $C=R_z((\beta-\alpha)/2)$. Define $S(c,t;W)$ to be the list $C_t$, $\mathrm{CNOT}_{c\to t}$, $B_t$, $\mathrm{CNOT}_{c\to t}$, $A_t$, $\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\delta})_c$. Each of $A,B,C$ is one arbitrary one-qubit gate, as in [[thm-qc-one-control-unitary-two-cnot]]. Define $T(a,b;t)$ by setting $J=((1+i)I+(1-i)X)/2$ and concatenating $S(b,t;J)$, $\mathrm{CNOT}_{a\to b}$, $S(b,t;J^*)$, $\mathrm{CNOT}_{a\to b}$, $S(a,t;J)$.

Define the ladder list $L(c_1,\ldots,c_s;t)$ with an ordered supply of at least $\max\{s-2,0\}$ distinct spare wires. For $s=1$ emit one CNOT; for $s=2$ emit $T(c_1,c_2;t)$. For $s\ge3$, use the first $s-2$ spares $a_1,\ldots,a_{s-2}$. Set $T_1=T(c_1,c_2;a_1)$, $T_j=T(c_{j+1},a_{j-1};a_j)$ for $2\le j\le s-2$, and $H=T(c_s,a_{s-2};t)$. Concatenate $T_1,\ldots,T_{s-2},H,T_{s-2},\ldots,T_1$ and then $T_2,\ldots,T_{s-2},H,T_{s-2},\ldots,T_2$; the latter list is just $H$ when $s=3$. This is the borrowed ladder used in [[lem-qc-borrowed-bit-multicontrolled-x-linear]].

Define $D(C;t;z)$ for an ordered nonempty control set $C$ and a distinct borrowed wire $z$. With one or two controls use the corresponding ladder base case and leave $z$ unused. With $r\ge3$ controls split $C$ into its first $p=\lceil r/2\rceil$ controls $A$ and the remaining $q=\lfloor r/2\rfloor$ controls $B$. Let $F=L(A;z)$ use spares from $B\cup\{t\}$, and let $G=L(B\cup\{z\};t)$ use spares from $A$. Emit $F,G,F,G$, using the same parameter choices for repeated lists. The stated spare supplies have at least $p-2$ and $q-1$ wires, respectively.

Define the positive-control no-workspace expansion $N(C;t;W)$ recursively. If $C$ is empty, emit $W_t$. If it has one wire $c$, emit $S(c,t;W)$. Otherwise write $C=A\cup\{b\}$, with $b$ its last control. Choose an orthonormal eigendecomposition $W=R\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)R^*$ by [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]], choose polar angles $\lambda_j=\cos u_j+i\sin u_j$ by [[thm-polar-form-with-unique-principal-argument]], and set $Z=R\operatorname{diag}(\cos(u_1/2)+i\sin(u_1/2),\cos(u_2/2)+i\sin(u_2/2))R^*$. The addition formulas of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]] specify these half-angle roots. Emit $S(b,t;Z)$, $D(A;b;t)$, $S(b,t;Z^*)$, $D(A;b;t)$, $N(A;t;Z)$. The last call has one fewer control and uses only its indicated wires.

For the positive-control clean-bit expansion with nonempty $C$ and clean wire $w$, emit $D(C;w;t)$, $S(w,t;W)$, and the reversed adjoint of that same $D$ list. With no controls emit $W_t$ and leave $w$ unused. These are the two constructions analyzed in [[thm-qc-multicontrolled-ancilla-resource-tradeoff]]. For a pattern control, conjugate the selected whole positive-control list by one $X$ on each zero-valued control, ordering each set of these $X$ gates by wire position. Reverse the ordered middle block by using $XVX$ as its single matrix parameter, not by adding target $X$ occurrences.

Use the selected literal elementary gate list for each call without deleting identity gates or cancelling neighboring gates. In the one-control base use the three target matrices and one control phase as four arbitrary one-qubit gates. Use the same choices and reversed adjoint gate lists for the return swaps. Reuse the supplied clean bit sequentially; each selected clean-bit construction returns it to $0$.

proposed_after_items.title: Correctness of Gray-Path Two-Level Synthesis
proposed_after_items.statement:
The algorithm of [[alg-qc-two-level-gate-to-elementary-gates]] realizes the exact two-level unitary on the ordered selected pair $(x,y)$ and fixes every other computational-basis vector. Write $d$ for their Hamming distance and $m=n-1$. Before expansion there are $2(d-1)$ pattern-controlled swaps and one pattern-controlled target block.

Here are exact post-expansion counts for its literal circuits. A cost pair $(c,q)$ counts CNOTs and arbitrary one-qubit gates, respectively; pairs are added componentwise and identity gate occurrences are retained. Define
$$E_1=(1,0),\quad E_2=(8,12),\quad E_s=(4s-8)(8,12)\quad(s\ge3),$$
$$B_1=(1,0),\quad B_2=(8,12),\quad B_r=2E_{\lceil r/2\rceil}+2E_{\lfloor r/2\rfloor+1}\quad(r\ge3).$$
For a positive $m$-controlled one-qubit call the no-workspace cost is
$$Q_0=(0,1),\quad Q_1=(2,4),\quad Q_m=Q_{m-1}+2B_{m-1}+(4,8)\quad(m\ge2),$$
and the selected one-clean-bit cost is $K_m=2B_m+(2,4)$ for $m\ge1$ (use $K_0=Q_0$ with no work bit). For each forward swap $j$, choose $S_j\in\{Q_m,K_m\}$, and for the middle block choose $T\in\{Q_m,K_m\}$. If $z_j$ and $z_V$ are the numbers of zero-valued controls in their patterns, the exact total pair is
$$2\sum_{j=0}^{d-2}\bigl(S_j+(0,2z_j)\bigr)+T+(0,2z_V).$$
Its sum of coordinates is the exact elementary gate count. All-no-workspace selection uses $n$ wires and $O(dn^2)$ gates; all-clean selection uses at most $n+1$ wires and $O(dn)$ gates. For mixed selections one clean bit suffices and is reused sequentially, returned to zero after each call. When $n=1$, the circuit is one arbitrary one-qubit gate with cost $(0,1)$ and no work bit.

statement.after:
Set $\omega=e^{i\pi/4}$, $K=\mathbb Q(\omega)$, $O=\mathbb Z[\omega]$, and
$D=O[1/2]=\mathbb Z[\omega,1/2]$. The relation $\omega^4=-1$ reduces every
element of $O$ to four integer coefficients in the power basis
$1,\omega,\omega^2,\omega^3$. The canonical dyadic encoding of a nonzero
$z\in D$ is

$$z=(a_0+a_1\omega+a_2\omega^2+a_3\omega^3)/2^r,$$

where $r\ge0$ is least and, if $r>0$, the four integers are not all even.
Zero is encoded with $r=0$ and all four coefficients zero. Arithmetic is exact:
multiply polynomials, reduce with $\omega^4=-1$, combine denominators, and
remove the common power of $2$ from the coefficients. The integral-basis
supplier [[thm-cyclotomic-ring-of-integers]] and the proof of
[[lem-qc-dyadic-coefficient-encoding]] justify existence and uniqueness.

references.title: Kliuchnikov, Maslov, and Mosca, Fast and efficient exact synthesis of single qubit unitaries generated by Clifford and T gates
de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

statement.after:
A matrix $U\in U(2)$ is exactly the matrix of a finite one-qubit Clifford+T
word if and only if all four entries of $U$ lie in $D$. This is a
single-qubit statement; no multi-qubit exact ring characterization is
asserted.

items.title: Circuit-family and computation cost model
items.statement:
Fix the finite circuit syntax and its complete self-delimiting binary description ([[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]]). For a circuit $C$, let $L(C)$ be the number of bits in that complete description, $g(C)$ its number of gate occurrences, and $w(C)$ its total number of wires.

Each clean or dirty ancilla coordinate additionally requires a declared ordered partition of the circuit wires into data register $D$ and ancilla register $A$, and a declared target unitary $V$ on $D$. In that factor order, the complete circuit unitary must satisfy the corresponding exact contract of [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]]. For such a supplied clean contract set $a_{\rm clean}(C)=|A|$, and for such a supplied dirty contract set $a_{\rm dirty}(C)=|A|$; the notation suppresses the declared interface, which is part of the cost instance and may differ between the two coordinates. If no corresponding contract is supplied, mark that coordinate not applicable. These are counts of declared contract registers, not maxima over possible partitions. Zero initialization alone supplies neither return contract. Every auxiliary wire remains counted in $w(C)$ ([[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]).

The gate sequence and supports determine a finite dependency order: each earlier gate occurrence must precede every later occurrence that acts on a shared wire. A **layering** assigns a positive integer layer to each gate occurrence, strictly increasing along those shared-wire precedence relations. Gates in one layer therefore have pairwise disjoint supports. Define the depth $d(C)$ to be the least number of layers in such a layering; if $C$ has no gates, set $d(C)=0$. If layers are written $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ in chronological order, the denotation is $U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}$, as in [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]].

For a family $(C_n)$ with a specified full-list generator $G$, let $t_G(n)$ be the worst-case number of Turing-machine transitions used by $G$ on unary input $1^n$. For a total acceptance predicate $A_n(x,z)$, let $t_A(n)$ and $s_A(n)$ be its worst-case deterministic transition count and tape-space use over all valid length-$n$ inputs and measured outputs, using a fixed effective encoding of the pair $(x,z)$. Any effective input description, classical preprocessing, or threshold computation has its own bit length and time/space bounds; these costs are not included in $t_G$ or $t_A$ unless the same machine performs them. The machine conventions are those of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]], [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

If the access model explicitly supplies a named oracle gate $\mathcal O$, let $q_{\mathcal O}(C)$ be the number of calls to it. With several named oracles, record a separate query coordinate for each. Ordinary finite-basis gates, oracle calls, circuit-description length, generator time, and classical bit costs remain separate; no oracle, controlled-oracle, inverse-oracle, or data-loading operation is assigned zero cost unless its interface explicitly says so.

For an approximate task with declared rational tolerance $0<\epsilon<1$, let $\ell(\epsilon)$ be the bit length of that exact binary-rational encoding. Exact finite-gate computations have no precision field. The **cost record** consists of all applicable coordinates
$$\bigl(L(C_n),g(C_n),d(C_n),w(C_n),a_{\rm clean}(C_n),a_{\rm dirty}(C_n),t_G(n),t_A(n),s_A(n),q_{\mathcal O}(C_n),\epsilon,\ell(\epsilon)\bigr).$$
An inapplicable coordinate is marked not applicable, not silently charged as zero. This definition records the resource model; separate theorems establish polynomial bounds.

items.title: Finite quantum promise-computation model
items.statement:
Let $\Pi=(Y,N)$ be a promise problem: $Y,N\subseteq\{0,1\}^*$ are disjoint, and no answer is required outside $Y\cup N$ ([[def-promise-problem]]). For every input length $n\ge0$, let $a(n)\in\mathbb N$ be the number of auxiliary qubits. The $n$ input wires are ordered with the first wire most significant: for $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$, $|x\rangle$ is the computational-basis vector indexed by
$$\operatorname{enc}_n(x)=\sum_{k<n}x_k2^{n-1-k}$$
([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]]). The auxiliary register has $a(n)$ wires and is initialized to $|0^{a(n)}\rangle$. When $n=0$ or $a(n)=0$, the corresponding zero-qubit register is the one-dimensional space $\mathbb C$, not the zero vector space.

For each $n$, a finite circuit $C_n$ acts on the ordered register of $n+a(n)$ wires and has the unitary denotation $U_{C_n}$ specified by [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]] and [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]]. The circuit syntax designates an ordered tuple of distinct output-wire indices; an acceptance specification uses that same tuple $O_n$, whose indices lie in $\{0,\ldots,n+a(n)-1\}$. It consists of this tuple and a total predicate $A_n(x,z)\in\{0,1\}$ for $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ and $z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}$. The tuple may be empty; then its measured output set contains only the empty word. Auxiliary wires are initialized to zero, but this definition does not require them to return to zero after the computation; that stronger clean-ancilla condition is defined in [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]].

A **finite quantum promise computation** is the data $(\Pi,(C_n)_{n\ge0},a,O,A)$ with these registers and predicates. Its output is classical: measure only the named output wires in the computational basis and accept exactly when $A_n(x,z)=1$. No intermediate measurement is part of this base model. Unless a full-list uniformity condition is imposed separately, the family need not be generated uniformly. When uniformity or cost is claimed, $A$ is supplied by one fixed deterministic Turing machine with an explicit polynomial worst-case time bound in the encoded pair $(x,z)$ ([[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]], [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]]). This is a mathematical finite-circuit model and makes no assertion about physical realization.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Sections IV.1–IV.2

items.title: Full-list uniform quantum circuit family
items.statement:
A **full-list uniform quantum circuit family** is a sequence $(C_n)_{n\ge0}$ together with one fixed deterministic one-tape Turing machine $G$ and constants $c\ge1$ and $k\in\mathbb N$ such that, on input the unary word $1^n$, $G$ halts within $c(n+1)^k$ transitions and its final tape is a valid self-delimiting binary description of the entire circuit $C_n$. The machine output convention is that of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]] and [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and running time is as in [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

The following fixed-order code makes the full circuit and its designated input/output wires effective. A unary natural $r\in\mathbb N$ is written $1^r0$, including the one-symbol code $0$ for $r=0$. A self-delimiting binary natural $r$ is written $1^{|\operatorname{bin}(r)|}0\operatorname{bin}(r)$, where $\operatorname{bin}(r)$ is its ordinary binary numeral with no leading zeros and $\operatorname{bin}(0)=0$. The header gives the input-wire count $n$ and total wire count $m$ in unary, followed by the gate count $g$ as a self-delimiting natural; validity requires $m\ge n$.

Each gate record consists of a two-bit label ($00,01,10,11$ for $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ respectively), followed by one self-delimiting wire index for $H,T,T^\dagger$ and two ordered self-delimiting indices for CNOT. Every index is less than $m$; CNOT indices are distinct, with the first the control and the second the target. The list contains exactly $g$ records. After the gate list, an output-count self-delimiting natural is followed by that many ordered, pairwise distinct wire indices, each less than $m$. Parsing rejects every other label, malformed or out-of-range index, repeated output index, truncated field, or trailing bit. This defines a total decoder by returning a fixed malformed-code symbol on any invalid word; effective binary encodings and total decoders are as in [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]].

The gate labels and matrices are the fixed finite library $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ of [[def-qc-clifford-t-gate-library]], with entries in $\mathbb Q(\zeta_8)=\mathbb Q(i,\sqrt2)$; CNOT is control-first. The remaining $m-n$ wires are auxiliary wires; their initial states are determined when a family is used in a computation model. This family convention adopts full-list generation. It makes no equivalence claim with indexed-gate uniformity and, in particular, does not assert that an indexed-gate generator can be expanded to the full list in polynomial time.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Sections III.2 and IV.1
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2

items.title: Quantum acceptance probability for a finite promise computation
items.statement:
Fix a length-$n$ finite promise computation from [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]], with input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, zero-initialized auxiliary register $|0^{a(n)}\rangle$, circuit unitary $U_{C_n}$, and ordered output-wire tuple $O_n$. Let $P_{O_n}$ be the tensor-factor permutation that moves $O_n$, in its declared order, to the front, and let $W_n$ be the ordered tuple of all remaining wires ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]). Set
$$\psi_x:=U_{C_n}(|x\rangle\otimes|0^{a(n)}\rangle),\qquad v_x:=\operatorname{coord}(P_{O_n}\psi_x).$$
Here coordinates are in the ordered computational basis, and the root inner product is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For $z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}$ and $w\in\{0,1\}^{|W_n|}$, write $e_{z,w}$ for the corresponding product-basis vector and define
$$p_{C_n}(z\mid x):=\sum_{w\in\{0,1\}^{|W_n|}}\left|\langle P_{O_n}\psi_x,e_{z,w}\rangle_{\rm root}\right|^2.$$
The acceptance probability is
$$p_{C_n}(x):=\sum_{\substack{z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}\\A_n(x,z)=1}}p_{C_n}(z\mid x).$$
Equivalently, if $E_{A,x}$ is the diagonal projection onto the basis vectors $(z,w)$ with $A_n(x,z)=1$, then $p_{C_n}(x)=\operatorname{Tr}(E_{A,x}v_xv_x^\dagger)$; the matrix adjoint is conjugate transpose in an orthonormal basis ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]]).

These are finite sums. The definition itself does not assert normalization, positivity of the resulting operator expression, or a probability bound; those consequences are the purpose of [[thm-qc-output-acceptance-law-normalizes]]. No Dirac bra convention is used here: every amplitude uses the root pairing displayed above.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Sections III.2 and IV.1
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2

items.title: A full-list uniform generator bounds circuit size and width
items.statement: If the generator in [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]] halts on input $1^n$ within $T(n)\le c(n+1)^k$ transitions, then the generated description has length at most $n+T(n)+O(1)$. Consequently its number of gates and total number of wires are polynomial in $n$. This is a full-list size bound; it does not establish equivalence with indexed-gate uniformity.
