items.title: Oracle-aware full-list quantum circuit family
items.statement:
An **oracle-aware full-list family** has an access specification and a deterministic polynomial-time full-list generator on unary input $1^n$, with the same machine, clock, and final-tape conventions as [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]. The access specification gives, at each length $n$, finitely many named ports $\mathcal O_{n,j}$, each a unitary on a positive number $k_{n,j}$ of qubits. These are mathematical unitary data supplied by the access specification, not matrices computed by the generator. For a parametrized oracle instance, fix that instance throughout a computation and all its repetitions. The generator, printed descriptors, and final classical predicate are independent of the hidden instance: its influence enters only through the granted unitary ports. Any public parameters are fixed explicitly as part of the family specification; oracle comparisons hold them fixed. A port acts only on the wires in its occurrence; there is no persistent private oracle memory, stochastic resampling, or communication between disjoint occurrences through hidden registers.

Each port has a descriptor: a distinct nonempty binary name, its width $k_{n,j}$, and four grant bits for forward, inverse, controlled-forward, and controlled-inverse access. At least one variant is granted. A granted variant has an explicitly specified positive integer query charge $c_{n,j,v}$; an ungranted variant cannot occur. Forward and inverse have arity $k_{n,j}$; controlled variants have arity $k_{n,j}+1$, with the first wire the control and the remaining ordered wires the target. Their mathematical actions are respectively $\mathcal O_{n,j}$, $\mathcal O_{n,j}^{\dagger}$, and the corresponding controlled unitary (identity on control $0$, the indicated unitary on control $1$). Mathematical existence of an inverse or controlled unitary grants no access to it. The descriptors printed by the generator must agree with the supplied access specification at every length; syntactic decoding alone does not decide this semantic condition.

The following is a separate binary format; the original two-bit Clifford+T format of [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]] remains unchanged. Use its unary and self-delimiting natural codes. The header gives $n,m$ in unary with $m\ge n$, then the total number $g$ of operation occurrences and the number of port descriptors as self-delimiting naturals. Each descriptor gives the name length as a self-delimiting natural followed by exactly that many name bits, the positive port width in unary, four grant bits in the order above, and one positive self-delimiting charge for each granted variant in that order. Descriptor order fixes port indices starting at zero.

The header and descriptors are followed by exactly $g$ operation records. A three-bit label $000,001,010,011$ denotes respectively ordinary $H,T,T^{\dagger},\mathrm{CNOT}$ and is followed by the same ordered wire-index fields as in the original format. Label $100$ denotes an oracle slot: a self-delimiting port index, a two-bit variant index in the descriptor order, and exactly the variant's arity many ordered self-delimiting wire indices. Every index is below $m$, and wires within each record are distinct. The final output-count and ordered distinct output-wire list use the original format. All other labels, duplicate names, ungranted variants, invalid fields, truncations, and trailing bits are rejected. As in the original code, the decoder is total by returning a malformed-code symbol on rejection. The generator prints this entire description, including every descriptor and every slot, within its explicit polynomial clock. The port count, widths, names, and charges must therefore fit in that printed description; neither an exponentially long list nor an implicit operation subroutine counts as full-list output.

For a fixed length and oracle instance, instantiating the slots gives an ordinary finite unitary circuit with a finite enlarged gate alphabet in the sense underlying [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]. Use the ordered wire embedding and chronological composition of that item. Zero auxiliary initialization, final output measurement, and a separately supplied total polynomial-time classical predicate are exactly those of [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]]; acceptance is the finite coordinate sum in [[def-qc-quantum-acceptance-probability]]. No oracle call is performed by the classical generator or predicate unless a separate classical access interface is declared; here neither is granted one.

In the cost convention of [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]], $g(C)$ counts all operation occurrences. Write $g_{\rm ord}(C)$ for the number of ordinary records and $N_{j,v}(C)$ for the number of slots for port $j$, variant $v$. Thus $g(C)=g_{\rm ord}(C)+\sum_{j,v}N_{j,v}(C)$. Record the raw call count $q_j(C)=\sum_vN_{j,v}(C)$ and, separately, the declared charged query cost $Q_j(C)=\sum_v c_{n,j,v}N_{j,v}(C)$. A polynomial bound on the binary description length does not imply a polynomial bound on $Q_j$ if charges have large binary values. Ordinary CNOT records incur ordinary gate cost and no query, even if a named port happens to have the same matrix. Oracle records remain query records even when their matrices admit an ordinary implementation; substituting such an implementation is a separate construction and cost claim.

The **ordinary mode** instead uses the exact original full-list code with no ports or query slots. In particular the oracle-aware format does not enlarge the gate library or alter the exact arithmetic convention of the QC14 BQP definition.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Sections III.2 and IV.1
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapters 2 and 13

items.title: Bounded-error repetition amplification
items.statement:
**Inputs.** In ordinary mode, a full-list uniform family generator $G$ in the exact fixed-library format of [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]; or, in oracle mode, an oracle-aware full-list generator and its granted access specification as in [[def-qc-oracle-full-list-circuit-family]]. In either mode supply a total deterministic acceptance-predicate machine $A$ and explicit polynomial clock bounds, with zero auxiliary initialization, output tuples, and acceptance as in [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]] and [[def-qc-quantum-acceptance-probability]]; machines that output exact binary rationals $\alpha(n),\beta(n),\delta(n)$ with explicit polynomial clock bounds; and a fixed positive integer-valued polynomial $s(n)$ with an exact rational-coefficient representation. The machine descriptions and clock bounds are fixed parts of the input data, and each rational output has polynomial bit length. Valid inputs satisfy, for every $n$,
$$0\le \beta(n)<\alpha(n)\le1,\qquad \alpha(n)-\beta(n)\ge\frac1{s(n)},\qquad 0<\delta(n)\le\frac12.$$
The procedure checks the clock and syntax at each requested length and returns INVALID if a run exceeds its supplied clock, a code is malformed, or any displayed inequality fails. Its domain consists of descriptions whose stated polynomial bounds and inequalities hold for all $n$; the procedure does not decide that global validity property for arbitrary machine descriptions.

**Instructions at length $n$.**

1. Run the supplied machines within their polynomial clocks to obtain the full description of $C_n$, $\alpha=\alpha(n)$, $\beta=\beta(n)$, and $\delta=u/v$ with positive integers $u,v$. In oracle mode, also compare the printed port descriptors with the supplied access specification at length $n$; on any mismatch return INVALID. Evaluate $s(n)$ exactly from its fixed rational-coefficient polynomial. Check that it is a positive integer, check exact rational syntax, and check the validity inequalities by integer arithmetic; on failure return INVALID.
2. Let $\ell(v)$ be the number of binary digits of $v$ and set
$$r:=2s^2\bigl(\ell(v)+1\bigr).$$
This is a positive integer. No logarithm or irrational ceiling is evaluated.
3. Allocate $r$ disjoint copies of the entire $C_n$ wire register in block order, with block $1$ first. Put the classical-basis input $|x\rangle$ on the first block's first $n$ wires; initialize every other wire to zero. For $j=2,\ldots,r$ in increasing order, and then $i=0,\ldots,n-1$ in increasing order, append a CNOT from wire $i$ of block $1$ to wire $i$ of block $j$, with the first wire as control. These operations map $|x\rangle|0^n\rangle^{\otimes(r-1)}$ to $|x\rangle^{\otimes r}$ and do not clone arbitrary superpositions. Then, for blocks $j=1,\ldots,r$ in order, append the records of $C_n$ in their supplied chronological order, shifting each wire index by $(j-1)w(C_n)$. This serializes each base circuit's records; gates listed in a common layer have disjoint supports, so serialization preserves its denotation. Keep the first block's $n$ input wires first in the output wire order and encode input count $n$; every other wire is auxiliary. In oracle mode, retain each slot's port and granted variant, shift only its ordered wire indices by the block offset, and copy the access descriptors once. The added CNOTs are ordinary records, never query slots. The repeated circuit has $r w(C_n)$ wires and $r g(C_n)+n(r-1)$ operation occurrences; in oracle mode its ordinary count is $r g_{\rm ord}(C_n)+n(r-1)$.
4. Concatenate the $r$ copies of the declared output tuple in copy order and measure that tuple at the final readout. For measured strings $z_1,\ldots,z_r$, compute $S=\#\{i:A_n(x,z_i)=1\}$. The single total output predicate returns YES exactly when $2S\ge r(\alpha+\beta)$, evaluated exactly: if $\alpha=A/B$ and $\beta=C/D$ with positive denominators, compare $2SBD$ with $r(AD+CB)$. Return NO otherwise.

The output is one full-list repeated circuit in the input mode's format and its total classical predicate. Ordinary mode uses only the original fixed library. In oracle mode every base port/variant occurrence is repeated $r$ times: $N_{j,v}$, raw call counts $q_j$, and charged query costs $Q_j$ all scale by $r$, with unchanged grants and per-call charges ([[def-qc-oracle-full-list-circuit-family]]). Query costs remain separate from ordinary gates and classical bit costs ([[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]). The endpoint comparison is classical postprocessing, not an intermediate measurement or coherent amplitude-amplification step. Correctness, uniformity, and resource bounds are separate claims proved by [[thm-qc-bounded-error-amplification-correct]].

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Section IV.2
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2 and Appendix B.2

items.title: Acceptance is invariant under an unconditional global phase
items.statement: For a finite promise computation, replacing its entire unconditional circuit unitary $U_C$ by $\lambda U_C$, where $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ and $|\lambda|=1$, leaves every output probability $p_C(z\mid x)$ and hence $p_C(x)$ unchanged. A scalar inserted only in the target block of a controlled operation need not preserve acceptance: there is an explicit two-qubit finite-circuit witness below.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Sections III.2 and IV.1
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2

items.title: The partial-output acceptance law is a finite probability law
items.statement: For every finite promise computation, every length $n$, and every classical input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, the output weights $p_{C_n}(z\mid x)$ from [[def-qc-quantum-acceptance-probability]] are nonnegative and sum to one over $z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}$. The acceptance probability is the probability of the event $\{z:A_n(x,z)=1\}$, lies in $[0,1]$, and agrees with the finite computational-basis POVM outcome law on the named output register.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Sections III.2 and IV.1
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2

items.title: BQP for promise problems in the fixed QC14 model
items.statement:
A promise problem $\Pi=(Y,N)$ belongs to **BQP in the QC14 model** when there exist a full-list uniform family $(C_n)$ and a polynomial-time acceptance predicate $A_n$ as in [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]] and [[def-qc-quantum-acceptance-probability]] such that, for every $x\in Y$,
$$p_{C_{|x|}}(x)\ge\frac23,$$
and for every $x\in N$,
$$p_{C_{|x|}}(x)\le\frac13.$$
By [[thm-qc-output-acceptance-law-normalizes]], $p_{C_n}(x)$ is the probability of the specified acceptance event and lies in $[0,1]$. No condition is imposed for $x\notin Y\cup N$ ([[def-promise-problem]]). The gate alphabet is exactly $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$; its matrix entries lie in $\mathbb Q(\zeta_8)=\mathbb Q(i,\sqrt2)$ as specified by [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]. This definition does not assert a BQP-versus-classical separation, nor does it assert an unproved equivalence with another circuit-uniformity convention.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Sections IV.1–IV.2
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2

items.title: Bounded-error repetition amplification is correct and uniform
items.statement: Assume the input family, rational threshold functions, gap polynomial, and clocks satisfy the valid-input conditions of [[alg-qc-bounded-error-amplification]]. Assume also that the base acceptance satisfies $p_{C_n}(x)\ge\alpha(n)$ for every length-$n$ YES input and $p_{C_n}(x)\le\beta(n)$ for every length-$n$ NO input, where $0\le\beta(n)<\alpha(n)\le1$ and $\alpha(n)-\beta(n)\ge1/s(n)$. On every input in the YES promise set, the amplified acceptance probability is at least $1-\delta(n)$; on every input in the NO promise set, it is at most $\delta(n)$. If $g(C_n)$ and $w(C_n)$ are the base gate count and total wire count, the repeated family has gate count $r(n)g(C_n)+n(r(n)-1)$ and width $r(n)w(C_n)$. Its depth, complete-description length, generator time, and classical predicate time and space are polynomial in $n$. Ordinary mode retains the exact original fixed gate library and full-list code. In oracle mode its ordinary gate count is $r(n)g_{\rm ord}(C_n)+n(r(n)-1)$, every port/variant count satisfies $N_{j,v}(C_n^{\rm rep})=r(n)N_{j,v}(C_n)$, and both raw query counts $q_j$ and charged query costs $Q_j$ are multiplied by $r(n)$ with the same granted access. Raw query counts are polynomial; charged query costs are polynomial whenever the base charged costs are polynomial. Whenever the base interface declares clean or dirty ancillary registers satisfying the corresponding exact contract, each such register's count is multiplied by $r(n)$; the extra input-copy wires remain in total width and are not counted as returned clean ancillas.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Section IV.2
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2 and Appendix B.2

items.title: BQP is unchanged by polynomially small bounded error
items.statement:
Let $q:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be computable in deterministic polynomial time and polynomially bounded, with $q(n)\ge2$ for all sufficiently large $n$. For every promise problem, the following are equivalent in the QC14 full-list model:

1. it has a uniformly generated family and polynomial-time acceptance predicate with acceptance at least $2/3$ on YES and at most $1/3$ on NO;
2. it has a uniformly generated family and polynomial-time acceptance predicate with acceptance at least $1-2^{-q(n)}$ on YES and at most $2^{-q(n)}$ on NO.

More generally, suppose a uniformly generated family with a polynomial-time acceptance predicate satisfies $p_{C_n}(x)\ge\alpha(n)$ on length-$n$ YES inputs and $p_{C_n}(x)\le\beta(n)$ on length-$n$ NO inputs, where $\alpha(n),\beta(n)$ are polynomial-time computable rationals and there is a positive integer-valued polynomial $s(n)$ such that $0\le\beta(n)<\alpha(n)\le1$ and $\alpha(n)-\beta(n)\ge1/s(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$. It can be modified to achieve the same exponentially small target error $2^{-q(n)}$. This result does not assert the gap-only implication $\mathrm{BQP}(\alpha,\beta)=\mathrm{BQP}$ for arbitrary endpoint thresholds.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Section IV.2
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2 and Appendix B.2

proposed_after_items.title: Circuit-family and computation cost model
proposed_after_items.statement:
Fix the finite circuit syntax and its complete self-delimiting binary description ([[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]]). For a circuit $C$, let $L(C)$ be the number of bits in that complete description, $g(C)$ its number of gate occurrences, and $w(C)$ its total number of wires.

Each clean or dirty ancilla coordinate additionally requires a declared ordered partition of the circuit wires into data register $D$ and ancilla register $A$, and a declared target unitary $V$ on $D$. In that factor order, the complete circuit unitary must satisfy the corresponding exact contract of [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]]. For such a supplied clean contract set $a_{\rm clean}(C)=|A|$, and for such a supplied dirty contract set $a_{\rm dirty}(C)=|A|$; the notation suppresses the declared interface, which is part of the cost instance and may differ between the two coordinates. If no corresponding contract is supplied, mark that coordinate not applicable. These are counts of declared contract registers, not maxima over possible partitions. Zero initialization alone supplies neither return contract. Every auxiliary wire remains counted in $w(C)$ ([[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]).

The gate sequence and supports determine a finite dependency order: each earlier gate occurrence must precede every later occurrence that acts on a shared wire. A **layering** assigns a positive integer layer to each gate occurrence, strictly increasing along those shared-wire precedence relations. Gates in one layer therefore have pairwise disjoint supports. Define the depth $d(C)$ to be the least number of layers in such a layering; if $C$ has no gates, set $d(C)=0$. If layers are written $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ in chronological order, the denotation is $U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}$, as in [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]].

For a family $(C_n)$ with a specified full-list generator $G$, let $t_G(n)$ be the worst-case number of Turing-machine transitions used by $G$ on unary input $1^n$. For a total acceptance predicate $A_n(x,z)$, let $t_A(n)$ and $s_A(n)$ be its worst-case deterministic transition count and tape-space use over all valid length-$n$ inputs and measured outputs, using a fixed effective encoding of the pair $(x,z)$. Any effective input description, classical preprocessing, or threshold computation has its own bit length and time/space bounds; these costs are not included in $t_G$ or $t_A$ unless the same machine performs them. The machine conventions are those of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]], [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

If the access model explicitly supplies a named oracle gate $\mathcal O$, let $q_{\mathcal O}(C)$ be the number of calls to it. With several named oracles, record a separate query coordinate for each. Ordinary finite-basis gates, oracle calls, circuit-description length, generator time, and classical bit costs remain separate; no oracle, controlled-oracle, inverse-oracle, or data-loading operation is assigned zero cost unless its interface explicitly says so.

For an approximate task with declared rational tolerance $0<\epsilon<1$, let $\ell(\epsilon)$ be the bit length of that exact binary-rational encoding. Exact finite-gate computations have no precision field. The **cost record** consists of all applicable coordinates
$$\bigl(L(C_n),g(C_n),d(C_n),w(C_n),a_{\rm clean}(C_n),a_{\rm dirty}(C_n),t_G(n),t_A(n),s_A(n),q_{\mathcal O}(C_n),\epsilon,\ell(\epsilon)\bigr).$$
An inapplicable coordinate is marked not applicable, not silently charged as zero. This definition records the resource model; separate theorems establish polynomial bounds.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Sections III.2 and IV.1
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2

proposed_after_items.title: Finite quantum promise-computation model
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $\Pi=(Y,N)$ be a promise problem: $Y,N\subseteq\{0,1\}^*$ are disjoint, and no answer is required outside $Y\cup N$ ([[def-promise-problem]]). For every input length $n\ge0$, let $a(n)\in\mathbb N$ be the number of auxiliary qubits. The $n$ input wires are ordered with the first wire most significant: for $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$, $|x\rangle$ is the computational-basis vector indexed by
$$\operatorname{enc}_n(x)=\sum_{k<n}x_k2^{n-1-k}$$
([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]]). The auxiliary register has $a(n)$ wires and is initialized to $|0^{a(n)}\rangle$. When $n=0$ or $a(n)=0$, the corresponding zero-qubit register is the one-dimensional space $\mathbb C$, not the zero vector space.

For each $n$, a finite circuit $C_n$ acts on the ordered register of $n+a(n)$ wires and has the unitary denotation $U_{C_n}$ specified by [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]] and [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]]. The circuit syntax designates an ordered tuple of distinct output-wire indices; an acceptance specification uses that same tuple $O_n$, whose indices lie in $\{0,\ldots,n+a(n)-1\}$. It consists of this tuple and a total predicate $A_n(x,z)\in\{0,1\}$ for $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ and $z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}$. The tuple may be empty; then its measured output set contains only the empty word. Auxiliary wires are initialized to zero, but this definition does not require them to return to zero after the computation; that stronger clean-ancilla condition is defined in [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]].

A **finite quantum promise computation** is the data $(\Pi,(C_n)_{n\ge0},a,O,A)$ with these registers and predicates. Its output is classical: measure only the named output wires in the computational basis and accept exactly when $A_n(x,z)=1$. No intermediate measurement is part of this base model. Unless a full-list uniformity condition is imposed separately, the family need not be generated uniformly. When uniformity or cost is claimed, $A$ is supplied by one fixed deterministic Turing machine with an explicit polynomial worst-case time bound in the encoded pair $(x,z)$ ([[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]], [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]]). This is a mathematical finite-circuit model and makes no assertion about physical realization.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Sections IV.1–IV.2
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2

proposed_after_items.title: Full-list uniform quantum circuit family
proposed_after_items.statement:
A **full-list uniform quantum circuit family** is a sequence $(C_n)_{n\ge0}$ together with one fixed deterministic one-tape Turing machine $G$ and constants $c\ge1$ and $k\in\mathbb N$ such that, on input the unary word $1^n$, $G$ halts within $c(n+1)^k$ transitions and its final tape is a valid self-delimiting binary description of the entire circuit $C_n$. The machine output convention is that of [[def-deterministic-one-tape-turing-machine]] and [[def-partial-function-computed-by-a-machine]], and running time is as in [[def-worst-case-time-and-space-complexity]].

The following fixed-order code makes the full circuit and its designated input/output wires effective. A unary natural $r\in\mathbb N$ is written $1^r0$, including the one-symbol code $0$ for $r=0$. A self-delimiting binary natural $r$ is written $1^{|\operatorname{bin}(r)|}0\operatorname{bin}(r)$, where $\operatorname{bin}(r)$ is its ordinary binary numeral with no leading zeros and $\operatorname{bin}(0)=0$. The header gives the input-wire count $n$ and total wire count $m$ in unary, followed by the gate count $g$ as a self-delimiting natural; validity requires $m\ge n$.

Each gate record consists of a two-bit label ($00,01,10,11$ for $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ respectively), followed by one self-delimiting wire index for $H,T,T^\dagger$ and two ordered self-delimiting indices for CNOT. Every index is less than $m$; CNOT indices are distinct, with the first the control and the second the target. The list contains exactly $g$ records. After the gate list, an output-count self-delimiting natural is followed by that many ordered, pairwise distinct wire indices, each less than $m$. Parsing rejects every other label, malformed or out-of-range index, repeated output index, truncated field, or trailing bit. This defines a total decoder by returning a fixed malformed-code symbol on any invalid word; effective binary encodings and total decoders are as in [[def-effective-binary-encoding-and-decoder]].

The gate labels and matrices are the fixed finite library $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ of [[def-qc-clifford-t-gate-library]], with entries in $\mathbb Q(\zeta_8)=\mathbb Q(i,\sqrt2)$; CNOT is control-first. The remaining $m-n$ wires are auxiliary wires; their initial states are determined when a family is used in a computation model. This family convention adopts full-list generation. It makes no equivalence claim with indexed-gate uniformity and, in particular, does not assert that an indexed-gate generator can be expanded to the full list in polynomial time.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Sections III.2 and IV.1
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2

proposed_after_items.title: Quantum acceptance probability for a finite promise computation
proposed_after_items.statement:
Fix a length-$n$ finite promise computation from [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]], with input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, zero-initialized auxiliary register $|0^{a(n)}\rangle$, circuit unitary $U_{C_n}$, and ordered output-wire tuple $O_n$. Let $P_{O_n}$ be the tensor-factor permutation that moves $O_n$, in its declared order, to the front, and let $W_n$ be the ordered tuple of all remaining wires ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]). Set
$$\psi_x:=U_{C_n}(|x\rangle\otimes|0^{a(n)}\rangle),\qquad v_x:=\operatorname{coord}(P_{O_n}\psi_x).$$
Here coordinates are in the ordered computational basis, and the root inner product is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For $z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}$ and $w\in\{0,1\}^{|W_n|}$, write $e_{z,w}$ for the corresponding product-basis vector and define
$$p_{C_n}(z\mid x):=\sum_{w\in\{0,1\}^{|W_n|}}\left|\langle P_{O_n}\psi_x,e_{z,w}\rangle_{\rm root}\right|^2.$$
The acceptance probability is
$$p_{C_n}(x):=\sum_{\substack{z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}\\A_n(x,z)=1}}p_{C_n}(z\mid x).$$
Equivalently, if $E_{A,x}$ is the diagonal projection onto the basis vectors $(z,w)$ with $A_n(x,z)=1$, then $p_{C_n}(x)=\operatorname{Tr}(E_{A,x}v_xv_x^\dagger)$; the matrix adjoint is conjugate transpose in an orthonormal basis ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]]).

These are finite sums. The definition itself does not assert normalization, positivity of the resulting operator expression, or a probability bound; those consequences are the purpose of [[thm-qc-output-acceptance-law-normalizes]]. No Dirac bra convention is used here: every amplitude uses the root pairing displayed above.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Sections III.2 and IV.1
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2

proposed_after_items.title: A full-list uniform generator bounds circuit size and width
proposed_after_items.statement: If the generator in [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]] halts on input $1^n$ within $T(n)\le c(n+1)^k$ transitions, then the generated description has length at most $n+T(n)+O(1)$. Consequently its number of gates and total number of wires are polynomial in $n$. This is a full-list size bound; it does not establish equivalence with indexed-gate uniformity.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Section IV.1
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2

proposed_after_items.title: Oracle-aware full-list quantum circuit family
proposed_after_items.statement:
An **oracle-aware full-list family** has an access specification and a deterministic polynomial-time full-list generator on unary input $1^n$, with the same machine, clock, and final-tape conventions as [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]. The access specification gives, at each length $n$, finitely many named ports $\mathcal O_{n,j}$, each a unitary on a positive number $k_{n,j}$ of qubits. These are mathematical unitary data supplied by the access specification, not matrices computed by the generator. For a parametrized oracle instance, fix that instance throughout a computation and all its repetitions. The generator, printed descriptors, and final classical predicate are independent of the hidden instance: its influence enters only through the granted unitary ports. Any public parameters are fixed explicitly as part of the family specification; oracle comparisons hold them fixed. A port acts only on the wires in its occurrence; there is no persistent private oracle memory, stochastic resampling, or communication between disjoint occurrences through hidden registers.

Each port has a descriptor: a distinct nonempty binary name, its width $k_{n,j}$, and four grant bits for forward, inverse, controlled-forward, and controlled-inverse access. At least one variant is granted. A granted variant has an explicitly specified positive integer query charge $c_{n,j,v}$; an ungranted variant cannot occur. Forward and inverse have arity $k_{n,j}$; controlled variants have arity $k_{n,j}+1$, with the first wire the control and the remaining ordered wires the target. Their mathematical actions are respectively $\mathcal O_{n,j}$, $\mathcal O_{n,j}^{\dagger}$, and the corresponding controlled unitary (identity on control $0$, the indicated unitary on control $1$). Mathematical existence of an inverse or controlled unitary grants no access to it. The descriptors printed by the generator must agree with the supplied access specification at every length; syntactic decoding alone does not decide this semantic condition.

The following is a separate binary format; the original two-bit Clifford+T format of [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]] remains unchanged. Use its unary and self-delimiting natural codes. The header gives $n,m$ in unary with $m\ge n$, then the total number $g$ of operation occurrences and the number of port descriptors as self-delimiting naturals. Each descriptor gives the name length as a self-delimiting natural followed by exactly that many name bits, the positive port width in unary, four grant bits in the order above, and one positive self-delimiting charge for each granted variant in that order. Descriptor order fixes port indices starting at zero.

The header and descriptors are followed by exactly $g$ operation records. A three-bit label $000,001,010,011$ denotes respectively ordinary $H,T,T^{\dagger},\mathrm{CNOT}$ and is followed by the same ordered wire-index fields as in the original format. Label $100$ denotes an oracle slot: a self-delimiting port index, a two-bit variant index in the descriptor order, and exactly the variant's arity many ordered self-delimiting wire indices. Every index is below $m$, and wires within each record are distinct. The final output-count and ordered distinct output-wire list use the original format. All other labels, duplicate names, ungranted variants, invalid fields, truncations, and trailing bits are rejected. As in the original code, the decoder is total by returning a malformed-code symbol on rejection. The generator prints this entire description, including every descriptor and every slot, within its explicit polynomial clock. The port count, widths, names, and charges must therefore fit in that printed description; neither an exponentially long list nor an implicit operation subroutine counts as full-list output.

For a fixed length and oracle instance, instantiating the slots gives an ordinary finite unitary circuit with a finite enlarged gate alphabet in the sense underlying [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]. Use the ordered wire embedding and chronological composition of that item. Zero auxiliary initialization, final output measurement, and a separately supplied total polynomial-time classical predicate are exactly those of [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]]; acceptance is the finite coordinate sum in [[def-qc-quantum-acceptance-probability]]. No oracle call is performed by the classical generator or predicate unless a separate classical access interface is declared; here neither is granted one.

In the cost convention of [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]], $g(C)$ counts all operation occurrences. Write $g_{\rm ord}(C)$ for the number of ordinary records and $N_{j,v}(C)$ for the number of slots for port $j$, variant $v$. Thus $g(C)=g_{\rm ord}(C)+\sum_{j,v}N_{j,v}(C)$. Record the raw call count $q_j(C)=\sum_vN_{j,v}(C)$ and, separately, the declared charged query cost $Q_j(C)=\sum_v c_{n,j,v}N_{j,v}(C)$. A polynomial bound on the binary description length does not imply a polynomial bound on $Q_j$ if charges have large binary values. Ordinary CNOT records incur ordinary gate cost and no query, even if a named port happens to have the same matrix. Oracle records remain query records even when their matrices admit an ordinary implementation; substituting such an implementation is a separate construction and cost claim.

The **ordinary mode** instead uses the exact original full-list code with no ports or query slots. In particular the oracle-aware format does not enlarge the gate library or alter the exact arithmetic convention of the QC14 BQP definition.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Sections III.2 and IV.1
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapters 2 and 13

proposed_after_items.title: Bounded-error repetition amplification
proposed_after_items.statement:
**Inputs.** In ordinary mode, a full-list uniform family generator $G$ in the exact fixed-library format of [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]; or, in oracle mode, an oracle-aware full-list generator and its granted access specification as in [[def-qc-oracle-full-list-circuit-family]]. In either mode supply a total deterministic acceptance-predicate machine $A$ and explicit polynomial clock bounds, with zero auxiliary initialization, output tuples, and acceptance as in [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]] and [[def-qc-quantum-acceptance-probability]]; machines that output exact binary rationals $\alpha(n),\beta(n),\delta(n)$ with explicit polynomial clock bounds; and a fixed positive integer-valued polynomial $s(n)$ with an exact rational-coefficient representation. The machine descriptions and clock bounds are fixed parts of the input data, and each rational output has polynomial bit length. Valid inputs satisfy, for every $n$,
$$0\le \beta(n)<\alpha(n)\le1,\qquad \alpha(n)-\beta(n)\ge\frac1{s(n)},\qquad 0<\delta(n)\le\frac12.$$
The procedure checks the clock and syntax at each requested length and returns INVALID if a run exceeds its supplied clock, a code is malformed, or any displayed inequality fails. Its domain consists of descriptions whose stated polynomial bounds and inequalities hold for all $n$; the procedure does not decide that global validity property for arbitrary machine descriptions.

**Instructions at length $n$.**

1. Run the supplied machines within their polynomial clocks to obtain the full description of $C_n$, $\alpha=\alpha(n)$, $\beta=\beta(n)$, and $\delta=u/v$ with positive integers $u,v$. In oracle mode, also compare the printed port descriptors with the supplied access specification at length $n$; on any mismatch return INVALID. Evaluate $s(n)$ exactly from its fixed rational-coefficient polynomial. Check that it is a positive integer, check exact rational syntax, and check the validity inequalities by integer arithmetic; on failure return INVALID.
2. Let $\ell(v)$ be the number of binary digits of $v$ and set
$$r:=2s^2\bigl(\ell(v)+1\bigr).$$
This is a positive integer. No logarithm or irrational ceiling is evaluated.
3. Allocate $r$ disjoint copies of the entire $C_n$ wire register in block order, with block $1$ first. Put the classical-basis input $|x\rangle$ on the first block's first $n$ wires; initialize every other wire to zero. For $j=2,\ldots,r$ in increasing order, and then $i=0,\ldots,n-1$ in increasing order, append a CNOT from wire $i$ of block $1$ to wire $i$ of block $j$, with the first wire as control. These operations map $|x\rangle|0^n\rangle^{\otimes(r-1)}$ to $|x\rangle^{\otimes r}$ and do not clone arbitrary superpositions. Then, for blocks $j=1,\ldots,r$ in order, append the records of $C_n$ in their supplied chronological order, shifting each wire index by $(j-1)w(C_n)$. This serializes each base circuit's records; gates listed in a common layer have disjoint supports, so serialization preserves its denotation. Keep the first block's $n$ input wires first in the output wire order and encode input count $n$; every other wire is auxiliary. In oracle mode, retain each slot's port and granted variant, shift only its ordered wire indices by the block offset, and copy the access descriptors once. The added CNOTs are ordinary records, never query slots. The repeated circuit has $r w(C_n)$ wires and $r g(C_n)+n(r-1)$ operation occurrences; in oracle mode its ordinary count is $r g_{\rm ord}(C_n)+n(r-1)$.
4. Concatenate the $r$ copies of the declared output tuple in copy order and measure that tuple at the final readout. For measured strings $z_1,\ldots,z_r$, compute $S=\#\{i:A_n(x,z_i)=1\}$. The single total output predicate returns YES exactly when $2S\ge r(\alpha+\beta)$, evaluated exactly: if $\alpha=A/B$ and $\beta=C/D$ with positive denominators, compare $2SBD$ with $r(AD+CB)$. Return NO otherwise.

The output is one full-list repeated circuit in the input mode's format and its total classical predicate. Ordinary mode uses only the original fixed library. In oracle mode every base port/variant occurrence is repeated $r$ times: $N_{j,v}$, raw call counts $q_j$, and charged query costs $Q_j$ all scale by $r$, with unchanged grants and per-call charges ([[def-qc-oracle-full-list-circuit-family]]). Query costs remain separate from ordinary gates and classical bit costs ([[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]). The endpoint comparison is classical postprocessing, not an intermediate measurement or coherent amplitude-amplification step. Correctness, uniformity, and resource bounds are separate claims proved by [[thm-qc-bounded-error-amplification-correct]].

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Section IV.2
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2 and Appendix B.2

proposed_after_items.title: Acceptance is invariant under an unconditional global phase
proposed_after_items.statement: For a finite promise computation, replacing its entire unconditional circuit unitary $U_C$ by $\lambda U_C$, where $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ and $|\lambda|=1$, leaves every output probability $p_C(z\mid x)$ and hence $p_C(x)$ unchanged. A scalar inserted only in the target block of a controlled operation need not preserve acceptance: there is an explicit two-qubit finite-circuit witness below.

proposed_after_items.statement: For every finite promise computation, every length $n$, and every classical input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, the output weights $p_{C_n}(z\mid x)$ from [[def-qc-quantum-acceptance-probability]] are nonnegative and sum to one over $z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}$. The acceptance probability is the probability of the event $\{z:A_n(x,z)=1\}$, lies in $[0,1]$, and agrees with the finite computational-basis POVM outcome law on the named output register.

proposed_after_items.title: BQP for promise problems in the fixed QC14 model
proposed_after_items.statement:
A promise problem $\Pi=(Y,N)$ belongs to **BQP in the QC14 model** when there exist a full-list uniform family $(C_n)$ and a polynomial-time acceptance predicate $A_n$ as in [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]] and [[def-qc-quantum-acceptance-probability]] such that, for every $x\in Y$,
$$p_{C_{|x|}}(x)\ge\frac23,$$
and for every $x\in N$,
$$p_{C_{|x|}}(x)\le\frac13.$$
By [[thm-qc-output-acceptance-law-normalizes]], $p_{C_n}(x)$ is the probability of the specified acceptance event and lies in $[0,1]$. No condition is imposed for $x\notin Y\cup N$ ([[def-promise-problem]]). The gate alphabet is exactly $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$; its matrix entries lie in $\mathbb Q(\zeta_8)=\mathbb Q(i,\sqrt2)$ as specified by [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]. This definition does not assert a BQP-versus-classical separation, nor does it assert an unproved equivalence with another circuit-uniformity convention.

proposed_after_items.title: Bounded-error repetition amplification is correct and uniform
proposed_after_items.statement: Assume the input family, rational threshold functions, gap polynomial, and clocks satisfy the valid-input conditions of [[alg-qc-bounded-error-amplification]]. Assume also that the base acceptance satisfies $p_{C_n}(x)\ge\alpha(n)$ for every length-$n$ YES input and $p_{C_n}(x)\le\beta(n)$ for every length-$n$ NO input, where $0\le\beta(n)<\alpha(n)\le1$ and $\alpha(n)-\beta(n)\ge1/s(n)$. On every input in the YES promise set, the amplified acceptance probability is at least $1-\delta(n)$; on every input in the NO promise set, it is at most $\delta(n)$. If $g(C_n)$ and $w(C_n)$ are the base gate count and total wire count, the repeated family has gate count $r(n)g(C_n)+n(r(n)-1)$ and width $r(n)w(C_n)$. Its depth, complete-description length, generator time, and classical predicate time and space are polynomial in $n$. Ordinary mode retains the exact original fixed gate library and full-list code. In oracle mode its ordinary gate count is $r(n)g_{\rm ord}(C_n)+n(r(n)-1)$, every port/variant count satisfies $N_{j,v}(C_n^{\rm rep})=r(n)N_{j,v}(C_n)$, and both raw query counts $q_j$ and charged query costs $Q_j$ are multiplied by $r(n)$ with the same granted access. Raw query counts are polynomial; charged query costs are polynomial whenever the base charged costs are polynomial. For a base clean or dirty interface whose declared ancillary register is disjoint from the first $n$ input wires, the input-copy stage acts only on data, and the corresponding exact contract is preserved with its declared register count multiplied by $r(n)$; the extra input-copy wires remain in total width and are not counted as returned clean ancillas.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Section IV.2
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2 and Appendix B.2

proposed_after_items.title: BQP is unchanged by polynomially small bounded error
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $q:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be computable in deterministic polynomial time and polynomially bounded, with $q(n)\ge2$ for all sufficiently large $n$. For every promise problem, the following are equivalent in the QC14 full-list model:

1. it has a uniformly generated family and polynomial-time acceptance predicate with acceptance at least $2/3$ on YES and at most $1/3$ on NO;
2. it has a uniformly generated family and polynomial-time acceptance predicate with acceptance at least $1-2^{-q(n)}$ on YES and at most $2^{-q(n)}$ on NO.

More generally, suppose a uniformly generated family with a polynomial-time acceptance predicate satisfies $p_{C_n}(x)\ge\alpha(n)$ on length-$n$ YES inputs and $p_{C_n}(x)\le\beta(n)$ on length-$n$ NO inputs, where $\alpha(n),\beta(n)$ are polynomial-time computable rationals and there is a positive integer-valued polynomial $s(n)$ such that $0\le\beta(n)<\alpha(n)\le1$ and $\alpha(n)-\beta(n)\ge1/s(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$. It can be modified to achieve the same exponentially small target error $2^{-q(n)}$. This result does not assert the gap-only implication $\mathrm{BQP}(\alpha,\beta)=\mathrm{BQP}$ for arbitrary endpoint thresholds.

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Section IV.2
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2 and Appendix B.2

items.title: Phase aware n qubit pauli group
items.statement:
The displayed tensor powers are tensor maps on the ordered factors, using [[def-qc-tensor-map]].
Fix an integer $n\ge 1$. Let $\mathcal H_n=Q_2^{\otimes n}$ be the ordered tensor register of $n$ qubits from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and let $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. We name the wires $1,\ldots,n$; wire $j$ is position $j-1$ in the source's $0$-based factor list. Bit tuples use the big-endian encoding from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so the first wire is the most significant bit. Write $X_j$ and $Z_j$ for the tensor maps with the displayed one-qubit matrix on wire $j$ and the identity on every other wire. For $x,z\in\mathbb F_2^n$, set $X^x=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n X^{x_j}$ and $Z^z=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n Z^{z_j}$, where an exponent $0$ means the identity on that factor and an exponent $1$ means the displayed Pauli matrix. For $k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, define

$$P(k,x,z):=i^kX^xZ^z.$$

The **phase-aware $n$-qubit Pauli set** $\mathcal P_n$ is the set of these operators with matrix multiplication. Its scalar subset is $Z_n:=\{i^k I_{\mathcal H_n}:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$. The product-and-adjoint theorem proves that $\mathcal P_n$ is a group and that $Z_n$ is its center.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7

proof_obligations: define multiplication and identity conventions before using the group name.
items.axiom_use: None; this is a finite-dimensional definition.

items.title: Hadamard pauli action
items.statement: For a Hadamard gate $H_j$ on factor $j$, conjugation swaps the binary coordinates $x_j,z_j$ and changes the phase exactly by $2x_jz_j$ modulo $4$. In particular $HXH=Z$, $HZH=X$, and $HYH=-Y$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14
Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits

proof_obligations: explicit matrix/conjugation computation.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof is a finite matrix and tensor calculation.

items.title: Phase gate pauli action
items.statement: For a phase gate $S_j=\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$ on factor $j$, the binary update is $(x_j,z_j)\mapsto(x_j,z_j+x_j)$ and the phase update is $k\mapsto k+x_j$ modulo $4$. In particular $SXS^*=Y$ and $SZS^*=Z$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14
Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits

proof_obligations: explicit matrix calculation consistent with item 3’s phase convention.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof is a finite matrix and tensor calculation.

items.title: Pauli product and adjoint
items.statement:
For $k,k'\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$ and $x,z,x',z'\in\mathbb F_2^n$, with $P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z$ and $X^xZ^z$ ordered as written,

$$P(k,x,z)P(k',x',z')=P(k+k'+2(z\cdot x'),x+x',z+z'),$$

where the dot product is first evaluated in $\mathbb F_2$ as $0$ or $1$, and then multiplied by $2$ in $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$. The set $\mathcal P_n$ is a group. If $p\in\{0,1\}$ represents $x\cdot z\in\mathbb F_2$, then $P(k,x,z)^*=P(2p-k,x,z)=P(k,x,z)^{-1}$, and its center is $Z_n=\{i^k I:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7
Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits

proof_obligations: commute Zᶻ past Xˣ′ and track the scalar i power, including the integer representative of the parity bit.
items.axiom_use: None; all arguments are finite tensor and matrix calculations.

items.title: Binary Pauli label and quotient
items.statement:
Let $Z_n$ be the scalar center of $\mathcal P_n$. Define $P\sim Q$ when $P^{-1}Q\in Z_n$, and let $Q_n$ be the set of equivalence classes $[P]=PZ_n$. The proposed coset product is $[P][Q]=[PQ]$. The quotient theorem verifies this product is well-defined and proves that the assignment

$$\lambda:Q_n\longrightarrow V_n:=\mathbb F_2^n\oplus\mathbb F_2^n,\qquad [P(k,x,z)]\longmapsto(x,z)$$

is a group isomorphism to the additive group of $V_n$. A binary label deliberately forgets the scalar phase.

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7
M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications

proof_obligations: show the map is well-defined, onto, a homomorphism, and has exactly the scalar center as kernel.
items.axiom_use: None; this is a finite quotient construction.

items.title: Clifford normalizer
items.statement:
Work with actual unitary matrices, not equivalence classes modulo global phase. The $n$-qubit **Clifford normalizer** is

$$\mathcal C_n:=\{U\text{ unitary on }\mathcal H_n:U\mathcal P_nU^*=\mathcal P_n\}.$$

It is a group under matrix multiplication. Every scalar unitary $\lambda I$ with $|\lambda|=1$ belongs to $\mathcal C_n$ and has the same conjugation action as $I$; the chosen convention retains these distinct matrices.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: verify closure under products/inverses and distinguish global scalar phase from Pauli center.
items.axiom_use: None; group closure follows from finite matrix multiplication and unitary inverses.

items.title: CNOT Pauli action
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$ and let distinct $c,t\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be control and target indices. For CNOT $C_{c\to t}$ acting on $y\in\mathbb F_2^n$ by toggling coordinate $t$ by $y_c$, conjugation sends

$$P(k,x,z)\longmapsto P(k,x',z'),\qquad x'_t=x_t+x_c,\quad z'_c=z_c+z_t,$$

with all other coordinates unchanged and additions in $\mathbb F_2$. In particular, $X_c\mapsto X_cX_t$, $Z_c\mapsto Z_c$, $X_t\mapsto X_t$, and $Z_t\mapsto Z_cZ_t$; the phase coordinate $k$ is unchanged in the fixed $X^xZ^z$ order.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits

proof_obligations: calculate images on the four generators and extend using item 3.
items.axiom_use: None; the gate rules are finite basis and matrix calculations.

items.title: Hermitian Pauli phase criterion
items.statement: For $P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z\in\mathcal P_n$, the operator is Hermitian exactly when $k\equiv x\cdot z\pmod 2$. In that case $P(k,x,z)^2=I$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: compute the adjoint under the fixed Xᶻ ordering.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses the finite phase-aware product law.

items.title: Binary symplectic form
items.statement:
On $V_n=\mathbb F_2^n\oplus\mathbb F_2^n$, with coordinate order $(x,z)$, define

$$\omega((x,z),(x',z')):=x\cdot z'+z\cdot x'.$$

This is a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form over $\mathbb F_2$; $V_n$ has dimension $2n$. In characteristic two, alternating also implies symmetry.

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7
M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications

proof_obligations: check bilinearity and alternation in characteristic two; prove nondegeneracy by testing coordinate vectors. Optional supplier: thm-alternating-forms-have-a-symplectic-normal-form.
items.axiom_use: None; all claims follow by finite coordinate calculations.

items.title: Binary Pauli quotient isomorphism
items.statement: The map $\pi:\mathcal P_n\to V_n$, $P(k,x,z)\mapsto(x,z)$, is a surjective group homomorphism with kernel exactly $Z_n$. Therefore the quotient map in [[def-qc-binary-pauli-label-and-quotient]] is an isomorphism $\mathcal P_n/Z_n\cong (V_n,+)$, and $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}V_n=2n$. No phase or label ambiguity occurs, including when $n=1$.

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7
M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

proof_obligations: Prove exact Pauli label uniqueness up to scalar using ordered computational-basis vectors.
Use the phase-aware multiplication law to prove homomorphism, kernel, surjectivity, and dimension, including n=1.
items.axiom_use: None; surjectivity, injectivity, and dimension use explicit finite coordinates.

items.title: Phase-aware binary Clifford tableau
items.statement:
Fix the generator order $X_1,\ldots,X_n,Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$ and label order $(x,z)$, with wire indices as in [[def-qc-phase-aware-n-qubit-pauli-group]]. For an actual Clifford unitary $U\in\mathcal C_n$, write each exact generator image uniquely as

$$UX_jU^*=P(k_j,x_j,z_j),\qquad UZ_jU^*=P(k_{n+j},x_{n+j},z_{n+j}).$$

Its **phase-aware binary Clifford tableau** is the pair $(S,p)$, where $S\in M_{2n}(\mathbb F_2)$ has as its ordered columns the $2n$ labels $(x_j,z_j)$ just listed and $p=(k_1,\ldots,k_{2n})\in(\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z)^{2n}$. The phase vector retains the exact mod-$4$ generator-image phases; it is not discarded with the binary labels. The columns define the unique linear map on $V_n$ taking the ordered standard basis to those columns. Only pairs arising from a Clifford are called Clifford tableaux; arbitrary binary matrices and phase vectors need not be valid. A scalar global phase on $U$ does not change its tableau.

references.title: Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: Fix generator and wire order explicitly.
Keep exact mod-4 phases distinct from the binary label block.
items.axiom_use: None; the tableau records finitely many exact generator images.

items.title: Clifford circuits lift binary symplectic transvections
items.statement: For every nonzero $v=(x,z)\in V_n$, the transvection $\tau_v(w)=w+\omega(w,v)v$ is induced on binary Pauli labels by an explicit Clifford circuit made from local $H$, $S$, $S^*$, CNOT, and wire swaps. Its mod-$4$ phase lift is computed by applying the exact gate update rules in sequence; no phase coordinate is suppressed.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

proof_obligations: construct a local Clifford circuit sending any nonzero Hermitian Pauli to Z_1
conjugate the S_1 lift and track every phase update
items.axiom_use: None; each circuit and reduction is finite and uses no choice principle.

items.title: Symplectic transvections generate the binary symplectic group
items.statement: Let $V$ be any finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb F_2$ with a nondegenerate alternating form $\omega$, and let $\dim V=2n$. Call an invertible linear map $T:V\to V$ **symplectic** when $\omega(Tu,Tw)=\omega(u,w)$ for all $u,w\in V$. For each $v\in V$, define the transvection $\tau_v(w)=w+\omega(w,v)v$. Every symplectic map is a finite composition of these transvections. The form on $V_n$ from [[def-qc-binary-symplectic-form]] is the application needed here. This is a choice-free finite-dimensional reduction.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

proof_obligations: prove transvections are symplectic involutions
prove transitivity on nonzero vectors and the stabilizer reduction
induct on n using the orthogonal complement
items.axiom_use: None; the reduction uses finite-dimensional linear algebra and finite induction, with no choice principle.

items.title: Pauli commutator is symplectic pairing
items.statement:
For $a=(x,z)$ and $b=(x',z')$ in $V_n$ and any phases $k,k'$, 

$$P(k,x,z)P(k',x',z')=(-1)^{\omega(a,b)}P(k',x',z')P(k,x,z).$$

Thus the Pauli operators commute exactly when their labels are symplectically orthogonal.

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7
M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits

proof_obligations: compare the two exact phase-aware products; binary labels alone do not prove signed group identities.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof compares the finite phase-aware products.

items.title: Clifford induces symplectic map
items.statement: For each $U\in\mathcal C_n$, conjugation induces an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-linear map $S_U:V_n\to V_n$ satisfying $\omega(S_Ua,S_Ub)=\omega(a,b)$ for all $a,b\in V_n$. Thus $S_U$ is symplectic. The assignment respects multiplication: $S_{UV}=S_U\circ S_V$ for all $U,V\in\mathcal C_n$.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7

proof_obligations: show conjugation descends through the scalar quotient and is invertible
derive linearity and preservation of the commutator pairing
items.axiom_use: None; conjugation and the quotient action use finite-dimensional algebra only.

items.title: Clifford to binary symplectic action is surjective
items.statement: For every $n\ge1$, write $\operatorname{Sp}(V_n,\omega)$ for the group of invertible $\mathbb F_2$-linear maps $T:V_n\to V_n$ satisfying $\omega(Ta,Tb)=\omega(a,b)$ for all $a,b$. For every $T\in\operatorname{Sp}(V_n,\omega)$ there is a Clifford circuit $U$ made from Hadamard gates $H$, phase gates $S,S^*$, CNOT, and wire swaps whose induced action on binary Pauli labels is $T$. Since the phase gate satisfies $S^*=S^3$, this group is also generated by $H$, $S$, CNOT, and swaps. Hence the conjugation homomorphism from the Clifford normalizer to $\operatorname{Sp}(V_n,\omega)$ is onto. The proof uses finite transvection reduction and exact mod-$4$ phase updates at every gate.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: prove transvection generation by finite symplectic reduction
give an explicit Clifford circuit lifting each transvection and track mod-4 phases
items.axiom_use: None; the decomposition and synthesis use finite induction, not arbitrary choice.

proposed_after_items.statement: The map $\pi:\mathcal P_n\to V_n$, $P(k,x,z)\mapsto(x,z)$, is a surjective group homomorphism with kernel exactly $Z_n$. Therefore the quotient map in [[def-qc-binary-pauli-label-and-quotient]] is an isomorphism $\mathcal P_n/Z_n\cong (V_n,+)$, and $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}V_n=2n$. No phase or label ambiguity occurs, including when $n=1$.

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7
M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

proof_obligations: Prove exact Pauli label uniqueness up to scalar using ordered computational-basis vectors.
Use the phase-aware multiplication law to prove homomorphism, kernel, surjectivity, and dimension, including n=1.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; surjectivity, injectivity, and dimension use explicit finite coordinates.

proposed_after_items.title: Phase-aware binary Clifford tableau
proposed_after_items.statement:
Fix the generator order $X_1,\ldots,X_n,Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$ and label order $(x,z)$, with wire indices as in [[def-qc-phase-aware-n-qubit-pauli-group]]. For an actual Clifford unitary $U\in\mathcal C_n$, write each exact generator image uniquely as

$$UX_jU^*=P(k_j,x_j,z_j),\qquad UZ_jU^*=P(k_{n+j},x_{n+j},z_{n+j}).$$

Its **phase-aware binary Clifford tableau** is the pair $(S,p)$, where $S\in M_{2n}(\mathbb F_2)$ has as its ordered columns the $2n$ labels $(x_j,z_j)$ just listed and $p=(k_1,\ldots,k_{2n})\in(\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z)^{2n}$. The phase vector retains the exact mod-$4$ generator-image phases; it is not discarded with the binary labels. The columns define the unique linear map on $V_n$ taking the ordered standard basis to those columns. Only pairs arising from a Clifford are called Clifford tableaux; arbitrary binary matrices and phase vectors need not be valid. A scalar global phase on $U$ does not change its tableau.

references.title: Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: Fix generator and wire order explicitly.
Keep exact mod-4 phases distinct from the binary label block.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; the tableau records finitely many exact generator images.

proposed_after_items.title: Clifford circuits lift binary symplectic transvections
proposed_after_items.statement: For every nonzero $v=(x,z)\in V_n$, the transvection $\tau_v(w)=w+\omega(w,v)v$ is induced on binary Pauli labels by an explicit Clifford circuit made from local $H$, $S$, $S^*$, CNOT, and wire swaps. Its mod-$4$ phase lift is computed by applying the exact gate update rules in sequence; no phase coordinate is suppressed.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

proof_obligations: construct a local Clifford circuit sending any nonzero Hermitian Pauli to Z_1
conjugate the S_1 lift and track every phase update
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; each circuit and reduction is finite and uses no choice principle.

proposed_after_items.title: Symplectic transvections generate the binary symplectic group
proposed_after_items.statement: Let $V$ be any finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb F_2$ with a nondegenerate alternating form $\omega$, and let $\dim V=2n$. Call an invertible linear map $T:V\to V$ **symplectic** when $\omega(Tu,Tw)=\omega(u,w)$ for all $u,w\in V$. For each $v\in V$, define the transvection $\tau_v(w)=w+\omega(w,v)v$. Every symplectic map is a finite composition of these transvections. The form on $V_n$ from [[def-qc-binary-symplectic-form]] is the application needed here. This is a choice-free finite-dimensional reduction.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

proof_obligations: prove transvections are symplectic involutions
prove transitivity on nonzero vectors and the stabilizer reduction
induct on n using the orthogonal complement
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; the reduction uses finite-dimensional linear algebra and finite induction, with no choice principle.

proposed_after_items.title: Pauli commutator is symplectic pairing
proposed_after_items.statement:
For $a=(x,z)$ and $b=(x',z')$ in $V_n$ and any phases $k,k'$, 

$$P(k,x,z)P(k',x',z')=(-1)^{\omega(a,b)}P(k',x',z')P(k,x,z).$$

Thus the Pauli operators commute exactly when their labels are symplectically orthogonal.

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7
M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits

proof_obligations: compare the two exact phase-aware products; binary labels alone do not prove signed group identities.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; the proof compares the finite phase-aware products.

proposed_after_items.title: Clifford induces symplectic map
proposed_after_items.statement: For each $U\in\mathcal C_n$, conjugation induces an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-linear map $S_U:V_n\to V_n$ satisfying $\omega(S_Ua,S_Ub)=\omega(a,b)$ for all $a,b\in V_n$. Thus $S_U$ is symplectic. The assignment respects multiplication: $S_{UV}=S_U\circ S_V$ for all $U,V\in\mathcal C_n$.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7

proof_obligations: show conjugation descends through the scalar quotient and is invertible
derive linearity and preservation of the commutator pairing
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; conjugation and the quotient action use finite-dimensional algebra only.

proposed_after_items.title: Clifford to binary symplectic action is surjective
proposed_after_items.statement: For every $n\ge1$, write $\operatorname{Sp}(V_n,\omega)$ for the group of invertible $\mathbb F_2$-linear maps $T:V_n\to V_n$ satisfying $\omega(Ta,Tb)=\omega(a,b)$ for all $a,b$. For every $T\in\operatorname{Sp}(V_n,\omega)$ there is a Clifford circuit $U$ made from Hadamard gates $H$, phase gates $S,S^*$, CNOT, and wire swaps whose induced action on binary Pauli labels is $T$. Since the phase gate satisfies $S^*=S^3$, this group is also generated by $H$, $S$, CNOT, and swaps. Hence the conjugation homomorphism from the Clifford normalizer to $\operatorname{Sp}(V_n,\omega)$ is onto. The proof uses finite transvection reduction and exact mod-$4$ phase updates at every gate.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: prove transvection generation by finite symplectic reduction
give an explicit Clifford circuit lifting each transvection and track mod-4 phases

items.title: Pauli measurement branch semantics
items.statement:
Let $H_n=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$ be an ordered $n$-qubit register, let
$\rho\in M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$ be a density operator, and let $M\in M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$
be a Hermitian Pauli observable with $M^2=I$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ define

$$P_b:=\frac{I+(-1)^bM}{2},\qquad p_b:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b),\qquad \mathcal I_b(\rho):=P_b\rho P_b.$$

The outcome $b$ has probability $p_b$. Its conditional density operator is
$\rho_b:=\mathcal I_b(\rho)/p_b$ when $p_b>0$; it is $\bot$ (no assigned
conditional density operator) when $p_b=0$.
The branch map $\mathcal I_b$ is the projective measurement instrument for the
$(-1)^b$ eigenspace of $M$. A non-Hermitian phase-aware Pauli is outside this
definition. For $n\ge1$, Hermiticity of $P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z$ means
$k\equiv x\cdot z\pmod2$; in particular $Y=iXZ$ is admitted. For $n=0$,
the admitted observables are $I_{H_0}$ and $-I_{H_0}$.

The hypotheses and meanings of density operator, Pauli observable, projective
measurement, POVM outcome law, and instrument are the cited suppliers. The
local projector calculation is [[lem-qc-pauli-measurement-projectors]].

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, §20.2
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: complementary orthogonal projectors and total probability one.

items.title: Pauli measurement projectors and total probability
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let
$\rho$ be a density operator on $H$, and let $M$ be a Hermitian Pauli
observable on $H$ with $M^2=I_H$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ set

$$P_b:=\frac{I_H+(-1)^bM}{2},\qquad p_b:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b).$$

Then $P_0,P_1$ are complementary orthogonal projections and
$p_0,p_1\ge0$, with $p_0+p_1=1$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, §20.2
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: Verify complementary orthogonal projectors, positive branch weights, and total probability one.

items.title: A maximal stabilizer label space is self-dual
items.statement:
Let $V=\mathbb F_2^{2n}$ have the standard symplectic form
$\omega((x,z),(x',z'))=x\cdot z'+z\cdot x'$. If $L\le V$ is isotropic and
$r=\dim L$, then

$$\dim L^\perp=2n-r.$$

Consequently $r\le n$, and if $r=n$ then

$$L^\perp:=\{v\in V:\omega(v,\ell)=0\text{ for every }\ell\in L\}=L.$$

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, §20.1
Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits, §II

proof_obligations: Prove the annihilator dimension formula by nondegeneracy and rank-nullity, including the zero subspace.

items.title: Stabilizer subgroup
items.statement:
For an ordered register of $n$ qubits, a **stabilizer subgroup** is an abelian
subgroup $S$ of the Hermitian $n$-qubit Pauli operators such that
$-I\notin S$. The binary label of a phase-aware Pauli $P(k,x,z)$ is
$(x,z)\in\mathbb F_2^{2n}$. Define the **rank** of $S$ by

$$\operatorname{rank}(S):=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}\operatorname{span} \{(x,z):P(k,x,z)\in S\}.$$

The binary label convention and commutation form are supplied by the cited
Pauli items. [[lem-qc-stabilizer-subgroup-label-space-and-order]] proves that
this label span is isotropic, its dimension is independent of any generating
set, and $|S|=2^{\operatorname{rank}(S)}$. Matrix multiplication gives the
phase-aware Pauli group operation by
[[thm-qc-pauli-product-and-adjoint]]. For $n=0$, the Pauli group is the
empty-register convention of [[def-qc-pauli-group-on-zero-qubits]].

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, §20.1
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: show the span is isotropic and rank is independent of generating set.

Reuses existing root supplier def-dimension from linear-independence-bases-and-dimension; no duplicate QC carrier is proposed.

items.title: Pauli projectors define a finite measurement instrument
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let
$M$ be a Hermitian Pauli observable on $H$ with $M^2=I_H$. Put
$P_b=(I_H+(-1)^bM)/2$ and define
$\mathcal I_b(X)=P_bXP_b$ for $b\in\{0,1\}$. Then the maps
$(\mathcal I_0,\mathcal I_1)$ form a finite instrument from $H$ to $H$. For
every density operator $\rho$ on $H$, the outcome weight of branch $b$ is
$\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b)$.

references.title: John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14 §14.1
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, §20.2

proof_obligations: Verify complete positivity of every ancilla amplification and trace preservation of the summed branches.

items.title: Positive-probability Pauli branches are density operators
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let
$\rho$ be a density operator on $H$, and let $M$ be a Hermitian Pauli
observable on $H$ with $M^2=I_H$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ put
$P_b=(I_H+(-1)^bM)/2$ and $p_b=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b)$. If $p_b>0$,
then the normalized branch

$$\rho_b:=\frac{P_b\rho P_b}{p_b}$$

is a density operator.

references.title: John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14 §14.1
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, §20.2

proof_obligations: Prove that a positive-probability branch map divided by its weight is nonnegative and trace one.

items.title: Zero-probability Pauli measurement branch
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let
$\rho$ be a density operator on $H$, and let $M$ be a Hermitian Pauli
observable on $H$ with $M^2=I_H$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ put
$P_b=(I_H+(-1)^bM)/2$ and $p_b=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b)$. If $p_b=0$,
then $P_b\rho P_b=0$. The outcome has probability zero and, under the
conditional-state convention, has no normalized conditional state.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, §20.3
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: derive P_bρP_b=0 from positivity and zero trace.

items.title: Finite adaptive Pauli-measurement circuit tree
items.statement:
Fix an ordered $n$-qubit register and a finite gate alphabet as in
[[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. A **finite adaptive
Pauli-measurement circuit tree** is a finite rooted tree whose leaves are
terminal and whose nonterminal nodes are of one of these two types:

1. A gate node is labelled by a gate occurrence on the ordered register and
   has one successor. Its state update is conjugation by the global unitary
   assigned to that occurrence by
   [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]].
2. A measurement node is labelled by a Hermitian Pauli observable $M$ and has
   two outgoing edges labelled $b=0,1$. On input density operator $\rho$,
   edge $b$ has weight $p_b=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b)$ and unnormalized
   output $P_b\rho P_b$, where $P_b=(I+(-1)^bM)/2$ as in
   [[def-qc-pauli-measurement-branch-semantics]]. Its child state is
   $P_b\rho P_b/p_b$ only if $p_b>0$; an edge of weight zero is impossible
   and has no conditional state.

The observed measurement transcript is the ordered list of measurement-edge
labels on a root-to-leaf path. The tree itself specifies every later
instruction from that observed history, so its classical control is
deterministic. A path whose edges all have positive weights has probability
equal to their product. A path passing through a zero-weight edge has
probability zero, and its descendants are not evaluated because no
conditional state is assigned. A leaf outputs its terminal state; a ray is
assigned only on a positive-probability path whose input and gate/measurement
updates remain pure.

The complementary-projector and total-probability facts for each measurement
node are supplied by [[lem-qc-pauli-measurement-projectors]]. This definition
does not identify an instrument with a POVM or require uniqueness of such a
POVM.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, §20.3
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14 §14.1

items.title: Stabilizer state
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a rank-$n$ stabilizer subgroup on an ordered $n$-qubit register
$H_n=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$. A **pure stabilizer state** is the unique ray
in the common $+1$ fixed space

$$\mathcal C(S):=\{\psi\in H_n:g\psi=\psi\text{ for every }g\in S\}.$$

The cited projector-rank theorem proves that this common space is nonzero and
one-dimensional, so the ray is well defined. A normalized representative may
be used for probabilities, but the state itself is the ray, not a chosen
vector.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, §20.1
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: establish the common fixed space is nonzero and one-dimensional.

items.title: Stabilizer labels form an isotropic space of the same rank
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a stabilizer subgroup on $n\ge0$ qubits and let
$\lambda(P(k,x,z))=(x,z)$. Then $\lambda|_S$ is injective, its image $L$ is an
isotropic $\mathbb F_2$-subspace, the rank $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}L$ depends only
on $S$ and not on a generating list, and
$|S|=2^{\dim_{\mathbb F_2}L}$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, §20.1
Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits, §II

proof_obligations: Prove label injectivity, isotropy, rank independence, and the finite subgroup cardinality.

items.title: Stabilizer average is the fixed-space projector
items.statement:
For a stabilizer subgroup $S$ on $n$ qubits, the finite operator average

$$\Pi_S:=\frac{1}{|S|}\sum_{g\in S}g$$

is self-adjoint and idempotent, and its image is exactly the common $+1$ fixed
space $\mathcal C(S)$. If this image is the span of a unit vector $\psi$, then
$\Pi_S=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ under the root-linear-first Dirac convention.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, §20.3
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14 §14.3

proof_obligations: use group closure and Hermiticity, not simultaneous diagonalization by assertion.
