before_page.title: Finite Abelian Fourier Analysis

items.title: Dual group of a finite abelian group
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group ([[def-group]]) written additively. Its set of additive characters is
$$\widehat G:=\{\chi:G\to\mathbb C^{\times}:\chi(x+y)=\chi(x)\chi(y)\text{ for all }x,y\in G\},$$
where an additive character is the group homomorphism of [[def-additive-character-of-a-finite-abelian-group]]. For $\chi,\psi\in\widehat G$, define their pointwise product by $(\chi\psi)(x):=\chi(x)\psi(x)$. The constant-one function is denoted $1$, and the pointwise inverse is $\chi^{-1}(x):=\chi(x)^{-1}$.

This specifies a set and operations. The later theorem `thm-qa-finite-abelian-character-dual-is-finite-abelian-group` proves that these operations make $\widehat G$ a finite abelian group; no isomorphism $G\cong\widehat G$ is part of this definition.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Unnormalized convolution on a finite abelian group
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group ([[def-group]]), written additively, and let $f,g\in\mathbb C^G$ be functions ([[def-function-space]]). Their (unnormalized) convolution is the function
$$ (f*g)(z):=\sum_{x\in G}f(x)g(z-x),\qquad z\in G. $$
The sum is the finite sum of [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]] in the additive monoid of $\mathbb C$; it is independent of any enumeration of $G$. No factor of $|G|^{-1}$ is included. The Fourier convolution theorem below proves the resulting normalization factor.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Values of characters of finite groups have modulus one
items.statement: If $G$ is a finite abelian group, $\chi:G\to\mathbb C^{\times}$ is an additive character, and $x\in G$, then $|\chi(x)|=1$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: A cyclic group of order n has exactly n additive characters
items.statement: Write $C_n=\langle g\rangle$ additively, so $jg$ denotes the sum of $j$ copies of $g$ and $ng=0$. If $C_n$ has order $n\ge1$, then its set $\widehat{C_n}$ of additive characters has cardinality $n$. Each character is uniquely determined by $\chi(g)$, and the possible values are exactly the $n$ distinct complex $n$th roots of unity. For each such root $z$, the corresponding character is $\chi_z(jg)=z^j$ for every $j\in\mathbb Z$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Characters of a finite product factor coordinatewise
items.statement:
Let $G_1,\ldots,G_r$ be finite abelian groups and let $P=G_1\times\cdots\times G_r$ be their recursively parenthesized external direct product. By convention, $P$ is the trivial group when $r=0$. Restriction to the coordinate factors gives a bijection
$$\widehat P\longrightarrow\widehat{G_1}\times\cdots\times\widehat{G_r}.$$
Its inverse sends $(\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r)$ to $\chi(g_1,\ldots,g_r)=\prod_{i=1}^r\chi_i(g_i)$. For $r=0$, both sides are singletons.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Character annihilator of a subgroup
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with character dual $\widehat G$ ([[def-qa-finite-abelian-character-dual]]). For a subgroup $H\le G$ ([[def-subgroup]]), define its character annihilator by
$$H^{\perp}:=\{\chi\in\widehat G:\chi(h)=1\text{ for every }h\in H\}.$$
For any subset $K\subseteq\widehat G$ (in particular, for any subgroup once $\widehat G$ has been proved to be a group), define
$$K^{\perp}:=\{g\in G:\chi(g)=1\text{ for every }\chi\in K\}.$$
The pairing is evaluation, and the same convention is used in both directions. `lem-qa-finite-abelian-annihilators-are-subgroups` proves that these sets are subgroups when the input is a subgroup.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: A finite abelian group and its character dual have equal order
items.statement: If $G$ is a finite abelian group with invariant-factor decomposition $G\cong C_{n_1}\times\cdots\times C_{n_r}$, then $|\widehat G|=\prod_i n_i=|G|$. The empty product is allowed: it represents the trivial group and has value $1$. This is a finite-set cardinality assertion; it does not choose an isomorphism $G\cong\widehat G$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Pointwise character dual is a finite abelian group
items.statement: For a finite abelian group $G$, the pointwise product, constant-one identity and pointwise inverse on $\widehat G$ make it a finite abelian group. Its order is $|\widehat G|=|G|$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Dual-index character orthogonality
items.statement:
For a finite abelian group $G$ and $x,y\in G$,
$$\sum_{\chi\in\widehat G}\chi(x)\overline{\chi(y)}=\begin{cases}|G|,&x=y,\\0,&x\ne y.\end{cases}$$
This is orthogonality of the columns indexed by group elements. It is proved from cyclic root sums and is not inferred from row orthogonality.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Normalized Fourier transform on a finite abelian group
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and $\widehat G$ its character dual ([[def-qa-finite-abelian-character-dual]]), which is finite with $|\widehat G|=|G|$ ([[thm-qa-finite-abelian-dual-has-same-cardinality]]). Put $N:=|G|$ and $N_{\mathbb R}:=\iota_{\mathbb R}(N)$ its canonical real image ([[def-order-in-a-group]], [[def-canonical-natural]]). Since $G$ contains its identity, $N\ge1$, and hence $N_{\mathbb R}>0$ ([[lem-of-naturals-positive]]). Its rational power $N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}$ is therefore well defined ([[def-rational-power]], [[lem-rational-power-well-defined]]).

For $f\in\mathbb C^G$, define $F_Gf\in\mathbb C^{\widehat G}$ by
$$ (F_Gf)(\chi):=N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in G}f(x)\overline{\chi(x)},\qquad \chi\in\widehat G. $$
Here $\mathbb C^X$ is the space of all functions $X\to\mathbb C$ ([[def-function-space]]) and the sum is the finite sum in $\mathbb C$ ([[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]]). This fixes the negative-character sign and uses the same factor $N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}$ in both directions. Unitarity is proved separately; it is not part of this definition.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Subgroup-annihilator cardinality
items.statement:
For a subgroup $H\le G$ of a finite abelian group, restriction and inflation identify $H^\perp$ with the character dual of $G/H$. Consequently
$$|H^\perp|=|G/H|=[G:H]=\frac{|G|}{|H|},\qquad |H^\perp|\,|H|=|G|.$$
The quotient convention is left cosets, with additive notation.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Annihilators of subgroups are subgroups
items.statement: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. For every subgroup $H\le G$, $H^\perp$ is a subgroup of $\widehat G$. For every subgroup $K\le\widehat G$, $K^\perp$ is a subgroup of $G$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Finite abelian Fourier transform is unitary
items.statement:
Let $N_{\mathbb R}$ be the canonical positive real image of $|G|$ from [[def-qa-normalized-finite-abelian-fourier-transform]]. Define the finite coefficient matrix $U$, with rows indexed by $\widehat G$ and columns by $G$, by
$$U_{\chi,x}=N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}\overline{\chi(x)},\qquad \chi\in\widehat G,\ x\in G.$$
It is square and satisfies $U^*U=I_G$ and $UU^*=I_{\widehat G}$, where $U^*$ is the conjugate transpose and $I_X$ is the identity matrix indexed by $X$, with $(I_X)_{x,y}=1$ when $x=y$ and $0$ otherwise. These two identities are the meaning of “unitary” here.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Fourier transform of unnormalized convolution
items.statement:
For a finite abelian group $G$, $f,g:G\to\mathbb C$, and $\chi\in\widehat G$, put $N_{\mathbb R}:=\iota_{\mathbb R}(|G|)$. With the transform and unnormalized convolution defined above,
$$F_G(f*g)(\chi)=N_{\mathbb R}^{1/2}(F_Gf)(\chi)(F_Gg)(\chi).$$
Thus the factor is $\sqrt{|G|}$, not $1$ or $|G|$, for this pair of conventions.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Finite abelian group is canonically isomorphic to its double dual
items.statement:
For a finite abelian group $G$, give $\widehat G$ its pointwise multiplication. Its dual $\widehat{\widehat G}$ consists of functions $\Phi:\widehat G\to\mathbb C^{\times}$ satisfying $\Phi(\chi\psi)=\Phi(\chi)\Phi(\psi)$. The evaluation map
$$\operatorname{ev}:G\longrightarrow\widehat{\widehat G},\qquad \operatorname{ev}(g)(\chi):=\chi(g),$$
is a group isomorphism. The map itself is canonical; a decomposition into cyclic factors is used only to prove it is injective.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Fourier transform of a subgroup coset indicator
items.statement:
Let $G$ be finite abelian, $H\le G$, and $x_0\in G$. Put $N:=|G|$, $M:=|H|$, and $Q:=|H^\perp|$, which is finite by [[thm-qa-finite-abelian-subgroup-annihilator-cardinality]]. Write $N_{\mathbb R}:=\iota_{\mathbb R}(N)$, $M_{\mathbb R}:=\iota_{\mathbb R}(M)$, and $Q_{\mathbb R}:=\iota_{\mathbb R}(Q)$ for their canonical real images, as in [[def-qa-normalized-finite-abelian-fourier-transform]]. These are positive since $G$ and $H$ contain their identities and $H^\perp$ contains the trivial character, and they are viewed in $\mathbb C$ through its embedded copy of $\mathbb R$. For the indicator $1_{x_0+H}$,
$$F_G1_{x_0+H}(\chi)=\begin{cases}M_{\mathbb R}N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}\overline{\chi(x_0)},&\chi\in H^\perp,\\0,&\chi\notin H^\perp.\end{cases}$$
Consequently, the normalized uniform-coset function $M_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}1_{x_0+H}$ transforms to the function supported on $H^\perp$ with value $M_{\mathbb R}^{1/2}N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}\overline{\chi(x_0)}=Q_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}\overline{\chi(x_0)}$ there. The unnormalized indicator amplitude and normalized-state amplitude are distinct.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Finite abelian Fourier inversion
items.statement:
For every $f:G\to\mathbb C$ and $x\in G$,
$$f(x)=N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}\sum_{\chi\in\widehat G}(F_Gf)(\chi)\chi(x),\qquad N_{\mathbb R}:=\iota_{\mathbb R}(|G|).$$
Thus the inverse uses the positive character rather than its conjugate.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Finite abelian Parseval identity
items.statement:
For $f,g:G\to\mathbb C$,
$$\sum_{\chi\in\widehat G}(F_Gf)(\chi)\overline{(F_Gg)(\chi)}=\sum_{x\in G}f(x)\overline{g(x)}.$$
For a finite set $X$, the counting inner product on $\mathbb C^X$ is $\langle f,g\rangle_X:=\sum_{x\in X}f(x)\overline{g(x)}$; it is linear in the first argument. The displayed identity says this inner product is preserved.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Double annihilator returns the subgroup
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and $H\le G$. Under the canonical evaluation identification $G\cong\widehat{\widehat G}$,
$$(H^\perp)^\perp=H.$$

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

It is square and satisfies $U^*U=I_G$ and $UU^*=I_{\widehat G}$, where $U^*$ is the conjugate transpose and $I_X$ is the identity matrix indexed by $X$, with $(I_X)_{x,y}=1$ when $x=y$ and $0$ otherwise. These two identities are the meaning of “unitary” here.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

proposed_after_items.title: Fourier transform of unnormalized convolution
proposed_after_items.statement:
For a finite abelian group $G$, $f,g:G\to\mathbb C$, and $\chi\in\widehat G$, put $N_{\mathbb R}:=\iota_{\mathbb R}(|G|)$. With the transform and unnormalized convolution defined above,
$$F_G(f*g)(\chi)=N_{\mathbb R}^{1/2}(F_Gf)(\chi)(F_Gg)(\chi).$$
Thus the factor is $\sqrt{|G|}$, not $1$ or $|G|$, for this pair of conventions.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

proposed_after_items.title: Finite abelian group is canonically isomorphic to its double dual
proposed_after_items.statement:
For a finite abelian group $G$, give $\widehat G$ its pointwise multiplication. Its dual $\widehat{\widehat G}$ consists of functions $\Phi:\widehat G\to\mathbb C^{\times}$ satisfying $\Phi(\chi\psi)=\Phi(\chi)\Phi(\psi)$. The evaluation map
$$\operatorname{ev}:G\longrightarrow\widehat{\widehat G},\qquad \operatorname{ev}(g)(\chi):=\chi(g),$$
is a group isomorphism. The map itself is canonical; a decomposition into cyclic factors is used only to prove it is injective.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

proposed_after_items.title: Fourier transform of a subgroup coset indicator
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $G$ be finite abelian, $H\le G$, and $x_0\in G$. Put $N:=|G|$, $M:=|H|$, and $Q:=|H^\perp|$, which is finite by [[thm-qa-finite-abelian-subgroup-annihilator-cardinality]]. Write $N_{\mathbb R}:=\iota_{\mathbb R}(N)$, $M_{\mathbb R}:=\iota_{\mathbb R}(M)$, and $Q_{\mathbb R}:=\iota_{\mathbb R}(Q)$ for their canonical real images, as in [[def-qa-normalized-finite-abelian-fourier-transform]]. These are positive since $G$ and $H$ contain their identities and $H^\perp$ contains the trivial character, and they are viewed in $\mathbb C$ through its embedded copy of $\mathbb R$. For the indicator $1_{x_0+H}$,
$$F_G1_{x_0+H}(\chi)=\begin{cases}M_{\mathbb R}N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}\overline{\chi(x_0)},&\chi\in H^\perp,\\0,&\chi\notin H^\perp.\end{cases}$$
Consequently, the normalized uniform-coset function $M_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}1_{x_0+H}$ transforms to the function supported on $H^\perp$ with value $M_{\mathbb R}^{1/2}N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}\overline{\chi(x_0)}=Q_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}\overline{\chi(x_0)}$ there. The unnormalized indicator amplitude and normalized-state amplitude are distinct.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

proposed_after_items.title: Finite abelian Fourier inversion
proposed_after_items.statement:
For every $f:G\to\mathbb C$ and $x\in G$,
$$f(x)=N_{\mathbb R}^{-1/2}\sum_{\chi\in\widehat G}(F_Gf)(\chi)\chi(x),\qquad N_{\mathbb R}:=\iota_{\mathbb R}(|G|).$$
Thus the inverse uses the positive character rather than its conjugate.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

proposed_after_items.title: Finite abelian Parseval identity
proposed_after_items.statement:
For $f,g:G\to\mathbb C$,
$$\sum_{\chi\in\widehat G}(F_Gf)(\chi)\overline{(F_Gg)(\chi)}=\sum_{x\in G}f(x)\overline{g(x)}.$$
For a finite set $X$, the counting inner product on $\mathbb C^X$ is $\langle f,g\rangle_X:=\sum_{x\in X}f(x)\overline{g(x)}$; it is linear in the first argument. The displayed identity says this inner product is preserved.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

proposed_after_items.title: Double annihilator returns the subgroup
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and $H\le G$. Under the canonical evaluation identification $G\cong\widehat{\widehat G}$,
$$(H^\perp)^\perp=H.$$

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, version 6
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
John Preskill, Quantum Information, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms

statement.before:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, $U:H\to H$ a unitary, and $\psi\in H$ a unit vector with a promised phase $\theta\in[0,1)$ such that
$$U\psi=\exp(2\pi i\theta)\psi.$$
For an integer $m\ge1$, let $Q=2^m$. The phase register is $(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes m}$ with ordered computational basis indexed big-endian by
$x=\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}b_k2^{m-1-k}$, where $b_k\in\{0,1\}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]]).
Thus the wire of weight $2^j$ is $q_{m-1-j}$.

There are distinct forward-access options:

1. **Controlled-power access.** The model explicitly supplies one controlled $U^{2^j}$ operation for each $j=0,\ldots,m-1$. Each use is counted as one controlled-power query; an implementation's ordinary gate cost is recorded separately.
2. **Single controlled-unitary access.** The model supplies calls to $C(U)=\operatorname{diag}(I_H,U)$ in the control-first order of [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]]. A controlled $U^{2^j}$ may be implemented by $2^j$ sequential calls to $C(U)$; those calls are charged individually.

Optional **controlled inverse-power access** is a separate capability that explicitly supplies $C(U^{-2^j})$ for each required $j$. It is not implied by either forward option. It is needed only by a consuming procedure that reverses the controlled-power portion of a coherent QPE prefix. Reversing the inverse-QFT gate list does not use $U^{-1}$.

The finite ordered-register, gate, and measurement interpretations are those of [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The definition is an access-model promise: it does not assert that the supplied controlled powers have an efficient construction or that $\theta$ has an exact $m$-bit expansion.

items.title: Finite geometric sum for phase-estimation amplitudes
items.statement:
For $n\in\mathbb N$ and $z\in\mathbb C$, define
$$S_n(z):=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}z^j,$$
with the empty sum $S_0(z)=0$. Then
$$S_n(z)=\begin{cases}\iota_{\mathbb C}(n),&z=1,\\[2pt](1-z^n)/(1-z),&z\ne1,\end{cases}$$
where $\iota_{\mathbb C}$ is the canonical natural embedding of $\mathbb N$ into $\mathbb C$.

For $Q=2^m$, $\theta\in[0,1)$, and integer $y$, setting
$z=\exp(2\pi i(\theta-y/Q))$ gives
$z^Q=\exp(2\pi iQ\theta)$; moreover $z=1$ exactly when
$Q\theta-y\in Q\mathbb Z$.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite sums, recursion, and field laws.

items.title: Sine chord and linear bounds
items.statement:
For $0\le u\le1/2$ and $v\ge0$,
$$\sin(\pi u)\ge2u,\qquad \sin(v)\le v.$$
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses calculus on compact real intervals and no choice.

items.title: Circular phase distance modulo one
items.statement:
For a real $x\in[-1,1]$, define its circular distance to the nearest integer by
$$d_{\mathbb T}(x):=\min\{|x|,\,1-|x|\}.$$
Here $|x|$ is the real absolute value and $\min$ is the minimum of the displayed finite set ([[def-real-order]], [[def-max-min]]); existence of this finite minimum follows from [[lem-finite-set-has-max]]. Both entries lie in $[0,1]$, so the value lies in $[0,1/2]$. If $|x|\le1/2$, the nearest integer is $0$; if $x>1/2$, it is $1$; if $x<-1/2$, it is $-1$, so the formula is the distance to the nearest integer. For phases $\theta,\phi\in[0,1)$, their circular distance is $d_{\mathbb T}(\theta-\phi)$; the difference belongs to $(-1,1)$, the stated domain.
items.axiom_use: None; this is a finite minimum of two real numbers.

items.title: Quantum phase estimation
items.statement:
**Input.** An integer $m\ge1$; an $m$-qubit phase register; a finite-dimensional system register $H$; a unitary $U:H\to H$; a unit eigenvector $\psi$ with promised phase $\theta\in[0,1)$; and one of the forward access capabilities in [[def-qa-eigenphase-estimation-model]].

**Output.** A classical label $y\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$ and its phase estimate $y/Q$, where $Q=2^m$.

**Instructions.**

1. Initialize the phase register in $|0^m\rangle$ and the system register in $\psi$.
2. Apply the Hadamard $H=(X+Z)/\sqrt2$ of [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]] to each phase wire. This prepares $Q^{-1/2}\sum_{x=0}^{Q-1}|x\rangle\otimes\psi$ in the declared big-endian order.
3. For $j=0,\ldots,m-1$, apply the supplied controlled $U^{2^j}$ to control wire $q_{m-1-j}$ and the system. Under single controlled-unitary access, implement that operation with $2^j$ sequential calls to $C(U)$, as specified by the access model.
4. Apply the inverse of the positive-sign exact binary QFT circuit of [[def-qa-cyclic-quantum-fourier-transform]] and [[thm-qa-exact-binary-qft-circuit-correct]]. Construct it by reversing the chronological gate list and replacing each gate by its adjoint, including the final swaps and negating controlled-phase angles.
5. Perform the computational-basis projective measurement on the phase register. Its specified Lüders instrument has branch map $Z\mapsto (|y\rangle\langle y|\otimes I_H)Z(|y\rangle\langle y|\otimes I_H)$ for each label $y$ ([[def-qc-projective-measurement]], [[def-qc-instrument-and-conditional-state]]). Output the observed label $y$ and the ratio $y/Q$.

The inverse in step 4 is the inverse QFT, not $U^{-1}$; a forward QPE run makes no controlled inverse-unitary query. The coherent prefix is the circuit through step 4 before measurement. A consumer that coherently uncomputes this prefix needs the separate controlled inverse-power capability from [[def-qa-eigenphase-estimation-model]].
items.axiom_use: None; the procedure uses finite registers and supplied unitary access.

items.title: Phase-estimation finite outcome law
items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$, $Q=2^m$, and let the input be an eigenvector with
$U\psi=\exp(2\pi i\theta)\psi$, where $\theta\in[0,1)$.
For each $y\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$, the probability of measuring $y$ in the algorithm of [[alg-qa-quantum-phase-estimation]] is
$$P_\theta(y)=Q^{-2}\left|\sum_{j=0}^{Q-1}\exp\!\left(2\pi i j(\theta-y/Q)\right)\right|^2.$$
Thus the finite outcome kernel is defined at every phase, including $Q\theta\in\mathbb Z$; no quotient with a zero denominator is needed in this formula.
items.axiom_use: None; the normalization check is a finite sum and the measurement law is finite-dimensional.

items.title: Phase-estimation query and gate costs
items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$ and $Q=2^m$. Count costs in the ideal continuous-rotation submodel, where each exact controlled phase used by the binary QFT is one gate. If the controlled powers $C(U^{2^j})$, $0\le j<m$, are supplied as one query each, one run uses exactly $m$ controlled-power queries. If the only oracle is $C(U)$, the repeated implementation uses exactly $Q-1$ controlled-$U$ queries. If the supplied controlled-power circuits have ordinary gate counts $C_j$, the unitary gate count after the eigenstate input is provided is
$$\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}C_j+2m+\frac{m(m-1)}2+\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor.$$
The final register measurement reads $m$ bits and is not included in this unitary gate count. No cost-free power construction, fixed finite gate alphabet, uniform family, or state-preparation bound is asserted.
items.axiom_use: None; the counts are finite sums of the explicitly supplied operations.

items.title: Nearest-grid probability in phase estimation
items.statement:
For every $m\ge1$, $Q=2^m$, and $\theta\in[0,1)$, a nearest grid label $y\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$, minimizing $d_{\mathbb T}(\theta-y/Q)$, exists. Every nearest label satisfies
$$P_\theta(y)\ge\frac4{\pi^2}.$$
In particular, this holds at ties between adjacent labels and at the wrap-around between $Q-1$ and $0$.
items.axiom_use: None; the nearest label is constructed using the integer-part lemma.

items.title: Circular-distance tail bound in phase estimation
items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$, $Q=2^m$, $\theta\in[0,1)$, $\eta\in\mathbb R$, and
$K=\lfloor Q\eta\rfloor\ge2$. With
$d_{\mathbb T}(\theta-y/Q)$ as in [[def-qa-circular-phase-distance]],
$$\Pr_{y\sim P_\theta}\!\left[d_{\mathbb T}(\theta-y/Q)\ge\eta\right]\le\frac1{2(K-1)}.$$
items.axiom_use: None; the annulus count and series estimate are finite.

items.title: Exact phase recovery on the QPE grid
items.statement: Let $m\ge1$, $Q=2^m$, and $\theta\in[0,1)$. If $Q\theta=t\in\mathbb Z$, then $t\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$, phase estimation returns $y=t$ with probability $1$, and every other output has probability $0$.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite cyclic-character orthogonality.

items.title: Phase estimation on a superposition of eigenspaces
items.statement:
Let $U$ be a unitary on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$. Let $\Theta\subset[0,1)$ be its finite set of distinct eigenphases, and let $\Pi_\theta$ denote the orthogonal projection onto the full eigenspace for eigenvalue $\exp(2\pi i\theta)$; degeneracies are grouped in one projection. For $Q=2^m$, $m\ge1$, define
$$a_y(\theta):=Q^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{Q-1}\exp(2\pi ij(\theta-y/Q)),\qquad K_y:=\sum_{\theta\in\Theta}a_y(\theta)\Pi_\theta.$$
For a unit input $\psi=\sum_{\theta\in\Theta}\Pi_\theta\psi$, the unnormalized branch vector is $K_y\psi$ and
$$p_y=\|K_y\psi\|^2=\sum_{\theta\in\Theta}|a_y(\theta)|^2\|\Pi_\theta\psi\|^2.$$
If $p_y>0$, the conditional vector is $K_y\psi/\sqrt{p_y}$; if $p_y=0$, no conditional vector is assigned. The outcome law is an eigenspace-weighted mixture, while the conditional branch can retain coherent cross terms between distinct eigenspaces.

After discarding the phase register, the induced system instrument has branch maps $\mathcal I_y(X)=K_yXK_y^\dagger$ for operators $X$ on $H$. More generally, for a density operator $\rho$ on $H\otimes R$, where $R$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional reference space, the unnormalized reference-preserving branch after measuring and discarding the phase register is
$$\mathcal I_y^{(R)}(\rho)=(K_y\otimes I_R)\rho(K_y^\dagger\otimes I_R).$$
Its probability is $\operatorname{tr}\mathcal I_y^{(R)}(\rho)$, and the conditional state is $\mathcal I_y^{(R)}(\rho)/\operatorname{tr}\mathcal I_y^{(R)}(\rho)$ exactly when that probability is positive. With $w_\theta=\operatorname{tr}((\Pi_\theta\otimes I_R)\rho)$, the reference outcome law is $p_y=\sum_{\theta\in\Theta}|a_y(\theta)|^2w_\theta$, where $w_\theta\ge0$ and $\sum_\theta w_\theta=1$. If every eigenphase is on the $Q$-grid, then $K_y=\Pi_{y/Q}$ when $y/Q\in\Theta$ and $K_y=0$ otherwise, so the instrument branch is $X\mapsto K_yXK_y^\dagger$. If any eigenphase is off-grid, its nonzero coefficient has modulus less than one in every $K_y$, so $K_y^\dagger K_y$ is not a projection and the induced instrument is not the spectral projection instrument.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite-dimensional spectral decomposition and finite sums.

items.title: Phase-estimation nearest-grid and tail bounds
items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$, $Q=2^m$, and $\theta\in[0,1)$. Every nearest grid label $y$ has $P_\theta(y)\ge4/\pi^2$. For any $\eta\in\mathbb R$ with $K=\lfloor Q\eta\rfloor\ge2$,
$$\Pr_{y\sim P_\theta}\!\left[d_{\mathbb T}(\theta-y/Q)\ge\eta\right]\le\frac1{2(K-1)}.$$
If $Q\theta$ is an integer $t$, then $P_\theta(t)=1$ and all other labels have probability $0$.
items.axiom_use: None; this theorem combines finite probability bounds.

proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$, $Q=2^m$, and let the input be an eigenvector with
$U\psi=\exp(2\pi i\theta)\psi$, where $\theta\in[0,1)$.
For each $y\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$, the probability of measuring $y$ in the algorithm of [[alg-qa-quantum-phase-estimation]] is
$$P_\theta(y)=Q^{-2}\left|\sum_{j=0}^{Q-1}\exp\!\left(2\pi i j(\theta-y/Q)\right)\right|^2.$$
Thus the finite outcome kernel is defined at every phase, including $Q\theta\in\mathbb Z$; no quotient with a zero denominator is needed in this formula.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; the normalization check is a finite sum and the measurement law is finite-dimensional.

proposed_after_items.title: Phase-estimation query and gate costs
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$ and $Q=2^m$. Count costs in the ideal continuous-rotation submodel, where each exact controlled phase used by the binary QFT is one gate. If the controlled powers $C(U^{2^j})$, $0\le j<m$, are supplied as one query each, one run uses exactly $m$ controlled-power queries. If the only oracle is $C(U)$, the repeated implementation uses exactly $Q-1$ controlled-$U$ queries. If the supplied controlled-power circuits have ordinary gate counts $C_j$, the unitary gate count after the eigenstate input is provided is
$$\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}C_j+2m+\frac{m(m-1)}2+\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor.$$
The final register measurement reads $m$ bits and is not included in this unitary gate count. No cost-free power construction, fixed finite gate alphabet, uniform family, or state-preparation bound is asserted.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; the counts are finite sums of the explicitly supplied operations.

proposed_after_items.title: Nearest-grid probability in phase estimation
proposed_after_items.statement:
For every $m\ge1$, $Q=2^m$, and $\theta\in[0,1)$, a nearest grid label $y\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$, minimizing $d_{\mathbb T}(\theta-y/Q)$, exists. Every nearest label satisfies
$$P_\theta(y)\ge\frac4{\pi^2}.$$
In particular, this holds at ties between adjacent labels and at the wrap-around between $Q-1$ and $0$.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; the nearest label is constructed using the integer-part lemma.

proposed_after_items.title: Circular-distance tail bound in phase estimation
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$, $Q=2^m$, $\theta\in[0,1)$, $\eta\in\mathbb R$, and
$K=\lfloor Q\eta\rfloor\ge2$. With
$d_{\mathbb T}(\theta-y/Q)$ as in [[def-qa-circular-phase-distance]],
$$\Pr_{y\sim P_\theta}\!\left[d_{\mathbb T}(\theta-y/Q)\ge\eta\right]\le\frac1{2(K-1)}.$$
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; the annulus count and series estimate are finite.

proposed_after_items.title: Exact phase recovery on the QPE grid
proposed_after_items.statement: Let $m\ge1$, $Q=2^m$, and $\theta\in[0,1)$. If $Q\theta=t\in\mathbb Z$, then $t\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$, phase estimation returns $y=t$ with probability $1$, and every other output has probability $0$.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite cyclic-character orthogonality.

proposed_after_items.title: Phase estimation on a superposition of eigenspaces
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $U$ be a unitary on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$. Let $\Theta\subset[0,1)$ be its finite set of distinct eigenphases, and let $\Pi_\theta$ denote the orthogonal projection onto the full eigenspace for eigenvalue $\exp(2\pi i\theta)$; degeneracies are grouped in one projection. For $Q=2^m$, $m\ge1$, define
$$a_y(\theta):=Q^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{Q-1}\exp(2\pi ij(\theta-y/Q)),\qquad K_y:=\sum_{\theta\in\Theta}a_y(\theta)\Pi_\theta.$$
For a unit input $\psi=\sum_{\theta\in\Theta}\Pi_\theta\psi$, the unnormalized branch vector is $K_y\psi$ and
$$p_y=\|K_y\psi\|^2=\sum_{\theta\in\Theta}|a_y(\theta)|^2\|\Pi_\theta\psi\|^2.$$
If $p_y>0$, the conditional vector is $K_y\psi/\sqrt{p_y}$; if $p_y=0$, no conditional vector is assigned. The outcome law is an eigenspace-weighted mixture, while the conditional branch can retain coherent cross terms between distinct eigenspaces.

After discarding the phase register, the induced system instrument has branch maps $\mathcal I_y(X)=K_yXK_y^\dagger$ for operators $X$ on $H$. More generally, for a density operator $\rho$ on $H\otimes R$, where $R$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional reference space, the unnormalized reference-preserving branch after measuring and discarding the phase register is
$$\mathcal I_y^{(R)}(\rho)=(K_y\otimes I_R)\rho(K_y^\dagger\otimes I_R).$$
Its probability is $\operatorname{tr}\mathcal I_y^{(R)}(\rho)$, and the conditional state is $\mathcal I_y^{(R)}(\rho)/\operatorname{tr}\mathcal I_y^{(R)}(\rho)$ exactly when that probability is positive. With $w_\theta=\operatorname{tr}((\Pi_\theta\otimes I_R)\rho)$, the reference outcome law is $p_y=\sum_{\theta\in\Theta}|a_y(\theta)|^2w_\theta$, where $w_\theta\ge0$ and $\sum_\theta w_\theta=1$. If every eigenphase is on the $Q$-grid, then $K_y=\Pi_{y/Q}$ when $y/Q\in\Theta$ and $K_y=0$ otherwise, so the instrument branch is $X\mapsto K_yXK_y^\dagger$. If any eigenphase is off-grid, its nonzero coefficient has modulus less than one in every $K_y$, so $K_y^\dagger K_y$ is not a projection and the induced instrument is not the spectral projection instrument.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite-dimensional spectral decomposition and finite sums.

proposed_after_items.title: Phase-estimation nearest-grid and tail bounds
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $m\ge1$, $Q=2^m$, and $\theta\in[0,1)$. Every nearest grid label $y$ has $P_\theta(y)\ge4/\pi^2$. For any $\eta\in\mathbb R$ with $K=\lfloor Q\eta\rfloor\ge2$,
$$\Pr_{y\sim P_\theta}\!\left[d_{\mathbb T}(\theta-y/Q)\ge\eta\right]\le\frac1{2(K-1)}.$$
If $Q\theta$ is an integer $t$, then $P_\theta(t)=1$ and all other labels have probability $0$.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; this theorem combines finite probability bounds.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, $|0\rangle$ a specified unit vector, $A:H\to H$ a supplied unitary, and $\Pi_{\rm good}$ an explicitly supplied orthogonal projection. Put
$$S_0=I-2|0\rangle\langle0|,\qquad S_{\rm good}=I-2\Pi_{\rm good},\qquad Q=-A S_0A^*S_{\rm good}.$$
Each classical instance has an injective encoding $\operatorname{enc}$ from its declared instance set into $\{0,1\}^*$, with input size $|\operatorname{enc}(z)|$; the promise domain and output obligation are stated for that task. Supplied operator or oracle access is a separate resource declaration.

The success amplitude is $a=\|\Pi_{\rm good}A|0\rangle\|^2\in[0,1]$, and $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt a\in[0,\pi/2]$. Amplitude estimation returns an algebraically encoded estimate of $a$; its requested accuracy and failure probability are stated separately.

For counting, let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and set $N=2^n$ with address basis $\{|x\rangle:x\in\{0,1\}^n\}$ and a Boolean predicate $f$. Set $A=H^{\otimes n}$, $|0\rangle=|0^n\rangle$, $\Pi_{\rm good}=\sum_{f(x)=1}|x\rangle\langle x|$, and $t=|\{x:f(x)=1\}|$. Then the counting amplitude is $a=t/N$. The preparation uses exactly $n$ ordinary Hadamard gates. Access to the controlled membership reflection is a separate explicit resource.

Two phase-estimation access modes are allowed. In the power-query mode, the model supplies each $C(Q^{2^j})$ for $0\le j<m$ as one declared query, with its individual cost recorded. In the repeated-unitary mode the model supplies $C(Q)$ and implements $C(Q^{2^j})$ by $2^j$ sequential calls, for exactly $2^m-1$ controlled-$Q$ calls. In repeated-unitary mode, each controlled-$Q$ call expands as the composite $C(-I)C(A)C(S_0)C(A^*)C(S_{\rm good})$; controlled $A$, controlled $A^*$, controlled $S_0$, controlled $S_{\rm good}$, and the control phase $C(-I)$ must all be supplied or implemented and charged. In power-query mode each supplied controlled power has its own declared cost vector, including any constituent implementations the model uses. An uncontrolled phase query does not supply any of them. Query, ordinary-gate, state-preparation, measurement, and classical bit costs are separate coordinates.

items.title: Two nearest phase labels carry probability at least eight over pi squared
items.statement: Let $M=2^m$ with $m\ge1$, and let $\theta\in[0,1)$ be an eigenphase measured by the $M$-label QPE kernel. The two labels $\lfloor M\theta\rfloor$ and $\lceil M\theta\rceil$ reduced modulo $M$ (one label when $M\theta$ is an integer) have total outcome probability at least $8/\pi^2$.

items.title: Grover eigenphases encode the good probability
items.statement:
Let $\psi=A|0\rangle$, $a=\|\Pi_{\rm good}\psi\|^2$, and $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt a$. If $0<a<1$, define the unit vectors $G=\Pi_{\rm good}\psi/\sqrt a$ and $B=(I-\Pi_{\rm good})\psi/\sqrt{1-a}$. In the ordered basis $(B,G)$, the Grover iterate $Q$ of [[def-qa-13-amplitude-estimation-task]] restricts to
$$\begin{pmatrix}\cos(2\theta)&-\sin(2\theta)\\\sin(2\theta)&\cos(2\theta)\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its eigenvalues are $e^{2i\theta}$ and $e^{-2i\theta}$, and $\psi=\cos\theta B+\sin\theta G$ has squared overlap $1/2$ with each corresponding normalized eigenvector. At $a=0$, $\psi$ is a $+1$ eigenvector; at $a=1$, it is a $-1$ eigenvector.

items.title: Finite exact comparison of real cyclotomic values
items.statement: For an integer $s\ge2$, let $\zeta_s=e^{2\pi i/s}$ and let $P,R\in\mathbb Q[X]$ be given coefficient lists such that $P(\zeta_s)$ and $R(\zeta_s)$ are real. There is a terminating deterministic exact procedure to decide which of these two real numbers is larger, or whether they are equal. Its bit-operation cost is charged to the classical cost model; no polynomial bound is asserted.

items.title: QFT-based amplitude estimation
items.statement:
**Input.** An instance from [[def-qa-13-amplitude-estimation-task]], an integer $m\ge2$, $M=2^m$, and either the declared controlled-power access mode or repeated controlled-$Q$ access.

**Instructions.** Prepare $\psi=A|0\rangle$, run the $M$-label QPE circuit on $Q$ using controlled powers $Q^{2^j}$, $j=0,\ldots,m-1$, and measure its phase register to obtain $y\in\{0,\ldots,M-1\}$. Output the exact cyclotomic value
$$\widetilde a=\sin^2(\pi y/M)=\frac{2-\zeta_M^y-\zeta_M^{-y}}4,\qquad \zeta_M=e^{2\pi i/M},$$
with the real embedding specified by this root. A decimal approximation is postprocessing and is charged separately. The leading minus in $Q$ is retained: on a controlled call it is the control phase $C(-I)$, not a discarded standalone global phase.

items.title: Quantum counting by uniform-state amplitude estimation
items.statement:
**Input.** A Boolean predicate $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, an integer $n\ge0$, $N=2^n$, an explicitly supplied controlled membership reflection for $S_{\rm good}$, a power of two $M=2^m\ge2$, and the other controlled accesses in [[def-qa-13-amplitude-estimation-task]].

Prepare $N^{-1/2}\sum_x|x\rangle=H^{\otimes n}|0^n\rangle$, run the $m$-qubit QPE circuit for $Q$ with $M=2^m$ labels, measure $y$, and output the exact algebraic fraction estimate $\widetilde a=\sin^2(\pi y/M)$ and count estimate $\widetilde t=N\widetilde a$. For $M\ge4$ this is the QFT amplitude-estimation circuit of [[alg-qa-13-phase-estimation-amplitude-estimation]]; for $M=2$, use its one-phase-qubit QPE circuit directly, without invoking the $M\ge4$ error theorem. The fraction and count are real-valued algebraic outputs; integer rounding is optional postprocessing. The controlled membership reflection is an explicit access requirement. In repeated-unitary mode each controlled $Q$ call charges one controlled membership reflection; in power-query mode each supplied controlled power carries its declared cost vector, including any membership-reflection implementations it uses. Neither access mode is inferred from the bare phase oracle $|x\rangle\mapsto(-1)^{f(x)}$.

items.title: Median confidence amplification for amplitude estimation
items.statement:
**Input.** The amplitude-estimation task, rational $0<\epsilon\le1$ and rational $0<\delta<1$.

Initialize $m=0$ and $M=1$. Repeatedly increment $m$ and double $M$ while $M<88/(7\epsilon)$, using exact rational comparison, so that $M=2^m$. Set $r=1$ and repeatedly increase $r$ by $2$ while $2^r<(2/\delta)^8$, using exact rational comparisons. Run $r$ independent fresh copies of the QFT estimator with phase-register size $M$, and return the middle order statistic of their exact algebraic estimates (ties are ordered by their exact value and identical values are interchangeable).

items.title: Amplitude-estimation additive error and success probability
items.statement:
For the QFT-based estimator with $M=2^m\ge4$ and integer $k\ge1$, its output satisfies
$$|\widetilde a-a|\le\frac{2\pi k\sqrt{a(1-a)}}M+\frac{\pi^2k^2}{M^2}$$
with probability at least $8/\pi^2$ when $k=1$, and with probability strictly greater than $1-1/[2(k-1)]$ when $k\ge2$. In particular the $k=1$ error is at most $\pi/M+\pi^2/M^2$. At $a=0$ the output is exactly zero; at $a=1$ it is exactly one.

For every allowed access instance and $M=2^m\ge4$, the prescribed signed controlled circuit and its exact real cyclotomic output are well-defined, retaining the controlled relative phase and separately charged classical output processing.

items.title: Exact query count for the finite-grid iterative estimator
items.statement:
Across the finite-grid schedule with $K\ge1$ and $S\ge1$, forward $A$ calls equal $S\sum_{k=0}^K(m_k+1)$, inverse $A^*$ calls equal $S\sum_{k=0}^K m_k$, and both zero-input reflections and good-predicate reflections equal $S\sum_{k=0}^K m_k$. Thus the total number of $A/A^*$ calls is $S\sum_{k=0}^K(2m_k+1)=S(1+\sum_{k=1}^K(2^k+1))=O(S2^K)$. This count gives no finite-sample success guarantee.

For all integers $K,S,J\ge1$, the finite-grid procedure terminates and returns a uniquely determined exact algebraic output under its least-label tie rule. Its displayed factors are the Bernoulli likelihood factors of the prescribed independent shots; no finite-sample accuracy guarantee is asserted.

items.title: Exact zero-label probability for counting
items.statement:
For a fresh Count run with $L=2^\ell\ge2$ and $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt{t/N}$, the QPE label is zero exactly when the raw count estimate is zero. If $0<t<N$, then
$$\Pr(y=0)=\frac{\sin^2(L\theta)}{L^2\sin^2\theta}.$$
For $t=0$ this probability is $1$; when $L=2$ and $0<t<N$ it is $\cos^2\theta$.

items.title: Amplitude-estimation query and precision complexity
items.statement: For $M=2^m\ge4$, repeated controlled-$Q$ access uses exactly $M-1$ controlled-$Q$ applications in one run; each expands to one call each to controlled $A$, controlled $A^*$, controlled $S_0$, controlled $S_{\rm good}$, and the control phase. Supplied controlled-power access uses exactly $m$ power queries and reports their separate costs. With fixed success probability, additive amplitude error $\epsilon\in(0,1]$ is obtained with $M=\Theta(1/\epsilon)$, hence $O(1/\epsilon)$ repeated controlled-$Q$ calls; state preparation, ordinary gates, and classical encoding are separate costs.

items.title: Quantum counting error and boundary cases
items.statement:
For an integer $n\ge0$, $N=2^n$, $t$ marked addresses among $N$, and $M=2^m\ge4$, the raw estimate satisfies
$$|\widetilde t-t|\le\frac{2\pi k\sqrt{t(N-t)}}M+\frac{\pi^2k^2N}{M^2}$$
with the same success probabilities as the amplitude-estimation theorem for integer $k\ge1$. If $t=0$, the raw estimate is zero with certainty. If $t=N$, the raw estimate is $N$ with certainty because $M$ is even.

For every integer $n\ge0$ and dyadic $M\ge2$, the counting procedure is well-defined, prepares the uniform state with exactly $n$ ordinary Hadamards, specializes the task amplitude to $a=t/N$, and returns the exact algebraic pair $(\widetilde a,N\widetilde a)$ with separately charged optional rounding. Its one-phase-qubit $M=2$ branch is included in this well-definedness claim; the error guarantee above concerns $M\ge4$.

items.title: Explicit median confidence guarantee for amplitude estimation
items.statement:
For rational $0<\epsilon\le1$ and $0<\delta<1$, the median procedure of [[alg-qa-13-median-confidence-estimation]] returns $\widetilde a$ with $|\widetilde a-a|\le\epsilon$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.

Both rational scheduling loops terminate at their least prescribed values, and the odd finite list has a well-defined exact algebraic middle order statistic. Its phase-register size is admissible for the one-run estimator; preparations, queries and comparison bit work retain their separately declared costs.

items.title: Relative approximate counting with unknown marked count
items.statement:
**Input.** A Boolean predicate on $N=2^n\ge1$ addresses with an integer $n\ge0$, the fully declared controlled counting access model, and rational $0<\epsilon\le1$.

Set $\ell=0$. Repeatedly increment $\ell$, set $L=2^\ell$, run a fresh Count$(f,L)$, and stop exactly when its label $y$ is nonzero or $L^2\ge4N$. The test $y\ne0$ is an exact finite label test. Initialize $m=0$ and $M=1$; repeatedly increment $m$ and double $M$ while $M<[20(22/7)^2/\epsilon]L$, using exact rational comparison, so that $M=2^m$. Run a fresh Count$(f,M)$ and use [[lem-qa-13-certified-count-output-rounding]] to output an integer within $2/3$ of its exact algebraic count estimate. The scale loop returns the least power of two meeting its rational threshold; all scales are powers of two and the multiplier grows as $1/\epsilon$ times $L$.

items.title: Quantum counting query complexity
items.statement: For an integer $n\ge0$, $N=2^n$, and a power of two $M=2^m\ge4$, Count uses exactly $M-1$ repeated controlled-Grover calls, or exactly $m$ supplied controlled-power queries, in addition to its $n$ ordinary Hadamards for uniform-state preparation. At fixed success probability, additive count error $\epsilon_c\in(0,N]$ is obtained using $O(N/\epsilon_c)$ repeated controlled-Grover calls; additive fraction error $\epsilon_f\in(0,1]$ uses $O(1/\epsilon_f)$. The count-dependent error bound retains the terms $2\pi k\sqrt{t(N-t)}/M$ and $\pi^2k^2N/M^2$. Algebraic output encoding and integer rounding have separate classical bit costs.

items.statement: In the repeated controlled-$Q$ access mode, the median estimator uses exactly $r(M-1)$ controlled-$Q$ calls. items.title: Relative approximate counting query complexity
items.statement: For an integer $n\ge0$, $N=2^n$, a predicate with $0\le t\le N$ marked addresses, and rational $0<\epsilon\le1$, in the repeated controlled-$Q$ access mode the dyadic relative-counting procedure uses expected $O(\epsilon^{-1}\sqrt{N/t})$ controlled-$Q$ calls when $t>0$, and exactly one controlled membership-reflection call per such controlled Grover call. items.title: Relative approximate counting success guarantee
items.statement:
For the dyadic relative-counting procedure with rational $0<\epsilon\le1$, if $t>0$ its integer output is within $\epsilon t$ of $t$ with probability at least $2/3$. If $t=0$, every rough and final Count output is exactly zero, the loop stops at its finite cutoff, and the output is zero with certainty.

For every stated input, both dyadic scheduling loops terminate and the final certified integer rounding terminates. The final scale is the least dyadic value at least $T=[20(22/7)^2/\epsilon]L$, hence $T\le M<2T$ and $M\ge20\pi^2L/\epsilon$. Fresh preparations and all controlled access and bit costs remain as declared.

proposed_after_items.title: Two nearest phase labels carry probability at least eight over pi squared
proposed_after_items.statement: Let $M=2^m$ with $m\ge1$, and let $\theta\in[0,1)$ be an eigenphase measured by the $M$-label QPE kernel. proposed_after_items.title: Amplitude estimation and counting input/output contract
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, $|0\rangle$ a specified unit vector, $A:H\to H$ a supplied unitary, and $\Pi_{\rm good}$ an explicitly supplied orthogonal projection. Put
$$S_0=I-2|0\rangle\langle0|,\qquad S_{\rm good}=I-2\Pi_{\rm good},\qquad Q=-A S_0A^*S_{\rm good}.$$
Each classical instance has an injective encoding $\operatorname{enc}$ from its declared instance set into $\{0,1\}^*$, with input size $|\operatorname{enc}(z)|$; the promise domain and output obligation are stated for that task. Supplied operator or oracle access is a separate resource declaration.

The success amplitude is $a=\|\Pi_{\rm good}A|0\rangle\|^2\in[0,1]$, and $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt a\in[0,\pi/2]$. Amplitude estimation returns an algebraically encoded estimate of $a$; its requested accuracy and failure probability are stated separately.

For counting, let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and set $N=2^n$ with address basis $\{|x\rangle:x\in\{0,1\}^n\}$ and a Boolean predicate $f$. Write $H_{\rm Had}=2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ for the one-qubit Hadamard gate, distinct from the space $H$, and set $A=H_{\rm Had}^{\otimes n}$, $|0\rangle=|0^n\rangle$, $\Pi_{\rm good}=\sum_{f(x)=1}|x\rangle\langle x|$, and $t=|\{x:f(x)=1\}|$. Then the counting amplitude is $a=t/N$. The preparation uses exactly $n$ ordinary Hadamard gates. Access to the controlled membership reflection is a separate explicit resource.

Two phase-estimation access modes are allowed. In the power-query mode, the model supplies each $C(Q^{2^j})$ for $0\le j<m$ as one declared query, with its individual cost recorded. In the repeated-unitary mode the model supplies $C(Q)$ and implements $C(Q^{2^j})$ by $2^j$ sequential calls, for exactly $2^m-1$ controlled-$Q$ calls. In repeated-unitary mode, each controlled-$Q$ call expands as the composite $C(-I)C(A)C(S_0)C(A^*)C(S_{\rm good})$; controlled $A$, controlled $A^*$, controlled $S_0$, controlled $S_{\rm good}$, and the control phase $C(-I)$ must all be supplied or implemented and charged. In power-query mode each supplied controlled power has its own declared cost vector, including any constituent implementations the model uses. An uncontrolled phase query does not supply any of them. Query, ordinary-gate, state-preparation, measurement, and classical bit costs are separate coordinates.

proposed_after_items.title: Grover eigenphases encode the good probability
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $\psi=A|0\rangle$, $a=\|\Pi_{\rm good}\psi\|^2$, and $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt a$. If $0<a<1$, define the unit vectors $G=\Pi_{\rm good}\psi/\sqrt a$ and $B=(I-\Pi_{\rm good})\psi/\sqrt{1-a}$. In the ordered basis $(B,G)$, the Grover iterate $Q$ of [[def-qa-13-amplitude-estimation-task]] restricts to
$$\begin{pmatrix}\cos(2\theta)&-\sin(2\theta)\\\sin(2\theta)&\cos(2\theta)\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its eigenvalues are $e^{2i\theta}$ and $e^{-2i\theta}$, and $\psi=\cos\theta B+\sin\theta G$ has squared overlap $1/2$ with each corresponding normalized eigenvector. At $a=0$, $\psi$ is a $+1$ eigenvector; at $a=1$, it is a $-1$ eigenvector.

proposed_after_items.title: Iterative no-QFT amplitude estimation by finite-grid likelihood
proposed_after_items.statement:
**Input.** An instance of the task [[def-qa-13-amplitude-estimation-task]] with the same $H,|0\rangle,A,\Pi_{\rm good}$ supplied under the prepared-success-subspace access contract of [[def-qa-12-prepared-success-subspace]]. That contract supplies and charges the uncontrolled calls to $A,A^*,S_0,S_{\rm good}$. Additionally require supplied access to the good/bad projective measurement $\{\Pi_{\rm good},I-\Pi_{\rm good}\}$ of [[def-qc-projective-measurement]], with each use charged in the measurement coordinate and any implementation costs charged separately; no controlled access is used. Also require integers $K,S,J\ge1$.

Set $m_0=0$ and $m_k=2^{k-1}$ for $1\le k\le K$. For each $k=0,\ldots,K$, perform $S$ repetitions: prepare a fresh $A|0\rangle$, apply exactly $m_k$ signed Grover iterates using [[alg-qa-12-amplitude-amplification]], measure the good/bad projective measurement, and record the outcome. Let $h_k$ be the number of good outcomes at scale $k$.

Set $s=2J$ and $\zeta_s=e^{2\pi i/s}$. For an integer $q$, let $\rho_s(q)$ be its least residue in $\{0,\ldots,s-1\}$. For grid labels $j=0,\ldots,J$, put $\theta_j=j\pi/(2J)$ and define the likelihood
$$L_j=\prod_{k=0}^K\sin^{2h_k}((2m_k+1)\theta_j)\cos^{2(S-h_k)}((2m_k+1)\theta_j),$$
where every zeroth power is $1$. For each label $j$ and scale $k=0,\ldots,K$, set
$$r_{kj}=\rho_s((2m_k+1)j),\qquad r'_{kj}=\rho_s(-r_{kj}),$$
and form the rational polynomials
$$U_{kj}(X)=\frac{2-X^{r_{kj}}-X^{r'_{kj}}}{4},\qquad V_{kj}(X)=\frac{2+X^{r_{kj}}+X^{r'_{kj}}}{4}.$$
Put $P_j(X)=\prod_{k=0}^K U_{kj}(X)^{h_k}V_{kj}(X)^{S-h_k}$, treating every zeroth power as $1$. The polynomials $P_j$ are the exact comparison inputs for the likelihoods $L_j$: compare $P_i(\zeta_s)$ and $P_j(\zeta_s)$ using [[lem-qa-13-real-cyclotomic-comparison]], and choose the least label $\widehat j$ attaining the maximum.

Set $E_{\widehat j}(X)=(2-X^{\widehat j}-X^{\rho_s(-\widehat j)})/4$ and return $\widetilde a=E_{\widehat j}(\zeta_s)$, encoded by the pair $(s,E_{\widehat j})$. Each shot uses a fresh state and ordinary measurement. This is a finite-grid likelihood procedure, not a finite-sample $\epsilon,\delta$ guarantee; no such guarantee is asserted here.

proposed_after_items.title: QFT-based amplitude estimation
proposed_after_items.statement:
**Input.** An instance from [[def-qa-13-amplitude-estimation-task]], an integer $m\ge2$, $M=2^m$, and either the declared controlled-power access mode or repeated controlled-$Q$ access.

**Instructions.** Prepare $\psi=A|0\rangle$, run the $M$-label QPE circuit on $Q$ using controlled powers $Q^{2^j}$, $j=0,\ldots,m-1$, and measure its phase register to obtain $y\in\{0,\ldots,M-1\}$. Output the exact cyclotomic value
$$\widetilde a=\sin^2(\pi y/M)=\frac{2-\zeta_M^y-\zeta_M^{-y}}4,\qquad \zeta_M=e^{2\pi i/M},$$
with the real embedding specified by this root. A decimal approximation is postprocessing and is charged separately. The leading minus in $Q$ is retained: on a controlled call it is the control phase $C(-I)$, not a discarded standalone global phase.

proposed_after_items.title: Quantum counting by uniform-state amplitude estimation
proposed_after_items.statement:
**Input.** A Boolean predicate $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, an integer $n\ge0$, $N=2^n$, an explicitly supplied controlled membership reflection for $S_{\rm good}$, a power of two $M=2^m\ge2$, and the other controlled accesses in [[def-qa-13-amplitude-estimation-task]].

Prepare $N^{-1/2}\sum_x|x\rangle=H^{\otimes n}|0^n\rangle$, run the $m$-qubit QPE circuit for $Q$ with $M=2^m$ labels, measure $y$, and output the exact algebraic fraction estimate $\widetilde a=\sin^2(\pi y/M)$ and count estimate $\widetilde t=N\widetilde a$. For $M\ge4$ this is the QFT amplitude-estimation circuit of [[alg-qa-13-phase-estimation-amplitude-estimation]]; for $M=2$, use its one-phase-qubit QPE circuit directly, without invoking the $M\ge4$ error theorem. The fraction and count are real-valued algebraic outputs; integer rounding is optional postprocessing. The controlled membership reflection is an explicit access requirement. In repeated-unitary mode each controlled $Q$ call charges one controlled membership reflection; in power-query mode each supplied controlled power carries its declared cost vector, including any membership-reflection implementations it uses. Neither access mode is inferred from the bare phase oracle $|x\rangle\mapsto(-1)^{f(x)}$.

proposed_after_items.statement:
**Input.** The amplitude-estimation task, rational $0<\epsilon\le1$ and rational $0<\delta<1$.

Initialize $m=0$ and $M=1$. Repeatedly increment $m$ and double $M$ while $M<88/(7\epsilon)$, using exact rational comparison, so that $M=2^m$. Set $r=1$ and repeatedly increase $r$ by $2$ while $2^r<(2/\delta)^8$, using exact rational comparisons. proposed_after_items.title: Rational-interval rounding of a counting output
proposed_after_items.statement:
**Input.** Public integers $N\ge1$, even $M\ge2$, and $0\le y<M$. The output is an integer $q$. All sums, factorials, comparisons and ceiling operations below use exact rational or integer arithmetic, charged as classical bit work under [[def-qa-classical-bit-cost]].

If $y=0$, return $q=0$. Otherwise initialize $r=4$. Compute $R_r=8^{2r+2}/(2r+2)!$; while $NR_r\ge1/24$, increment $r$ by one and recompute $R_r$. At the first $r$ with $NR_r<1/24$, set
$$D_r=\sum_{k=1}^r\frac{2k\,8^{2k-1}}{(2k)!}.$$

Initialize $h=1$. Compute
$$S_h=\sum_{k=0}^{h-1}\frac{(-1)^k}{2k+1},\qquad e_h=\frac4{2h+1},\qquad [a_h,b_h]=\frac{2y}{M}[4S_h-e_h,4S_h+e_h].$$
These are the arctangent-series enclosures from [[thm-principal-inverse-tangent-calculus]] and [[thm-alternating-series-test]]. Set $x_h=(a_h+b_h)/2$ and $\rho_h=(b_h-a_h)/2$. While either $[a_h,b_h]\nsubseteq[0,8]$ or $ND_r\rho_h\ge1/24-NR_r$, increment $h$ by one and recompute $S_h,e_h,a_h,b_h,x_h,\rho_h$.

For the first accepted $h$, compute
$$C_r(x_h)=\sum_{k=0}^r\frac{(-1)^k x_h^{2k}}{(2k)!},\qquad E=D_r\rho_h+R_r,$$
$$u=\frac N2(1-C_r(x_h)-E),\qquad v=\frac N2(1-C_r(x_h)+E).$$
Return $q=\lceil v-2/3\rceil$, computing the rational ceiling by integer division. The termination and error guarantee are established in [[lem-qa-13-certified-count-output-rounding]].

proposed_after_items.statement: Given integers $N\ge1$, even $M\ge2$, and $0\le y<M$, let $z=N\sin^2(\pi y/M)$. proposed_after_items.title: Amplitude-estimation additive error and success probability
proposed_after_items.statement:
For the QFT-based estimator with $M=2^m\ge4$ and integer $k\ge1$, its output satisfies
$$|\widetilde a-a|\le\frac{2\pi k\sqrt{a(1-a)}}M+\frac{\pi^2k^2}{M^2}$$
with probability at least $8/\pi^2$ when $k=1$, and with probability strictly greater than $1-1/[2(k-1)]$ when $k\ge2$. In particular the $k=1$ error is at most $\pi/M+\pi^2/M^2$. At $a=0$ the output is exactly zero; at $a=1$ it is exactly one.

For every allowed access instance and $M=2^m\ge4$, the prescribed signed controlled circuit and its exact real cyclotomic output are well-defined, retaining the controlled relative phase and separately charged classical output processing.

proposed_after_items.title: Exact query count for the finite-grid iterative estimator
proposed_after_items.statement:
Across the finite-grid schedule with $K\ge1$ and $S\ge1$, forward $A$ calls equal $S\sum_{k=0}^K(m_k+1)$, inverse $A^*$ calls equal $S\sum_{k=0}^K m_k$, and both zero-input reflections and good-predicate reflections equal $S\sum_{k=0}^K m_k$. Thus the total number of $A/A^*$ calls is $S\sum_{k=0}^K(2m_k+1)=S(1+\sum_{k=1}^K(2^k+1))=O(S2^K)$. This count gives no finite-sample success guarantee.

For all integers $K,S,J\ge1$, the finite-grid procedure terminates and returns a uniquely determined exact algebraic output under its least-label tie rule. Its displayed factors are the Bernoulli likelihood factors of the prescribed independent shots; no finite-sample accuracy guarantee is asserted.

proposed_after_items.title: Exact zero-label probability for counting
proposed_after_items.statement:
For a fresh Count run with $L=2^\ell\ge2$ and $\theta=\arcsin\sqrt{t/N}$, the QPE label is zero exactly when the raw count estimate is zero. If $0<t<N$, then
$$\Pr(y=0)=\frac{\sin^2(L\theta)}{L^2\sin^2\theta}.$$
For $t=0$ this probability is $1$; when $L=2$ and $0<t<N$ it is $\cos^2\theta$.

proposed_after_items.statement: For $M=2^m\ge4$, repeated controlled-$Q$ access uses exactly $M-1$ controlled-$Q$ applications in one run; each expands to one call each to controlled $A$, controlled $A^*$, controlled $S_0$, controlled $S_{\rm good}$, and the control phase. Supplied controlled-power access uses exactly $m$ power queries and reports their separate costs. With fixed success probability, additive amplitude error $\epsilon\in(0,1]$ is obtained with $M=\Theta(1/\epsilon)$, hence $O(1/\epsilon)$ repeated controlled-$Q$ calls; state preparation, ordinary gates, and classical encoding are separate costs.

proposed_after_items.title: Quantum counting error and boundary cases
proposed_after_items.statement:
For an integer $n\ge0$, $N=2^n$, $t$ marked addresses among $N$, and $M=2^m\ge4$, the raw estimate satisfies
$$|\widetilde t-t|\le\frac{2\pi k\sqrt{t(N-t)}}M+\frac{\pi^2k^2N}{M^2}$$
with the same success probabilities as the amplitude-estimation theorem for integer $k\ge1$. If $t=0$, the raw estimate is zero with certainty. If $t=N$, the raw estimate is $N$ with certainty because $M$ is even.

For every integer $n\ge0$ and dyadic $M\ge2$, the counting procedure is well-defined, prepares the uniform state with exactly $n$ ordinary Hadamards, specializes the task amplitude to $a=t/N$, and returns the exact algebraic pair $(\widetilde a,N\widetilde a)$ with separately charged optional rounding. Its one-phase-qubit $M=2$ branch is included in this well-definedness claim; the error guarantee above concerns $M\ge4$.

proposed_after_items.statement:
For rational $0<\epsilon\le1$ and $0<\delta<1$, the median procedure of [[alg-qa-13-median-confidence-estimation]] returns $\widetilde a$ with $|\widetilde a-a|\le\epsilon$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.

proposed_after_items.title: Relative approximate counting with unknown marked count
proposed_after_items.statement:
**Input.** A Boolean predicate on $N=2^n\ge1$ addresses with an integer $n\ge0$, the fully declared controlled counting access model, and rational $0<\epsilon\le1$.

Set $\ell=0$. Repeatedly increment $\ell$, set $L=2^\ell$, run a fresh Count$(f,L)$, and stop exactly when its label $y$ is nonzero or $L^2\ge4N$. The test $y\ne0$ is an exact finite label test. Initialize $m=0$ and $M=1$; repeatedly increment $m$ and double $M$ while $M<[20(22/7)^2/\epsilon]L$, using exact rational comparison, so that $M=2^m$. Run a fresh Count$(f,M)$ and run [[alg-qa-13-certified-count-output-rounding]] on $(N,M,y)$ to output an integer within $2/3$ of its exact algebraic count estimate, as proved by [[lem-qa-13-certified-count-output-rounding]]. The scale loop returns the least power of two meeting its rational threshold; all scales are powers of two and the multiplier grows as $1/\epsilon$ times $L$.

proposed_after_items.title: Quantum counting query complexity
proposed_after_items.statement: For an integer $n\ge0$, $N=2^n$, and a power of two $M=2^m\ge4$, Count uses exactly $M-1$ repeated controlled-Grover calls, or exactly $m$ supplied controlled-power queries, in addition to its $n$ ordinary Hadamards for uniform-state preparation. At fixed success probability, additive count error $\epsilon_c\in(0,N]$ is obtained using $O(N/\epsilon_c)$ repeated controlled-Grover calls; additive fraction error $\epsilon_f\in(0,1]$ uses $O(1/\epsilon_f)$. The count-dependent error bound retains the terms $2\pi k\sqrt{t(N-t)}/M$ and $\pi^2k^2N/M^2$. Algebraic output encoding and integer rounding have separate classical bit costs.

proposed_after_items.statement: In the repeated controlled-$Q$ access mode, the median estimator uses exactly $r(M-1)$ controlled-$Q$ calls. proposed_after_items.statement: For an integer $n\ge0$, $N=2^n$, a predicate with $0\le t\le N$ marked addresses, and rational $0<\epsilon\le1$, in the repeated controlled-$Q$ access mode the dyadic relative-counting procedure uses expected $O(\epsilon^{-1}\sqrt{N/t})$ controlled-$Q$ calls when $t>0$, and exactly one controlled membership-reflection call per such controlled Grover call. proposed_after_items.title: Relative approximate counting success guarantee
proposed_after_items.statement:
For the dyadic relative-counting procedure with rational $0<\epsilon\le1$, if $t>0$ its integer output is within $\epsilon t$ of $t$ with probability at least $2/3$. If $t=0$, every rough and final Count output is exactly zero, the loop stops at its finite cutoff, and the output is zero with certainty.

For every stated input, both dyadic scheduling loops terminate and the final certified integer rounding terminates. The final scale is the least dyadic value at least $T=[20(22/7)^2/\epsilon]L$, hence $T\le M<2T$ and $M\ge20\pi^2L/\epsilon$. Fresh preparations and all controlled access and bit costs remain as declared.

statement_or_definition.before:
Fix an integer N≥1, a nonempty finite set D⊆{0,1}^N, and a Boolean function f:D→{0,1}. A Boolean query problem is the tuple (N,D,f) with input x∈D and standard XOR oracle
$$O_x|i,b,w\rangle=|i,b\oplus x_i,w\rangle\quad (i\in[N],\ b\in\{0,1\}).$$
For 0≤ε<1/2, Q_ε(f) is the least worst-case number of these oracle calls of an algorithm outputting f(x) with probability at least 1−ε for every x∈D. The input promise does not restrict the oracle address. Only query calls are counted here; no gate-efficiency assertion is part of this definition.
statement_or_definition.after:
Fix an integer N≥1, a nonempty finite set D⊆{0,1}^N, and a Boolean function f:D→{0,1}. A Boolean query problem is the tuple (N,D,f) with input x∈D and standard XOR oracle
$$O_x|i,b,w\rangle=|i,b\oplus x_i,w\rangle\quad (i\in[N],\ b\in\{0,1\}).$$
The local address register is $\mathbb C^N$ with ordered basis $|i\rangle=e_{i-1}$, $i\in[N]$. For its qubit realization, set $a=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ and encode $i$ by the $a$-bit binary word for $i-1$. Define the total bit function $\widetilde x$ on all $a$-bit words by $\widetilde x(j)=x_{j+1}$ for $0\le j<N$ and $\widetilde x(j)=0$ for $N\le j<2^a$. The standard bit-flip query for $\widetilde x$ restricts to $O_x$ on the encoded local register and acts as the identity on unused address codewords. Algorithms in the local model use the $N$-address register at query calls.

For 0≤ε<1/2, Q_ε(f) is the least worst-case number of these oracle calls of an algorithm outputting f(x) with probability at least 1−ε for every x∈D. The input promise does not restrict the oracle address. Only query calls are counted here; no gate-efficiency assertion is part of this definition.

statement_or_definition.before:
For a finite matrix A indexed by D×D and Boolean masks Δ={Δ_i}_{i=1}^N, define
$$
\gamma_2(A\mid\Delta):=\inf \max\!\left\{\max_{x\in D}\sum_i\|u_{x,i}\|^2,\ \max_{y\in D}\sum_i\|v_{y,i}\|^2\right\},
$$
where the infimum is over finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and vector families satisfying
$$A_{xy}=\sum_i(\Delta_i)_{xy}\langle u_{x,i}|v_{y,i}\rangle_D\quad(x,y\in D).$$
Set the value to $+\infty$ if no such families exist. Every feasible family may be taken in dimension at most $2|D|$ for each i.

\gamma_2(A\mid\Delta):=\inf \max\!\left\{\max_{x\in D}\sum_i\|u_{x,i}\|^2,\ \max_{y\in D}\sum_i\|v_{y,i}\|^2\right\},

items.title: Finite real semidefinite programs satisfy strong duality under strict feasibility
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $n\ge1$, $m\ge0$, $A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m$ be linear, $b\in\mathbb R^m$, and $C\in\mathbb S^n$, where $\mathbb S^n$ is the space of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices with Frobenius pairing $\langle X,Y\rangle_F=\sum_{r,s}X_{rs}Y_{rs}$. Define the primal and dual values
$$p^*=\sup\{\langle C,X\rangle_F:A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\},\qquad d^*=\inf\{b^Ty:A^*y-C\succeq0\},$$
where $A^*$ is the Euclidean adjoint in these finite-dimensional coordinates. Suppose both feasible sets contain strict points, meaning $A(X_0)=b$ with $X_0\succ0$ and $A^*y_0-C\succ0$, and suppose both optimal values are finite. Then $p^*=d^*$, and both extrema are attained.

Here $X\succeq0$ means $v^TXv\ge0$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^n$, while $X\succ0$ means strict inequality for nonzero $v$.
proof_obligations: State the exact primal/dual cones, affine constraints, objective maps, and sign convention for the filtered-γ₂/adversary SDPs.
Exhibit strict feasible primal and dual points for these particular programs; prove feasibility, finite optimal values, and attainment hypotheses rather than assuming them.

Construct the exact finite-dimensional closed convex epigraph/separation set and prove it is closed; apply the existing point-versus-closed-convex separation theorem only after checking its nonempty/closed/convex hypotheses.
Derive the separating functional, identify its components with a dual feasible point and objective bound, and prove weak duality plus the reverse inequality/attainment for this SDP pair.

items.title: Effective spectral gap for a product of two reflections
items.statement_or_definition:
Let H be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, Π and Δ orthogonal projections on H, R_Π=2Π-I and R_Δ=2Δ-I, and U=R_ΠR_Δ. For 0≤ω≤π, let E_ω be the spectral projection of U onto eigenvalues e^{iφ} whose principal arguments satisfy |φ|≤ω. If Δw=0, then
$$\|E_\omega\Pi w\|\le \frac{\omega}{2}\|w\|.$$
proof_obligations: Use Jordan's lemma to decompose into invariant one- and two-dimensional blocks; compute the 2×2 rotation and bound |sin(φ/2)|≤|φ|/2.
Handle rank-zero/full blocks explicitly.

items.title: Finite Boolean query problem and error model for adversary bounds
items.statement_or_definition:
Fix an integer N≥1, a nonempty finite set D⊆{0,1}^N, and a Boolean function f:D→{0,1}. A Boolean query problem is the tuple (N,D,f) with input x∈D and standard XOR oracle
$$O_x|i,b,w\rangle=|i,b\oplus x_i,w\rangle\quad (i\in[N],\ b\in\{0,1\}).$$
For 0≤ε<1/2, Q_ε(f) is the least worst-case number of these oracle calls of an algorithm outputting f(x) with probability at least 1−ε for every x∈D. The input promise does not restrict the oracle address. Only query calls are counted here; no gate-efficiency assertion is part of this definition.
proof_obligations: Bind all later matrices to the finite input set D and the same query convention.
This local interface consumes the already defined query/polynomial setting without importing a physics model.

items.title: Controlled input-consistency reflection from a bit query
items.statement_or_definition:
**Inputs.** A Boolean query problem with $N\ge1$, promised input $x\in D$ accessed by its standard XOR oracle, a finite work space $K$, a one-bit control $c$, and a data register with orthogonal decomposition
$$\mathcal H=\operatorname{span}\{|start\rangle\}\oplus(\mathbb C^N\otimes K\otimes\mathbb C^2),$$
where the address basis is $|i\rangle=e_{i-1}$ for $i\in[N]$ and $|start\rangle$ is a specified unit vector orthogonal to the query summand,
and one clean scratch bit $u=0$. Fix a known address $i_0\in[N]$. Define the consistency sum
$$\Pi_x=|start\rangle\langle start|+\sum_{i=1}^N|i\rangle\langle i|\otimes I_K\otimes|x_i\rangle\langle x_i|.$$

**Output.** A gate list for the controlled plus-on-range reflection $2\Pi_x-I$ on the data register, returning the scratch bit to zero.

**Instructions.** In query mode route address $i$ to the oracle and use $u$ as its target. In start mode route the oracle address to the fixed $i_0$ and apply a Hadamard to $u$, so its query target is $|+\rangle$. Make one unconditional standard XOR oracle call. Apply phase $-1$ exactly when $c=1$, the mode is query, and the response bit $z$ differs from $u$; disable this phase on start and when $c=0$. Make a second unconditional XOR call with the same address routing. In start mode apply the Hadamard to $u$ again. Return the data and control registers and the scratch. No controlled unknown-oracle call is invoked.
proof_obligations: Specify the finite orthogonal start/query mode, response/work factors, clean scratch and comparison phase.
Give the exact two-query procedure and state that both calls are ordinary standard XOR calls, not controlled black-box access.
Defer its correctness and exact two-query property to the separate theorem items.

items.title: Input-mismatch masks and entrywise filtering
items.statement_or_definition:

$$(\Delta_i)_{xy}:=\mathbf 1[x_i\ne y_i].$$

proof_obligations: Fix matrix indexing/order, real versus complex entries, and the zero-input/constant-function convention.

items.title: Filtered γ₂ factorization norm for query mismatch masks
items.statement_or_definition:
For a finite matrix A indexed by D×D and Boolean masks Δ={Δ_i}_{i=1}^N, define
$$
\gamma_2(A\mid\Delta):=\inf \max\!\left\{\max_{x\in D}\sum_i\|u_{x,i}\|^2,\ \max_{y\in D}\sum_i\|v_{y,i}\|^2\right\},
$$
where the infimum is over finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and vector families satisfying
$$A_{xy}=\sum_i(\Delta_i)_{xy}\langle u_{x,i}|v_{y,i}\rangle_D\quad(x,y\in D).$$
Set the value to $+\infty$ if no such families exist. Every feasible family may be taken in dimension at most $2|D|$ for each i.
proof_obligations: State linear-first/Dirac convention, finite dimension sufficiency, attainment conditions and infeasible-support cases.

items.title: Dual vector formulation of the general adversary bound
items.statement_or_definition:
For every finite nonconstant partial Boolean function $f:D\to\{0,1\}$,
$$\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(f)=\min_{\{v_{x,i}\}}\max\{C_0,C_1\},\qquad C_b:=\max_{x:f(x)=b}\sum_i\|v_{x,i}\|^2.$$
The vectors lie in a common finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and satisfy, for all distinct $x,y$,
$$\sum_{i:x_i\ne y_i}\langle v_{x,i}|v_{y,i}\rangle_D=\mathbf1[f(x)\ne f(y)].$$
The minimum is attained. If only opposite-output constraints are initially required, tensoring each vector with $|x_i\oplus f(x)\rangle$ imposes the equal-output zero constraints without changing costs or cross-output values.
proof_obligations: Derive the SDP dual from the signed symmetric Γ program entry by entry.
Use the finite SDP duality lemma and show feasibility/attainment under the nonconstant Boolean hypotheses.
Explain balancing the 0/1 vector-family costs by reciprocal scaling.

To impose zero equal-output constraints without raising the objective, replace v_(x,i) by v_(x,i)⊗|x_i xor f(x)⟩. For terms with x_i≠y_i, the added labels coincide iff f(x)≠f(y); cross-output inner products remain unchanged and equal-output products vanish. An output-label factor alone would instead kill the required cross-output products.

items.title: Bounded-error evaluation from a dual adversary certificate
items.statement_or_definition:
**Inputs.** A finite nonconstant Boolean function $f:D\to\{0,1\}$ on $N\ge1$ input bits and a supplied finite dual-vector certificate $\{v_{x,i}\}$ in a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $V$, meaning that for every distinct $x,y\in D$,
$$\sum_{i:x_i\ne y_i}\langle v_{x,i}|v_{y,i}\rangle_D=\mathbf1[f(x)\ne f(y)].$$
Its class costs $C_b:=\max_{x:f(x)=b}\sum_i\|v_{x,i}\|^2$ satisfy $C_0,C_1\le A$ for a supplied bound $A\ge1$. The declared standard XOR input oracle is available. The input-independent controlled witness-span reflection specified below is a nonoracle operation in this query model; no efficient gate implementation for it is assumed.

**Output.** A Boolean estimate of $f(x)$ for the promised input $x\in D$.

**Instructions.** Use the finite work space
$$\mathcal H=\operatorname{span}\{|start\rangle\}\oplus(\mathbb C^N\otimes V\otimes\mathbb C^2).$$
Here the address basis is $|i\rangle=e_{i-1}$ for $i\in[N]$, and $|start\rangle$ is a specified unit vector orthogonal to the query summand.
The witness family is classical instance data used to specify a subspace, not an input-dependent state preparation. Define
$$\nu_x=1+\frac1{2A}\sum_i\|v_{x,i}\|^2,\qquad |\psi_x\rangle=\nu_x^{-1/2}\left(|start\rangle+\frac1{\sqrt{2A}}\sum_i|i\rangle|v_{x,i}\rangle|x_i\rangle\right).$$
Let $\Delta$ project onto the span of all $|\psi_y\rangle$ with $f(y)=1$, and let
$$\Pi_x=|start\rangle\langle start|+\sum_{i=1}^N|i\rangle\langle i|\otimes I_V\otimes|x_i\rangle\langle x_i|$$
project onto $|start\rangle$ plus query states whose response is $x_i$. Form the exact ordered product
$$U_x=(2\Pi_x-I)(2\Delta-I).$$

Choose $M=2^m$ as the least power of two satisfying $M\ge512A$. Initialize the data register to $|start\rangle$ and apply the coherent QPE gate list followed by its projective readout on $U_x$. Implement controlled $U_x$ in chronological order by controlled $(2\Delta-I)$, then controlled $(2\Pi_x-I)$, retaining both plus-on-range signs. Repeat that complete controlled circuit $2^j$ times for the required power $U_x^{2^j}$ at each $j=0,\ldots,m-1$. Each controlled input-dependent reflection is the two-unconditional-query consistency-reflection circuit of [[alg-qa-16-controlled-consistency-reflection]]. For the measured phase label $y$, return $1$ exactly when $y=0$ and return $0$ otherwise. No gate-complexity bound is asserted for the input-independent reflection about the full witness span or the remaining nonoracle gates.
proof_obligations: Specify all tensor registers, the orthogonal start/query mode, certificate balance and normalization ν_x.
Define the phase-estimation circuit and output threshold y=0 exactly; M is the least power of two with M≥512A.
For f(x)=1, use |ψ_x⟩ in both ranges and show |⟨start|ψ_x⟩|²=1/ν_x≥2/3.
For f(x)=0, construct |φ_x⟩=μ_x^{-1/2}(|start⟩−√(2A)Σ_i|i⟩|v_{x,i}⟩|1−x_i⟩), μ_x=1+2AΣ_i||v_{x,i}||²≤1+2A²; prove Δ|φ_x⟩=0 and Π_x|φ_x⟩=|start⟩/√μ_x.

Apply the effective spectral-gap bound with angular threshold ω=1/(4A); bound the nonzero-phase QPE probability at y=0 using the geometric-sum tail and show the combined false-positive probability is below 1/3 for M≥512A.
Do not assert an efficient gate implementation of reflection about the full witness span.
Apply the exact QC reflection sign/unitarity theorem to both R_x and R_Δ before controlling their product; preserve U_x=(2Π_x−I)(2Δ−I) exactly.

items.title: Input-distribution certificates upper-bound the nonnegative adversary value
items.statement_or_definition:
For a nonconstant finite Boolean query problem (N,D,f), let each p_x be a probability distribution on [N]. If
$$\eta:=\min_{f(x)\ne f(y)}\sum_{i:x_i\ne y_i}\sqrt{p_x(i)p_y(i)}>0,$$
then the nonnegative adversary value satisfies $\operatorname{Adv}(f)\le1/\eta$.
proof_obligations: Choose a nonnegative unit top eigenvector for an arbitrary feasible Γ.
Insert the pairwise overlap inequality into its Rayleigh quotient and bound each filtered term by ||Γ∘Δ_i|| times the squared norm of its weighted vector.
