proposed_after_items.title: Szegedy-walk marked-set detection
proposed_after_items.statement:
**Input.** A finite symmetric lazy row-stochastic matrix $P$ on nonempty $X$, with uniform stationary law and, when $|X|\ge2$, real promised lower gap $\delta_0\in(0,1]$ satisfying $\delta(P)=1-\lambda_2(P)\ge\delta_0$; a marked predicate with promise $\mathcal M=\varnothing$ or $|\mathcal M|/|X|\ge\varepsilon_0$ for real $\varepsilon_0\in(0,1]$; and a real failure target $\beta\in(0,1)$. Supply an exact two-outcome projective test on the first register with its Lüders instrument and declared cost $C_{\rm mark}$; this cost includes the marked-branch label readout and verification. The finite classical input supplies, for each $z\in\{\delta_0,\varepsilon_0,\beta\}$, a certified dyadic bracket $[z_-,z_+]$ encoded by finite binary numerators and exponents, with
$$0<z_-\le z\le z_+\le\min(1,2z_-).$$
The bracket containments are input promises; every endpoint bit and all subsequent comparison, precision, and bit-time costs are charged. Such a finite bracket exists for every real parameter in the stated interval. The numerical input model also supplies terminating exact comparisons for rational values and the algebraic real parts of roots of unity used below; it declares and charges their bit-time and description costs. Write $\underline\delta=(\delta_0)_-$, $\underline\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_0)_-$, and $\underline\beta=\beta_-$. Also supply a circuit $A_{\rm unif}$ preparing $|s\rangle=|X|^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in X}|x\rangle$ with its cost and a row-preparation access model for the absorbing chain $P'$ of [[lem-qa-18-absorbing-walk-discriminant-decomposition]]. The model supplies $V_{P'}$, its inverse and controlled forms, the clean-state reflection and its controlled form, and the swap and controlled swap needed for the one-reflection walk; each constituent is separately charged. If $|X|=1$, the procedure measures its sole label with the marked predicate and terminates exactly, without using the gap parameter or walk. Marked-check, preparation, controlled-walk, inverse, gate, precision, comparison, and description-bit costs are separate declared inputs. A matrix alone supplies none of these circuits.

**Output.** `NONEMPTY` if a marked label is found or the phase test accepts; otherwise `EMPTY`. A found label is returned and checked against the supplied predicate.

**Instructions.**

1. If $|X|=1$, measure its only label, evaluate the supplied predicate and return the exact answer. Otherwise set $\gamma_0=\arccos(1-\underline\delta\,\underline\varepsilon)$. Start at $m=6$ and increment until the exact comparison
$$1-\underline\delta\,\underline\varepsilon\le\cos(\pi 2^{5-m}),$$
and set $Q=2^m$. Since the compared cosine is the real part of a root of unity, this is a finite exact algebraic comparison; it is equivalent to $m=\lceil\log_2(32\pi/\gamma_0)\rceil$. Start at $k=1$ and increment until the exact rational comparison $6^k\underline\beta\ge1$ holds, equivalently $k=\lceil\ln(1/\underline\beta)/\ln6\rceil$. Both loops terminate because $\underline\delta\,\underline\varepsilon>0$ and $\underline\beta>0$. All comparisons and their bit costs are part of the declared input cost model.
2. Repeat the following fresh-state run $k$ times, stopping early if `NONEMPTY` is returned.
3. Prepare $|s\rangle$ with $A_{\rm unif}$ and apply the supplied row preparation $V_{P'}$ to obtain the two-register row state. On the first register, use the supplied two-outcome projective measurement with $\Pi_1=\sum_{x\in\mathcal M}|x\rangle\langle x|\otimes I_{\rm rest}$ and $\Pi_0=I-\Pi_1$, with Lüders branch maps $Z\mapsto\Pi_aZ\Pi_a$. These maps form a valid instrument: the projections are non-negative, sum to identity, and equal their own non-negative square roots, so [[thm-qc-luders-instrument-of-a-povm-is-valid]] applies. If outcome $1$ occurs, measure the first register in its computational basis, verify the resulting label $x\in\mathcal M$, and output `NONEMPTY` and $x$ immediately. If outcome $0$ occurs with positive probability, continue with its normalized projected state; this preserves coherence among all unmarked labels. Outcome $0$ is impossible when $\mathcal M=X$, so no conditional state is needed there.
4. On the unmarked branch, apply the coherent QPE circuit prefix from [[alg-qa-quantum-phase-estimation]] to the conditioned two-register state for the one-reflection walk $U'=S(2T'T'^*-I)$, where $T'$ is the row-preparation map for $P'$. The QPE prefix is a finite unitary circuit and acts on this arbitrary conditioned superposition; its eigenvector input in the outcome analysis does not restrict the circuit's input domain. Measure the phase register only after the controlled-power and inverse-QFT circuit has run. Use supplied controlled powers if available; otherwise implement each controlled $U'^{2^j}$ by $2^j$ sequential controlled one-step $U'$ calls. The factorwise controlled call charges controlled $V_{P'}^\dagger$, controlled $V_{P'}$, the controlled clean-state reflection, and controlled swap. No controlled inverse of $U'$ is used.
5. For the measured integer $y\in\{0,\ldots,Q-1\}$, compute $d(y)=\min(y/Q,1-y/Q)$ using exact rational arithmetic. Since $0<\underline\delta\,\underline\varepsilon\le1$, the principal inverse-cosine convention and cosine monotonicity give $0<\gamma_0\le\pi/2$. Return `NONEMPTY` exactly when $d(y)>\gamma_0/(4\pi)$; equality takes the `EMPTY` branch. This strict comparison is finite: if $d(y)>1/8$ accept, and if $d(y)\le1/8$ compare the algebraic numbers $\cos(4\pi d(y))$ and $1-\underline\delta\,\underline\varepsilon$, accepting exactly when the former is strictly smaller. Here $4\pi d(y)$ is a rational multiple of $\pi$, so its cosine is the real part of a root of unity; monotonicity of cosine on $[0,\pi]$ gives the stated comparison. Charge the exact comparison and all phase-register/inverse-QFT gates.
6. If all $k$ fresh runs fail to return `NONEMPTY`, output `EMPTY`. A run uses one marked check, the supplied uniform-state and one row-preparation costs, one $m$-bit QPE, and its explicitly charged controlled-walk calls. With only one-step controlled access, QPE uses exactly $Q-1$ controlled $U'$ calls. Gate synthesis, bracket-description bits, exact comparison arithmetic, and classical threshold bits are additional charged costs.

proposed_after_items.title: Coherent Johnson row access with stored values
proposed_after_items.statement: For the lazy Johnson chain and XOR value oracle in [[def-qa-18-element-distinctness-johnson-walk]], write $d_f(S)$ for the values at the indices of $S$, in increasing index order. In the pure value-query model, encoded vertex preparation costs $r$ queries. Coherent row preparation and its inverse, including controlled versions, cost at most two queries each. The corresponding controlled row-space reflection costs at most four queries, and a controlled $W=U^2$ step and its inverse cost at most eight. A stationary two-register walk state costs at most $r+2$ queries, and its marked check uses zero value queries. Gates, memory, uniform generation, and exact coefficient preparation are separate resources; no gate-time bound is asserted.

proposed_after_items.title: Element-distinctness O(N^{2/3}) query bound
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $N\ge4$, $f:[N]\to\mathcal V$ be given by the coherent value oracle in [[def-qa-18-element-distinctness-johnson-walk]], and suppose some distinct $a,b$ satisfy $f(a)=f(b)$. For any $2\le r\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor$, the lazy Johnson walk has absolute gap $\delta=N/[2r(N-r)]$, marked stationary mass at least $\varepsilon=r(r-1)/[N(N-1)]$, stored-vertex setup value-query cost $r$, elementary replacement-update cost $2$, and check cost $0$. The controlled row-access construction of [[lem-qa-18-johnson-stored-data-query-access]] supplies stationary edge-state setup at most $r+2$, controlled row reflection at most $4$, and controlled two-reflection walk/inverse at most $8$ value queries. The reversible-walk finding theorem therefore gives a constant-success marked-subset finder with

$$r+O\!\left(\frac{N}{\sqrt r}\right)$$

value queries. Taking $r=\min\{\lfloor N/2\rfloor,\max\{2,\lfloor N^{2/3}\rfloor\}\}$ gives $O(N^{2/3})$ queries. A measured marked subset contains a colliding pair among its stored values, which can be output without further value queries; comparison gates are separate resources.

proposed_after_items.title: Walk detection correctness and cost
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $P=(I+Q)/2$ be a finite symmetric lazy transition matrix on a nonempty finite set $X$, with uniform stationary law. Fix real promise parameters $\delta_0,\varepsilon_0\in(0,1]$ and $\beta\in(0,1)$. When $|X|\ge2$, suppose $\lambda_2(P)\le1-\delta_0$; the marked-set promise is $\mathcal M=\varnothing$ or $|\mathcal M|/|X|\ge\varepsilon_0$. The finite algorithm input includes certified dyadic brackets $[z_-,z_+]$ for $z\in\{\delta_0,\varepsilon_0,\beta\}$ with $0<z_-\le z\le z_+\le\min(1,2z_-)$; the containment is an input promise and every endpoint bit and comparison cost is charged separately. Such brackets exist for every allowed real parameter. For $|X|=1$, the promise parameters are unused. Write $\underline\delta=(\delta_0)_-$, $\underline\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_0)_-$, and $\underline\beta=\beta_-$. Give the algorithm the stated uniform-state circuit, a row-preparation access model for the absorbing chain $P'$, its controlled and inverse calls needed for the one-reflection walk, the marked check, and all their separate costs. Put

$$\gamma_0=\arccos(1-\underline\delta\,\underline\varepsilon),\quad m=\min\{j\ge6:1-\underline\delta\,\underline\varepsilon\le\cos(\pi2^{5-j})\},\quad Q=2^m,\quad k=\min\{j\ge1:6^j\underline\beta\ge1\},$$

where the least-integer formulas are exactly the finite comparisons used by the algorithm. Then [[alg-qa-18-szegedy-phase-detection]] has no false positive on an empty marked set and outputs `NONEMPTY` with probability at least $1-\beta$ on every promised nonempty instance. For $|X|\ge2$, let $C_{\rm init}=C_{\rm unif}+C_{\rm row}$, where the terms are the supplied uniform-state and one row-preparation costs, $C_{\rm mark}$ an upper bound for the initial marked/unmarked Lüders test and its marked-branch label readout and verification, $C_{\rm walk}$ the cost of one controlled one-reflection walk call, and $G_{\rm QPE}(m)$ the phase-register preparation and inverse-QFT gate cost. Its worst-case charged quantum cost is at most

$$k\bigl(C_{\rm init}+C_{\rm mark}+(Q-1)C_{\rm walk}+G_{\rm QPE}(m)\bigr),$$

when only one-step controlled-walk access is supplied. The factorwise implementation of $C_{\rm walk}$ charges one controlled row-preparation inverse, one controlled row preparation, the controlled clean-state reflection, and the controlled swap. With separately supplied controlled powers, replace $(Q-1)C_{\rm walk}$ by the sum of their $m$ declared costs. The bracket ratios imply $Q=O((\delta_0\varepsilon_0)^{-1/2})$ and $k=O(1+\ln(1/\beta))$, so the approved all-real parameter scope retains the same asymptotic resource bound. This is a detection result; a `NONEMPTY` phase-test outcome does not supply a marked label. Synthesis, endpoint bits, exact algebraic/rational comparisons, description bits and precision remain separate coordinates.

proposed_after_items.title: Element-distinctness gate cost in the QRAM model
proposed_after_items.statement:
Fix an injective encoding of values in $[M]$ by $b=O(\log(M+1))$ bits and take the parameter $r$ from [[thm-qa-18-element-distinctness-query-cost]]. For $N\ge4096$, the finite canonical storage of [[def-qa-18-canonical-skip-list-for-element-distinctness]] has hash-table lookup, rank/select, complement-unranking, value insertion/deletion, and collision-check subroutines with $\operatorname{polylog}(N+M)$ QRAM gate-time when their bounded searches do not overrun; the table uses $O(N^{2/3}\log^3(N+M))$ memory bits. A fixed threshold $N_0\ge4096$ is chosen below; the search uses this storage for $N\ge N_0$ and direct value comparison for the finite range $4\le N<N_0$.

For $N\ge N_0$, let $G_{\rm subset}$ be the gate-time of the supplied uniform $r$-subset preparation. Assume an explicit compatible realization of the controlled/inverse Johnson-walk access used by reversible finding exists on this canonical storage, uses the local operations proved below with their reversible overflow/overrun caps, and preserves the hash seed. Let $G_{\rm row}$ be the maximum gate-time of one charged walk-update unit in that realization, including the forward, inverse, controlled, reflection, and swap capabilities supplied for the lazy Johnson walk in [[def-qa-17-walk-access-model]] and any encoding conversion. Under this explicit interface assumption, the complete search has value-query cost $O(N^{2/3})$ and gate-time

$$G_{\rm subset}+O\!\left(r\operatorname{polylog}(N+M)+N^{2/3}\bigl(G_{\rm row}+\operatorname{polylog}(N+M)\bigr)\right).$$

The local storage operations are proved below; this item does not construct the compatible full row-access circuit or derive polylogarithmic bounds for $G_{\rm subset}$ and $G_{\rm row}$. The unconditional $O(N^{2/3}\operatorname{polylog}(N+M))$ gate-time conclusion requires $G_{\rm subset}=O(N^{2/3}\operatorname{polylog}(N+M))$ and $G_{\rm row}=O(\operatorname{polylog}(N+M))$.

The phase-estimation part of this gate-time profile uses the ideal continuous-rotation submodel of [[thm-qa-phase-estimation-access-cost]], where each exact controlled phase is one gate occurrence. Any synthesis overhead for a fixed finite gate alphabet is a separate cost.

For a Boolean value circuit with $S$ non-input nodes, including constants, $E$ input-port uses counted with multiplicity, and $m$ output bits, the serial compiler [[alg-qc-reversible-embedding]] implements one reversible XOR value query using at most $6S+4E+m$ ordinary gate occurrences. With the full DAG-layer parameters $D,F$ of [[thm-qc-reversible-embedding-parallel-depth]] (including any non-output nodes), its alternative parallel implementation uses at most $6S+4E+3m$ occurrences and has depth at most

$$2D\bigl(2\lceil\log_2(F+1)\rceil+3\bigr)+2\lceil\log_2(m+1)\rceil+1.$$

This bounds the written depth of the supplied parallel schedule under [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]. It does not claim minimum-layer depth or include the other ordinary gates used by the walk data structure.

items.title: Exact simulation of two commuting terms
items.statement:
If two finite-dimensional self-adjoint matrices $H_1,H_2$ commute, then every first-order product step is exact:
$$e^{-ihH_1}e^{-ihH_2}=e^{-ih(H_1+H_2)}\qquad(h\in\mathbb R).$$
Consequently $S_1(t/r)^r=U_{H_1+H_2}(t)$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$ and $r\ge1$.

items.title: First-order error for two Pauli terms
items.statement:
For the Pauli matrices
$$X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\quad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},$$
the two-term Hamiltonian $H=X+Z$ has first-order commutator bound $t^2/r$. Also, for every $\lambda\ge0$, the same fixed total matrix $H=Z$ has the decomposition $H_1=\lambda X$, $H_2=Z-\lambda X$, whose commutator certificate grows with $\lambda$ although $\|H\|=1$.

statement.after:
Let $A$ be an $N\times N$ Hermitian matrix with at most $d$ nonzero entries in each row, $\|A\|_{\rm op}\le1$, supplied with the full sparse access model of [[def-qa-27-cks-sparse-oracle-model]]. Its finite-precision values must decode to a Hermitian $\widetilde A$ with certified $\|A-\widetilde A\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_{\rm val}$, and the exact QA25 encoding and simulator-call certificates must satisfy the budgets in [[alg-qa-27-cks-variable-time-linear-solver]]. Let $|b\rangle$ be a normalized state supported on eigenvalues with $|\lambda|\ge1/\kappa$ for declared $\kappa\ge1$, prepared by a supplied clean-work unitary $B$. For targets $0<\epsilon<1$ and $0<\rho<1/3$, execute the constructor at supplied rationals $\epsilon/2<e\le\epsilon$ and $\rho/2<\beta\le\rho$, with access and construction certificates for these requests. The uncapped `efficient-qsvt` constructor, or a finite-cap construction that completes its certificates, outputs with probability at least $1-\rho$ a conditional pure system state admitting a unit representative within vector-norm error $\epsilon$ of $A^+|b\rangle/\|A^+|b\rangle\|$, for every fixed $0<\rho<1/3$. Here the output is conditioned on its classical execution transcript: for any unit representative $\psi$ of its ray, there exists $\omega\in\mathbb C$, $|\omega|=1$, such that $\|\omega\psi-A^+|b\rangle/\|A^+|b\rangle\|\|\le\epsilon$. This terminal-state phase convention does not change any coherent stage, block-encoding, or controlled-operation phase specified by the access contract.

For the prescribed precision schedule and least admissible OP1A degree bounds just specified, the query bound is $O\!\left(d\kappa\,\operatorname{poly}\!\left(\log\frac{d\kappa}{\epsilon},\log\frac1\rho\right)\right)$ calls in each declared row-location, reverse-location, value, and input-preparation query coordinate; inverse and coherent forms retain their separate coordinates. A construction-cap exhaustion returns its declared timeout and is not included in this success guarantee. If the support of $|b\rangle$ has the smaller condition number $\kappa'<\kappa$, $\kappa$ may be replaced by $\kappa'$. The output is a quantum state; no classical coordinate list is promised.

The separate gate-efficient conclusion holds only under this explicit gate specialization: every required forward, inverse and controlled form of $B$, row-location, reverse-location, value access, and the $\widetilde A/d$ block encoding has a uniform circuit using at most $g_0=\operatorname{polylog}(N,d,\kappa,1/\epsilon,1/\rho)$ gates per call; state preparation, selected/input reflections, reversible clock predicates, dilution rotations, and the final zero-work instrument and controlled reflections also use at most $g_0$ gates per invocation; and each QA25 simulation at time $t$ and clean-input error $\xi$ has a uniform circuit using $O((d|t|+\log(1/\xi))g_0)$ gates, with the same bound for every required controlled or inverse form. The QFTs, reversible phase comparisons and majority circuits, and efficient-grid rounding circuits used by the probability estimator must also have uniform polylogarithmic gate counts at every allowed scale. A uniform phase compiler must implement each QSVT phase within its allocated error using at most $g_0$ gates. Under these conditions the total quantum gate count is $O(d\kappa\,\operatorname{polylog}(N,d,\kappa,1/\epsilon,1/\rho))$. Query bounds remain separate from these gate bounds. Classical polynomial/phase generation, exact algebraic comparison, median/schedule arithmetic, arithmetic bit implementation and compiler construction costs remain separate coordinates; no polylogarithmic total bit-time bound is inferred.

proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $A$ be an $N\times N$ Hermitian matrix with at most $d$ nonzero entries in each row, $\|A\|_{\rm op}\le1$, supplied with the full sparse access model of [[def-qa-27-cks-sparse-oracle-model]]. Its finite-precision values must decode to a Hermitian $\widetilde A$ with certified $\|A-\widetilde A\|_{\rm op}\le\epsilon_{\rm val}$, and the exact QA25 encoding and simulator-call certificates must satisfy the budgets in [[alg-qa-27-cks-variable-time-linear-solver]]. Let $|b\rangle$ be a normalized state supported on eigenvalues with $|\lambda|\ge1/\kappa$ for declared $\kappa\ge1$, prepared by a supplied clean-work unitary $B$. For targets $0<\epsilon<1$ and $0<\rho<1/3$, execute the constructor at supplied rationals $\epsilon/2<e\le\epsilon$ and $\rho/2<\beta\le\rho$, with access and construction certificates for these requests. The uncapped `efficient-qsvt` constructor, or a finite-cap construction that completes its certificates, outputs with probability at least $1-\rho$ a conditional pure system state admitting a unit representative within vector-norm error $\epsilon$ of $A^+|b\rangle/\|A^+|b\rangle\|$, for every fixed $0<\rho<1/3$. Here the output is conditioned on its classical execution transcript: for any unit representative $\psi$ of its ray, there exists $\omega\in\mathbb C$, $|\omega|=1$, such that $\|\omega\psi-A^+|b\rangle/\|A^+|b\rangle\|\|\le\epsilon$. This terminal-state phase convention does not change any coherent stage, block-encoding, or controlled-operation phase specified by the access contract.

For the prescribed precision schedule and least admissible OP1A degree bounds just specified, the query bound is $O\!\left(d\kappa\,\operatorname{poly}\!\left(\log\frac{d\kappa}{\epsilon},\log\frac1\rho\right)\right)$ calls in each declared row-location, reverse-location, value, and input-preparation query coordinate; inverse and coherent forms retain their separate coordinates. A construction-cap exhaustion returns its declared timeout and is not included in this success guarantee. If the support of $|b\rangle$ has the smaller condition number $\kappa'<\kappa$, $\kappa$ may be replaced by $\kappa'$. The output is a quantum state; no classical coordinate list is promised.

The separate gate-efficient conclusion holds only under this explicit gate specialization: every required forward, inverse and controlled form of $B$, row-location, reverse-location, value access, and the $\widetilde A/d$ block encoding has a uniform circuit using at most $g_0=\operatorname{polylog}(N,d,\kappa,1/\epsilon,1/\rho)$ gates per call; state preparation, selected/input reflections, reversible clock predicates, dilution rotations, and the final zero-work instrument and controlled reflections also use at most $g_0$ gates per invocation; and each QA25 simulation at time $t$ and clean-input error $\xi$ has a uniform circuit using $O((d|t|+\log(1/\xi))g_0)$ gates, with the same bound for every required controlled or inverse form. The QFTs, reversible phase comparisons and majority circuits, and efficient-grid rounding circuits used by the probability estimator must also have uniform polylogarithmic gate counts at every allowed scale. A uniform phase compiler must implement each QSVT phase within its allocated error using at most $g_0$ gates. Under these conditions the total quantum gate count is $O(d\kappa\,\operatorname{polylog}(N,d,\kappa,1/\epsilon,1/\rho))$. Query bounds remain separate from these gate bounds. Classical polynomial/phase generation, exact algebraic comparison, median/schedule arithmetic, arithmetic bit implementation and compiler construction costs remain separate coordinates; no polylogarithmic total bit-time bound is inferred.

**Input.** A coherent finite sampler $V$ whose decoded real output $v$ has finite range, a known rational upper bound $\sigma\ge0$ with $\operatorname{Var}(v)\le\sigma^2$, rational target $\varepsilon>0$, and rational desired failure probability $0<\rho<1$. All sample, value, inverse, controlled, predicate, and rotation circuits are explicit inputs with separately recorded costs. [[lem-qa-29-coherent-sampler-outcome-law]] identifies the distribution of each measured output with the sampler law. Every observable supplied to $\operatorname{PositiveMean}$ is computed on fresh executions of $V$ using its explicitly supplied, costed value, predicate, rotation, inverse, and controlled operations. For an observable depending on a previously measured classical value, the input supplies the corresponding circuits for each admissible value and charges their selection or computation; the measured value is held fixed while those circuits are used.

If $\sigma=0$, measure one fresh output and return it. Otherwise set $\varepsilon'=\min(\varepsilon,\sigma/2)$ and reserve $\varepsilon_0=7\varepsilon'/8$ for the ideal estimator. Define the following finite routine for any nonnegative finite-valued output $h$ and rational parameters $a,\rho_1$ with $0<a<1/2$ and $0<\rho_1<1$:

1. Let $k$ be the least nonnegative integer with $2^ka\ge1$, and let $M=2^m$ be the least power of two, with $m\ge0$ an integer, for which $M^2a^2\ge10^6k$. Their exact rational searches terminate by [[lem-qa-29-dyadic-parameters-terminate]]. Moreover $k\ge2$ because $2a<1$; since $Ma\ge0$ and $(Ma)^2\ge10^6k$, [[thm-of-square-roots]] and [[lem-of-square-monotone]] give $Ma\ge1000\sqrt{k}$, hence $M\ge1000\sqrt{k}/a>2000$.
2. For $\ell=0$, define $h_0=h\mathbf1_{[0,1)}$. For $1\le\ell\le k$, define $h_\ell=2^{-\ell}h\mathbf1_{[2^{\ell-1},2^\ell)}$. Each $h_\ell$ lies in $[0,1)$.
3. Since $M>2000$, the target $\eta_M=88/(7M)$ satisfies $0<\eta_M<1$ and $M\ge4$. For each $\ell=0,\ldots,k$, run [[alg-qa-29-quantum-expectation-estimation]] on $h_\ell$ over $[0,1]$ with target $\eta_M$ and failure probability $1/[10(k+1)]$. This selects phase-register size exactly $M$ under the current QA13 interface. Call the result $u_\ell$ and form $P(h)=u_0+\sum_{\ell=1}^k2^\ell u_\ell$.
4. Repeat this whole binned procedure an odd number $R_1$ of fresh independent circuit executions, as required by [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]], where $R_1$ is the least odd positive integer at least $\lceil2U_1/(3/10)^2\rceil+1$. Here $U_1$ is the upper endpoint of the certified logarithm interval for $\ln(1/\rho_1)$ from [[lem-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-series]], computed with interval width at most $1/4$. Return the median. This defines $\operatorname{PositiveMean}(h,a,\rho_1)$ for $0<\rho_1<1$.

For one outer trial, measure one fresh sampler output $v_0$ and set $m=v_0/\sigma$. Holding this coarse value fixed, let $Y=v_1/\sigma$ be the normalized output of a new sampler execution independent of the coarse measurement and define
$$B_m(Y)=Y-m,\qquad h_{-,m}(Y)=(-B_m(Y))\mathbf1_{B_m(Y)<0}/4,\qquad h_{+,m}(Y)=B_m(Y)\mathbf1_{B_m(Y)\ge0}/4.$$
Run $\operatorname{PositiveMean}$ separately on $h_{-,m}$ and $h_{+,m}$ with $a=\varepsilon_0/(32\sigma)$ and $\rho_1=1/9$, using fresh sampler executions independent of the coarse measurement and of the other call, conditional on the fixed $m$. If the results are $u_-,u_+$, return $\sigma(m-4u_-+4u_+)$. Count the coarse state preparation and all fresh preparations used by both $\operatorname{PositiveMean}$ calls in the total preparation count; every controlled or inverse call remains separately charged. Let $U_0$ be the upper endpoint of the certified logarithm interval for $\ln(1/\rho)$ from [[lem-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-series]], computed with interval width at most $1/4$. Repeat the outer trial an odd number $R_0$ of fresh independent circuit executions, as required by [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]], where $R_0$ is the least odd positive integer at least $\lceil18U_0\rceil+1$, and output the median.

Here $\ln$ is the natural logarithm from [[def-natural-logarithm]]. Its rational subroutine uses [[lem-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-series]] with tail at most $1/8$, yielding an interval of width at most $1/4$; every ceiling uses the interval's upper endpoint. The procedure is a finite sequence of operations in the supplied exact-access model, and the accuracy theorem assumes exact value, predicate, rotation, and reflection operations. It makes no guarantee for approximate replacements: any finite-gate implementation needs a separate certified error analysis that transfers both output accuracy and success probability, with compilation, gate, precision, bit, and ancilla costs recorded. No state reflection or value-loading operation is free.

$$S_N(x):=2\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{y^{2j+1}}{2j+1},\qquad T_N(x):=\frac{2|y|^{2N+1}}{(2N+1)(1-y^2)}.$$

items.title: Finite expectation-estimation task
items.statement:
A **finite expectation-estimation task** consists of a nonempty finite set $X$, a probability law $p:X\to[0,1]$ with $\sum_{x\in X}p_x=1$, and an exactly encoded real-valued function $g:X\to[a,b]$, where $a\le b$ are finite rationals. Its target is
$$\mu:=\mathbb E_p[g]=\sum_{x\in X}p_xg(x).$$

For rational parameters $\varepsilon>0$ and $0<\delta<1$, an $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ estimator is a randomized or quantum procedure that outputs a real number $\widetilde\mu$ satisfying
$$\Pr\bigl(|\widetilde\mu-\mu|\le\varepsilon\bigr)\ge1-\delta.$$
The task specifies the target law and success event only. A particular procedure must state how it accesses samples or coherent state preparation and must charge those resources separately.

A value that approximates an underlying real-valued observable to error $\tau$ defines a different task with target $\mathbb E_p[\widetilde g]$; any claim about $\mathbb E_p[g]$ must add the encoding error $\tau$ to its error budget.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Sections 1–2
C. M. Grinstead and J. L. Snell, Introduction to Probability, 2nd ed., Sections 1.2 and 6.1

items.title: One-sided concentration bound for independent median trials
items.statement:
Let $R\ge1$ be an integer, let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_R$ be independent Bernoulli random variables on a finite probability space with $\mathbb E[Z_i]\le p<1/2$, and put $S=\sum_{i=1}^RZ_i$. For every $t\ge0$,
$$\Pr(S-\mathbb E S\ge t)\le e^{-2t^2/R}.$$
Consequently, let $R$ be odd and let $T_1,\ldots,T_R$ be independent finite-valued real estimates on a finite probability space. If $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an interval and $\Pr(T_i\in I)\ge1-p$ for every $i$, then their median (the middle order statistic) lies in $I$ except with probability at most
$$\exp\bigl(-2R(1/2-p)^2\bigr).$$

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Lemma 1 and Theorems 3 and 5
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; only a finite family of independent Bernoulli variables is considered.

items.title: A terminating rational enclosure for the natural logarithm
items.statement:
For a rational $x>0$, put $y=(x-1)/(x+1)$. For each integer $N\ge1$, define the rational partial sum and remainder bound
$$S_N(x):=2\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{y^{2j+1}}{2j+1},\qquad T_N(x):=\frac{2|y|^{2N+1}}{(2N+1)(1-y^2)}.$$
Then $|y|<1$ and
$$|\ln x-S_N(x)|\le T_N(x).$$
For every rational tolerance $\tau>0$, the procedure that increases $N=1,2,\ldots$ until $T_N(x)\le\tau$ terminates using rational comparisons. It returns the certified interval $[S_N(x)-T_N(x),S_N(x)+T_N(x)]$, whose width is at most $2\tau$ and which contains $\ln x$.

references.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.100B Real Analysis, Spring 2025 full lecture notes
J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I, Logarithm and Exponential

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the construction uses finite rational arithmetic and a terminating natural-number search.

items.title: Finite termination of the dyadic estimator parameter searches
items.statement:
Let $a>0$ and $C>0$ be rational and let $k\ge1$ be an integer. Each of the following exact rational searches terminates:

1. increase an integer $j\ge0$ until $2^j a\ge1$;
2. after fixing $k$, increase an integer $m\ge0$ until $2^{2m}a^2\ge Ck$.

The first successful exponent is the least one satisfying its comparison. The second returns the least power of two $M=2^m$ with $M^2a^2\ge Ck$.

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I
T. Tao, Analysis I, 3rd ed.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the witnesses are obtained by one Archimedean bound and a finite search.

items.title: Classical bounded-sample mean baseline
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite real random variable taking values in a finite interval $[a,b]$ with $a\le b$, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent copies of $G$, with $n\ge1$. For $\overline X_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$ and $\mu=\mathbb E[G]$,
$$\mathbb E[\overline X_n]=\mu,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(\overline X_n)=\frac{\operatorname{Var}(G)}{n}\le\frac{(b-a)^2}{4n}.$$
Consequently, for every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$\Pr(|\overline X_n-\mu|>\varepsilon)\le\frac{(b-a)^2}{4n\varepsilon^2}.$$
The procedure uses exactly $n$ independent samples. If each draw and data load costs $C_{\rm draw}$ and $C_{\rm load}$, their total is $n(C_{\rm draw}+C_{\rm load})$; arithmetic for the encoded values is an additional separately charged cost. When $a=b$, every sample equals $\mu=a$ and the failure probability is zero.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Section 1
C. M. Grinstead and J. L. Snell, Introduction to Probability, 2nd ed., Sections 1.2 and 6.1
J. Matoušek and J. Vondrák, The Probabilistic Method, Lemma 5.1.3

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; only finite sums, finite samples, and their declared independence occur.

items.title: Uniform counting is finite indicator expectation
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set with $p_x=1/|X|$ for each $x$, let $S\subseteq X$, and define $g(x)=1$ for $x\in S$ and $g(x)=0$ otherwise. Then the expectation task for $(X,p,g)$ has target
$$\mu=\mathbb E[g]=\frac{|S|}{|X|}.$$

references.title: Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Section 4
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the sample space and all sums are finite.

items.title: Coherent finite sampler and observable value
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_{x\in X}p_x=1$, and let the value register contain an exact finite encoding of a real function $g:X\to[a,b]$, where $a\le b$ are finite rationals. A **coherent finite sampler** for $(X,p,g)$ is an explicitly supplied finite-dimensional unitary $V$ on ordered sample, value, and work registers such that
$$V|0\rangle=\sum_{x\in X}\sqrt{p_x}\,|x\rangle|g(x)\rangle|w_x\rangle,$$
where the sample labels $|x\rangle$ are distinct computational-basis vectors and each work state $|w_x\rangle$ has norm one. Zero-probability labels may occur and need no special branch. The registers and their order use [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] and [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]; each output is a pure state in the sense of [[def-qc-pure-state-and-ray]]. The separate item [[lem-qa-29-coherent-sampler-outcome-law]] verifies the induced measurement law.

The access contract lists the actual circuits or oracle interfaces for $V$, $V^\dagger$, controlled $V$ and controlled $V^\dagger$, value decoding, reversible arithmetic, any coherent predicate and controlled rotation, and the reflections used by the chosen estimator. Their availability is explicit under [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]]. A forward unitary alone does not grant an inverse or a controlled call.

The resource record follows [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]: charge state preparation, inverse and controlled access, data loading, value comparison and arithmetic, controlled-rotation synthesis and precision, good-state and initial-state reflections, gates, width, ancillas, and classical postprocessing separately. The state-preparation circuit and its costs are inputs; a state description is not a free QRAM or preparation oracle.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Sections 2–3
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

items.title: Measurement law of a coherent sampler
items.statement: For a coherent sampler $V$ with output state $|\psi\rangle=\sum_x\sqrt{p_x}|x\rangle|g(x)\rangle|w_x\rangle$ as in [[def-qa-29-coherent-sampler]], projective measurement of the sample register returns $x$ with probability $p_x$. If the value register is measured too, the pair $(x,g(x))$ has the same probability. The work register is not required to be measured, and work states for different labels need not be orthogonal.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Sections 2–3
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Sections 2.1–2.3
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3: Foundations II: Measurement and Evolution

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the proof uses finite orthonormal bases and finite sums.

items.title: Quantum counting as an expectation special case
items.statement:
**Input.** A Boolean domain $X=\{0,1\}^n$ with $N=2^n$, a predicate $f:X\to\{0,1\}$, a phase-register size $M=2^m$ for an integer $m\ge2$ (so $M\ge4$), and the uniform coherent access and controlled membership reflection required by [[alg-qa-13-counting-from-amplitude-estimation]]. Let $S=\{x:f(x)=1\}$.

Use the unchanged QA13 counting estimator [[alg-qa-13-counting-from-amplitude-estimation]] with this $M$ and its supplied access model, and return its real-valued count estimate. Do not round to an integer unless that additional postprocessing and its cost are explicitly requested. By [[thm-qa-29-counting-is-indicator-expectation]], this is the QA29 expectation task for the uniform law and observable $g=\mathbf 1_S$; the applicable counting guarantee is [[thm-qa-13-counting-error-guarantee]], whose phase-size hypothesis $M\ge4$ is met. This item defines no second amplitude-estimation or counting routine.

references.title: Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Section 4
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

items.title: Amplitude-estimation expectation estimator
items.statement:
**Input.** A finite expectation-estimation task with an exact encoded observable $g:X\to[a,b]$, a coherent sampler $V$ for its law, rational target $\varepsilon>0$, and rational failure probability $0<\delta<1$. For $a<b$, require $\varepsilon\le b-a$. The supplied access model must include every forward, inverse, controlled, value, predicate, and reflection operation that the chosen QA13 amplitude-estimation circuit invokes.

If $a=b$, return $a$. Otherwise compute the exact affine value
$$q(x)=\frac{g(x)-a}{b-a}\in[0,1].$$
Append a good flag to the coherent sampler. Reversibly compute $q(x)$ in the declared value workspace, apply the supplied one-qubit rotation
$$|0\rangle\longmapsto\sqrt{1-q(x)}|0\rangle+\sqrt{q(x)}|1\rangle$$
controlled by the sample/value registers, and uncompute all scratch used only for $q$. Let $A_q$ denote the resulting state-preparation unitary, including $V$ and the controlled rotation; let $P_{\rm good}$ project onto flag $|1\rangle$. Run the unchanged median-confidence estimator [[alg-qa-13-median-confidence-estimation]] on $(A_q,P_{\rm good})$ with amplitude tolerance $\eta=\varepsilon/(b-a)$ and failure probability $\delta$, and call its estimate $\widetilde q$. Return
$$\widetilde\mu=a+(b-a)\widetilde q.$$

For $a=b$, the exact-return branch has no quantum call. When $a<b$, the input is a costed finite circuit/oracle description. Charge each use of $A_q$, $A_q^\dagger$, controlled versions, the good and initial-state reflections, value decoding, reversible arithmetic and uncomputation, the controlled rotation and its precision, phase estimation, state preparation, gates, width, ancillas, and classical output processing according to [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. No operation is free because it is described by the law $p$ or observable $g$.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Theorem 3
Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Section 4
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

items.title: Variance-aware quantum Monte Carlo
items.statement:
**Input.** A coherent finite sampler $V$ whose decoded real output $v$ has finite range, a known rational upper bound $\sigma\ge0$ with $\operatorname{Var}(v)\le\sigma^2$, rational target $\varepsilon>0$, and rational desired failure probability $0<\rho<1$. All sample, value, inverse, controlled, predicate, and rotation circuits are explicit inputs with separately recorded costs. [[lem-qa-29-coherent-sampler-outcome-law]] identifies the distribution of each measured output with the sampler law. Every observable supplied to $\operatorname{PositiveMean}$ is computed on fresh executions of $V$ using its explicitly supplied, costed value, predicate, rotation, inverse, and controlled operations. For an observable depending on a previously measured classical value, the input supplies the corresponding circuits for each admissible value and charges their selection or computation; the measured value is held fixed while those circuits are used.

If $\sigma=0$, measure one fresh output and return it. Otherwise set $\varepsilon'=\min(\varepsilon,\sigma/2)$ and reserve $\varepsilon_0=7\varepsilon'/8$ for the ideal estimator. Define the following finite routine for any nonnegative finite-valued output $h$ and rational parameters $a,\rho_1$ with $0<a<1/2$ and $0<\rho_1<1$:

1. Let $k$ be the least nonnegative integer with $2^ka\ge1$, and let $M=2^m$ be the least power of two, with $m\ge0$ an integer, for which $M^2a^2\ge10^6k$. Their exact rational searches terminate by [[lem-qa-29-dyadic-parameters-terminate]]. Moreover $k\ge2$ because $2a<1$; since $Ma\ge0$ and $(Ma)^2\ge10^6k$, [[thm-of-square-roots]] and [[lem-of-square-monotone]] give $Ma\ge1000\sqrt{k}$, hence $M\ge1000\sqrt{k}/a>2000$.
2. For $\ell=0$, define $h_0=h\mathbf1_{[0,1)}$. For $1\le\ell\le k$, define $h_\ell=2^{-\ell}h\mathbf1_{[2^{\ell-1},2^\ell)}$. Each $h_\ell$ lies in $[0,1)$.
3. Since $M>2000$, the target $\eta_M=88/(7M)$ satisfies $0<\eta_M<1$ and $M\ge4$. For each $\ell=0,\ldots,k$, run [[alg-qa-29-quantum-expectation-estimation]] on $h_\ell$ over $[0,1]$ with target $\eta_M$ and failure probability $1/[10(k+1)]$. This selects phase-register size exactly $M$ under the current QA13 interface. Call the result $u_\ell$ and form $P(h)=u_0+\sum_{\ell=1}^k2^\ell u_\ell$.
4. Repeat this whole binned procedure an odd number $R_1$ of fresh independent circuit executions, as required by [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]], where $R_1$ is the least odd positive integer at least $\lceil2U_1/(3/10)^2\rceil+1$. Here $U_1$ is the upper endpoint of the certified logarithm interval for $\ln(1/\rho_1)$ from [[lem-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-series]], computed with interval width at most $1/4$. Return the median. This defines $\operatorname{PositiveMean}(h,a,\rho_1)$ for $0<\rho_1<1$.

For one outer trial, measure one fresh sampler output $v_0$ and set $m=v_0/\sigma$. Holding this coarse value fixed, let $Y=v_1/\sigma$ be the normalized output of a new sampler execution independent of the coarse measurement and define
$$B_m(Y)=Y-m,\qquad h_{-,m}(Y)=(-B_m(Y))\mathbf1_{B_m(Y)<0}/4,\qquad h_{+,m}(Y)=B_m(Y)\mathbf1_{B_m(Y)\ge0}/4.$$
Run $\operatorname{PositiveMean}$ separately on $h_{-,m}$ and $h_{+,m}$ with $a=\varepsilon_0/(32\sigma)$ and $\rho_1=1/9$, using fresh sampler executions independent of the coarse measurement and of the other call, conditional on the fixed $m$. If the results are $u_-,u_+$, return $\sigma(m-4u_-+4u_+)$. Count the coarse state preparation and all fresh preparations used by both $\operatorname{PositiveMean}$ calls in the total preparation count; every controlled or inverse call remains separately charged. Let $U_0$ be the upper endpoint of the certified logarithm interval for $\ln(1/\rho)$ from [[lem-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-series]], computed with interval width at most $1/4$. Repeat the outer trial an odd number $R_0$ of fresh independent circuit executions, as required by [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]], where $R_0$ is the least odd positive integer at least $\lceil18U_0\rceil+1$, and output the median.

Here $\ln$ is the natural logarithm from [[def-natural-logarithm]]. Its rational subroutine uses [[lem-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-series]] with tail at most $1/8$, yielding an interval of width at most $1/4$; every ceiling uses the interval's upper endpoint. The procedure is a finite sequence of operations in the supplied exact-access model, and the accuracy theorem assumes exact value, predicate, rotation, and reflection operations. It makes no guarantee for approximate replacements: any finite-gate implementation needs a separate certified error analysis that transfers both output accuracy and success probability, with compilation, gate, precision, bit, and ancilla costs recorded. No state reflection or value-loading operation is free.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Algorithms 1–3 and Theorems 3 and 5
Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Section 4

items.title: Quantum bounded-expectation guarantee and query cost
items.statement:
Let $g:X\to[a,b]$ be exactly encoded with $a\le b$, let $V$ be the coherent sampler of [[def-qa-29-coherent-sampler]], and let $\mu=\sum_xp_xg(x)$. If $a=b$, the algorithm [[alg-qa-29-quantum-expectation-estimation]] returns $a=\mu$ exactly. If $a<b$, then for rational $0<\varepsilon\le b-a$ and $0<\delta<1$ it returns $\widetilde\mu$ with $|\widetilde\mu-\mu|\le\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-\delta$. Writing $q=(\mu-a)/(b-a)$ and $M$ for its QA13 phase-register size, the median output also obeys
$$|\widetilde\mu-\mu|\le(b-a)\left(\frac{2\pi\sqrt{q(1-q)}}{M}+\frac{\pi^2}{M^2}\right)$$
with probability at least $1-\delta$ in either declared QA13 access mode. For $a<b$, in repeated controlled-$Q$ access it uses exactly $r(M-1)$ controlled-Grover calls, where $M$ and $r$ are the current QA13 median-interface parameters. In this mode its controlled-sampler/reflection query count is $O\bigl((b-a)\varepsilon^{-1}(1+\ln(1/\delta))\bigr)$ for all $0<\delta<1$, and $O\bigl((b-a)\varepsilon^{-1}\ln(1/\delta)\bigr)$ when $0<\delta\le1/2$. If $a=b$, the algorithm returns $a$ exactly with no quantum query.

For $a<b$, in supplied controlled-power access it instead uses exactly $rm$ controlled-power queries, where $M=2^m$; sum their separately declared costs over all $r$ runs. No $M-1$ constituent-call expansion is inferred for a supplied power.

The query bound is an oracle statement. Every controlled or inverse sampler call, good-state reflection, initial-state reflection, rotation, arithmetic operation, state preparation, and classical order-statistic computation retains its separately supplied cost.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Theorem 3
Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Theorem 12
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

items.title: Dyadic positive-mean estimator under an L2 bound
items.statement:
Let $h$ be a nonnegative finite-valued output of a coherent sampler, $s=\|h\|_2=(\mathbb E[h^2])^{1/2}$, and let $a,\rho_1$ be rational with $0<a<1/2$ and $0<\rho_1<1$. Let $\operatorname{PositiveMean}(h,a,\rho_1)$ be the subroutine defined in [[alg-qa-29-variance-aware-monte-carlo]]. Its output $u$ satisfies
$$|u-\mathbb E[h]|\le a(1+s)^2$$
with probability at least $1-\rho_1$. For $k=\lceil\log_2(1/a)\rceil$, its calls use
$$O\bigl(k\ln(k+1)(1+\ln(1/\rho_1))\bigr)$$
prepared output-state copies and
$$O\bigl(a^{-1}k^{3/2}\ln(k+1)(1+\ln(1/\rho_1))\bigr)$$
uses of the supplied state reflection when its binned QAE calls use repeated controlled-$Q$ access. The accuracy and prepared-copy bounds also hold in supplied controlled-power access; in that mode sum the separately declared power-query costs rather than infer this reflection count. All input access, band comparison, value arithmetic, controlled rotation, and finite-precision costs remain separately charged.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Algorithm 2 and Lemma 4
Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Theorem 12

items.title: Variance-aware quantum Monte Carlo guarantee
items.statement:
Let $v$ be the finite-valued real output of a coherent sampler with $\operatorname{Var}(v)\le\sigma^2$ for a known rational $\sigma\ge0$, and let rational $\varepsilon>0$. For each rational $0<\rho<1$, the algorithm [[alg-qa-29-variance-aware-monte-carlo]] returns $\widetilde\mu$ with $|\widetilde\mu-\mathbb E[v]|\le\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-\rho$. If $\sigma=0$, it returns the exact mean after one output preparation. For $\sigma>0$, put $z=\sigma/\varepsilon$ and $L=\max(2,z)$. In the exact coherent-access model, its resource counts are
$$O\!\left((1+\ln(1/\rho))\ln L\,\ln\ln(e^e+L)\right)$$
output-state preparations and
$$O\!\left((1+\ln(1/\rho))L(\ln L)^{3/2}\ln\ln(e^e+L)\right)$$
uses of the supplied state reflection in repeated controlled-$Q$ access, up to universal constants. Accuracy and the preparation bound hold in either declared access mode; in supplied controlled-power access sum the separately declared power costs instead of applying this reflection bound. Each state reflection is implemented through the supplied sampler and its inverse; these bounds do not turn variance alone into coherent access. A finite-gate approximation needs a separate certified error analysis before it can inherit this theorem.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Algorithm 3 and Theorem 5
Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Theorem 12

items.title: Coherent query-to-circuit cost translation
items.statement:
For a QA29 execution, group its complete value-rotated sampler preparations into the distinct supplied unitaries $A_j$, and let $N_j$ be the number of fresh standalone preparations of $A_j$ and $Q_j$ the number of controlled Grover rounds using it. Also let $V_t$ range over the supplied unrotated sampler preparations used for coarse measurements, with $N_t^0$ such fresh preparations. If each controlled Grover round for $A_j$ is the explicit product of one controlled $A_j$ call, one controlled $A_j^\dagger$ call, one controlled initial-state reflection, one controlled good-state reflection, and its control phase, then the exact primitive-call cost is
$$\sum_jN_jC_{A_j,\rm prep}+\sum_tN_t^0C_{V_t,\rm prep}+\sum_jQ_j(C_{A_j,c}+C_{A_j^\dagger,c}+C_{S_{0,j},c}+C_{S_{{\rm good},j},c}+C_{{\rm phase},j}),$$
where every $C$ is the declared cost of that operation. The preparation counts exclude the controlled $A_j$ and $A_j^\dagger$ occurrences inside Grover rounds, which are already included in the $Q_j$ terms. With a single $A_q$, no unrotated coarse preparations, and $N_{\rm prep}=N_q$, this reduces to the homogeneous formula $N_{\rm prep}C_{A_q,\rm prep}+Q(C_{A_q,c}+C_{A_q^\dagger,c}+C_{S_0,c}+C_{S_{\rm good},c}+C_{\rm phase})$. Value decoding, band comparisons, reversible arithmetic, controlled rotations, uncomputation, phase estimation, ancilla workspace, circuit description, and classical output/median computations add their own declared gate, width, bit, or oracle costs. If a complete reflection is instead supplied as a named oracle, charge that oracle's declared cost separately and do not also expand it into its components. No bare query bound becomes a gate bound without these implementations.

references.title: Gilles Brassard, Peter Høyer, Michele Mosca, and Alain Tapp, Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation, Section 4
Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Theorems 3 and 5

proposed_after_items.title: Finite expectation-estimation task
proposed_after_items.statement:
A **finite expectation-estimation task** consists of a nonempty finite set $X$, a probability law $p:X\to[0,1]$ with $\sum_{x\in X}p_x=1$, and an exactly encoded real-valued function $g:X\to[a,b]$, where $a\le b$ are finite rationals. Its target is
$$\mu:=\mathbb E_p[g]=\sum_{x\in X}p_xg(x).$$

For rational parameters $\varepsilon>0$ and $0<\delta<1$, an $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ estimator is a randomized or quantum procedure that outputs a real number $\widetilde\mu$ satisfying
$$\Pr\bigl(|\widetilde\mu-\mu|\le\varepsilon\bigr)\ge1-\delta.$$
The task specifies the target law and success event only. A particular procedure must state how it accesses samples or coherent state preparation and must charge those resources separately.

A value that approximates an underlying real-valued observable to error $\tau$ defines a different task with target $\mathbb E_p[\widetilde g]$; any claim about $\mathbb E_p[g]$ must add the encoding error $\tau$ to its error budget.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Sections 1–2
C. M. Grinstead and J. L. Snell, Introduction to Probability, 2nd ed., Sections 1.2 and 6.1

proposed_after_items.title: One-sided concentration bound for independent median trials
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $R\ge1$ be an integer, let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_R$ be independent Bernoulli random variables on a finite probability space with $\mathbb E[Z_i]\le p<1/2$, and put $S=\sum_{i=1}^RZ_i$. For every $t\ge0$,
$$\Pr(S-\mathbb E S\ge t)\le e^{-2t^2/R}.$$
Consequently, let $R$ be odd and let $T_1,\ldots,T_R$ be independent finite-valued real estimates on a finite probability space. If $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an interval and $\Pr(T_i\in I)\ge1-p$ for every $i$, then their median (the middle order statistic) lies in $I$ except with probability at most
$$\exp\bigl(-2R(1/2-p)^2\bigr).$$

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Lemma 1 and Theorems 3 and 5
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

proposed_after_items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; only a finite family of independent Bernoulli variables is considered.

proposed_after_items.title: Rational natural-logarithm enclosure search

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I, Section 5.4.1 (analytic logarithm interface)

proposed_after_items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; each iteration uses exact rational arithmetic.
proposed_after_items.statement:
**Input.** Rational numbers $x>0$ and $\tau>0$. **Output.** A positive integer $N$ and a rational interval $[L,U]$.

Compute $y=(x-1)/(x+1)$ and initialize $N=1$. At each iteration compute, by exact rational arithmetic,
$$S_N=2\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{y^{2j+1}}{2j+1},\qquad T_N=\frac{2|y|^{2N+1}}{(2N+1)(1-y^2)}.$$
If $T_N\le\tau$, return $N$ and $[L,U]=[S_N-T_N,S_N+T_N]$. Otherwise replace $N$ by $N+1$ and repeat. Each comparison is an exact rational comparison. Arithmetic and integer bit costs are charged separately; no running-time bound is part of this definition.

proposed_after_items.title: A terminating rational enclosure for the natural logarithm
proposed_after_items.statement:
For a rational $x>0$, put $y=(x-1)/(x+1)$. For each integer $N\ge1$, define the rational partial sum and remainder bound
$$S_N(x):=2\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{y^{2j+1}}{2j+1},\qquad T_N(x):=\frac{2|y|^{2N+1}}{(2N+1)(1-y^2)}.$$
Then $|y|<1$ and
$$|\ln x-S_N(x)|\le T_N(x).$$
For every rational tolerance $\tau>0$, the algorithm [[alg-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-enclosure]] terminates using rational comparisons. It returns the certified interval $[S_N(x)-T_N(x),S_N(x)+T_N(x)]$, whose width is at most $2\tau$ and which contains $\ln x$.

references.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.100B Real Analysis, Spring 2025 full lecture notes
J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I, Logarithm and Exponential

proposed_after_items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the construction uses finite rational arithmetic and a terminating natural-number search.

proposed_after_items.title: Finite termination of the dyadic estimator parameter searches
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $a>0$ and $C>0$ be rational and let $k\ge1$ be an integer. Each of the following exact rational searches terminates:

1. increase an integer $j\ge0$ until $2^j a\ge1$;
2. after fixing $k$, increase an integer $m\ge0$ until $2^{2m}a^2\ge Ck$.

The first successful exponent is the least one satisfying its comparison. The second returns the least power of two $M=2^m$ with $M^2a^2\ge Ck$.

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I
T. Tao, Analysis I, 3rd ed.

proposed_after_items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the witnesses are obtained by one Archimedean bound and a finite search.

proposed_after_items.title: Classical bounded-sample mean baseline
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite real random variable taking values in a finite interval $[a,b]$ with $a\le b$, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent copies of $G$, with $n\ge1$. For $\overline X_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$ and $\mu=\mathbb E[G]$,
$$\mathbb E[\overline X_n]=\mu,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(\overline X_n)=\frac{\operatorname{Var}(G)}{n}\le\frac{(b-a)^2}{4n}.$$
Consequently, for every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$\Pr(|\overline X_n-\mu|>\varepsilon)\le\frac{(b-a)^2}{4n\varepsilon^2}.$$
The procedure uses exactly $n$ independent samples. If each draw and data load costs $C_{\rm draw}$ and $C_{\rm load}$, their total is $n(C_{\rm draw}+C_{\rm load})$; arithmetic for the encoded values is an additional separately charged cost. When $a=b$, every sample equals $\mu=a$ and the failure probability is zero.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Section 1
C. M. Grinstead and J. L. Snell, Introduction to Probability, 2nd ed., Sections 1.2 and 6.1
J. Matoušek and J. Vondrák, The Probabilistic Method, Lemma 5.1.3

proposed_after_items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; only finite sums, finite samples, and their declared independence occur.

proposed_after_items.title: Uniform counting is finite indicator expectation
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set with $p_x=1/|X|$ for each $x$, let $S\subseteq X$, and define $g(x)=1$ for $x\in S$ and $g(x)=0$ otherwise. Then the expectation task for $(X,p,g)$ has target
$$\mu=\mathbb E[g]=\frac{|S|}{|X|}.$$

Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

proposed_after_items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the sample space and all sums are finite.

proposed_after_items.title: Coherent finite sampler and observable value
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_{x\in X}p_x=1$, and let the value register contain an exact finite encoding of a real function $g:X\to[a,b]$, where $a\le b$ are finite rationals. A **coherent finite sampler** for $(X,p,g)$ is an explicitly supplied finite-dimensional unitary $V$ on ordered sample, value, and work registers such that
$$V|0\rangle=\sum_{x\in X}\sqrt{p_x}\,|x\rangle|g(x)\rangle|w_x\rangle,$$
where the sample labels $|x\rangle$ are distinct computational-basis vectors and each work state $|w_x\rangle$ has norm one. Zero-probability labels may occur and need no special branch. The registers and their order use [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] and [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]; each output is a pure state in the sense of [[def-qc-pure-state-and-ray]]. The separate item [[lem-qa-29-coherent-sampler-outcome-law]] verifies the induced measurement law.

The access contract lists the actual circuits or oracle interfaces for $V$, $V^\dagger$, controlled $V$ and controlled $V^\dagger$, value decoding, reversible arithmetic, any coherent predicate and controlled rotation, and the reflections used by the chosen estimator. Their availability is explicit under [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]]. A forward unitary alone does not grant an inverse or a controlled call.

The resource record follows [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]: charge state preparation, inverse and controlled access, data loading, value comparison and arithmetic, controlled-rotation synthesis and precision, good-state and initial-state reflections, gates, width, ancillas, and classical postprocessing separately. The state-preparation circuit and its costs are inputs; a state description is not a free QRAM or preparation oracle.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Sections 2–3
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

proposed_after_items.title: Measurement law of a coherent sampler
proposed_after_items.statement: For a coherent sampler $V$ with output state $|\psi\rangle=\sum_x\sqrt{p_x}|x\rangle|g(x)\rangle|w_x\rangle$ as in [[def-qa-29-coherent-sampler]], projective measurement of the sample register returns $x$ with probability $p_x$. If the value register is measured too, the pair $(x,g(x))$ has the same probability. The work register is not required to be measured, and work states for different labels need not be orthogonal.

references.title: Ashley Montanaro, Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods, Sections 2–3
John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Sections 2.1–2.3
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3: Foundations II: Measurement and Evolution

proposed_after_items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the proof uses finite orthonormal bases and finite sums.

proposed_after_items.title: Quantum counting as an expectation special case
proposed_after_items.statement:
**Input.** A Boolean domain $X=\{0,1\}^n$ with $N=2^n$, a predicate $f:X\to\{0,1\}$, a phase-register size $M=2^m$ for an integer $m\ge2$ (so $M\ge4$), and the uniform coherent access and controlled membership reflection required by [[alg-qa-13-counting-from-amplitude-estimation]]. Let $S=\{x:f(x)=1\}$.

Use the unchanged QA13 counting estimator [[alg-qa-13-counting-from-amplitude-estimation]] with this $M$ and its supplied access model, and return its exact algebraic fraction estimate $\widetilde\mu=\widetilde t/N=\sin^2(\pi y/M)$ for the expectation task. Its real-valued count estimate $\widetilde t=N\widetilde\mu$ may also be reported, with count and expectation outputs explicitly distinguished. Do not round to an integer unless that additional postprocessing and its cost are explicitly requested. By [[thm-qa-29-counting-is-indicator-expectation]], this is the QA29 expectation task for the uniform law and observable $g=\mathbf 1_S$; the applicable count guarantee is [[thm-qa-13-counting-error-guarantee]], whose phase-size hypothesis $M\ge4$ is met. Divide its count-error radius by $N$ for the expectation-error radius, with the same success event and probability. This item defines no second amplitude-estimation or counting routine.

Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Section 19.3

proposed_after_items.title: Amplitude-estimation expectation estimator
proposed_after_items.statement:
**Input.** A finite expectation-estimation task with an exact encoded observable $g:X\to[a,b]$, a coherent sampler $V$ for its law, rational target $\varepsilon>0$, and rational failure probability $0<\delta<1$. For $a<b$, require $\varepsilon\le b-a$. The supplied access model must include every forward, inverse, controlled, value, predicate, and reflection operation that the chosen QA13 amplitude-estimation circuit invokes.

If $a=b$, return $a$. Otherwise compute the exact affine value
$$q(x)=\frac{g(x)-a}{b-a}\in[0,1].$$
Append a good flag to the coherent sampler. Reversibly compute $q(x)$ in the declared value workspace, apply the supplied one-qubit rotation
$$|0\rangle\longmapsto\sqrt{1-q(x)}|0\rangle+\sqrt{q(x)}|1\rangle$$
controlled by the sample/value registers, and uncompute all scratch used only for $q$. Let $A_q$ denote the resulting state-preparation unitary, including $V$ and the controlled rotation; let $P_{\rm good}$ project onto flag $|1\rangle$. Run the unchanged median-confidence estimator [[alg-qa-13-median-confidence-estimation]] on $(A_q,P_{\rm good})$ with amplitude tolerance $\eta=\varepsilon/(b-a)$ and failure probability $\delta$, and call its estimate $\widetilde q$. Return
$$\widetilde\mu=a+(b-a)\widetilde q.$$

For $a=b$, the exact-return branch has no quantum call. When $a<b$, the input is a costed finite circuit/oracle description. Charge each use of $A_q$, $A_q^\dagger$, controlled versions, the good and initial-state reflections, value decoding, reversible arithmetic and uncomputation, the controlled rotation and its precision, phase estimation, state preparation, gates, width, ancillas, and classical output processing according to [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. No operation is free because it is described by the law $p$ or observable $g$.

proposed_after_items.title: Variance-aware quantum Monte Carlo
proposed_after_items.statement:
**Input.** A coherent finite sampler $V$ whose decoded real output $v$ has finite range, a known rational upper bound $\sigma\ge0$ with $\operatorname{Var}(v)\le\sigma^2$, rational target $\varepsilon>0$, and rational desired failure probability $0<\rho<1$. All sample, value, inverse, controlled, predicate, and rotation circuits are explicit inputs with separately recorded costs. [[lem-qa-29-coherent-sampler-outcome-law]] identifies the distribution of each measured output with the sampler law. Every observable supplied to $\operatorname{PositiveMean}$ is computed on fresh executions of $V$ using its explicitly supplied, costed value, predicate, rotation, inverse, and controlled operations. For an observable depending on a previously measured classical value, the input supplies the corresponding circuits for each admissible value and charges their selection or computation; the measured value is held fixed while those circuits are used.

If $\sigma=0$, measure one fresh output and return it. Otherwise set $\varepsilon'=\min(\varepsilon,\sigma/2)$ and reserve $\varepsilon_0=7\varepsilon'/8$ for the ideal estimator. Define the following finite routine for any nonnegative finite-valued output $h$ and rational parameters $a,\rho_1$ with $0<a<1/2$ and $0<\rho_1<1$:

1. Let $k$ be the least nonnegative integer with $2^ka\ge1$, and let $M=2^m$ be the least power of two, with $m\ge0$ an integer, for which $M^2a^2\ge10^6k$. Their exact rational searches terminate by [[lem-qa-29-dyadic-parameters-terminate]]. Moreover $k\ge2$ because $2a<1$; since $Ma\ge0$ and $(Ma)^2\ge10^6k$, [[thm-of-square-roots]] and [[lem-of-square-monotone]] give $Ma\ge1000\sqrt{k}$, hence $M\ge1000\sqrt{k}/a>2000$.
2. For $\ell=0$, define $h_0=h\mathbf1_{[0,1)}$. For $1\le\ell\le k$, define $h_\ell=2^{-\ell}h\mathbf1_{[2^{\ell-1},2^\ell)}$. Each $h_\ell$ lies in $[0,1)$.
3. Since $M>2000$, the target $\eta_M=88/(7M)$ satisfies $0<\eta_M<1$ and $M\ge4$. For each $\ell=0,\ldots,k$, run [[alg-qa-29-quantum-expectation-estimation]] on $h_\ell$ over $[0,1]$ with target $\eta_M$ and failure probability $1/[10(k+1)]$. This selects phase-register size exactly $M$ under the current QA13 interface. Call the result $u_\ell$ and form $P(h)=u_0+\sum_{\ell=1}^k2^\ell u_\ell$.
4. Repeat this whole binned procedure an odd number $R_1$ of fresh independent circuit executions, as required by [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]], where $R_1$ is the least odd positive integer at least $\lceil2U_1/(3/10)^2\rceil+1$. Here $U_1$ is the upper endpoint of the certified logarithm interval for $\ln(1/\rho_1)$ from [[lem-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-series]], computed with interval width at most $1/4$. Return the median. This defines $\operatorname{PositiveMean}(h,a,\rho_1)$ for $0<\rho_1<1$.

For one outer trial, measure one fresh sampler output $v_0$ and set $m=v_0/\sigma$. Holding this coarse value fixed, let $Y=v_1/\sigma$ be the normalized output of a new sampler execution independent of the coarse measurement and define
$$B_m(Y)=Y-m,\qquad h_{-,m}(Y)=(-B_m(Y))\mathbf1_{B_m(Y)<0}/4,\qquad h_{+,m}(Y)=B_m(Y)\mathbf1_{B_m(Y)\ge0}/4.$$
Run $\operatorname{PositiveMean}$ separately on $h_{-,m}$ and $h_{+,m}$ with $a=\varepsilon_0/(32\sigma)$ and $\rho_1=1/9$, using fresh sampler executions independent of the coarse measurement and of the other call, conditional on the fixed $m$. If the results are $u_-,u_+$, return $\sigma(m-4u_-+4u_+)$. Count the coarse state preparation and all fresh preparations used by both $\operatorname{PositiveMean}$ calls in the total preparation count; every controlled or inverse call remains separately charged. Let $U_0$ be the upper endpoint of the certified logarithm interval for $\ln(1/\rho)$ from [[lem-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-series]], computed with interval width at most $1/4$. Repeat the outer trial an odd number $R_0$ of fresh independent circuit executions, as required by [[def-qa-quantum-query-algorithm]], where $R_0$ is the least odd positive integer at least $\lceil18U_0\rceil+1$, and output the median.

Here $\ln$ is the natural logarithm from [[def-natural-logarithm]]. For each logarithm input $x=1/\rho_1$ or $x=1/\rho$, its rational subroutine runs [[alg-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-enclosure]] on $(x,1/8)$; [[lem-qa-29-certified-natural-logarithm-series]] certifies tail at most $1/8$ and interval width at most $1/4$; every ceiling uses the interval's upper endpoint. The procedure is a finite sequence of operations in the supplied exact-access model, and the accuracy theorem assumes exact value, predicate, rotation, and reflection operations. It makes no guarantee for approximate replacements: any finite-gate implementation needs a separate certified error analysis that transfers both output accuracy and success probability, with compilation, gate, precision, bit, and ancilla costs recorded. No state reflection or value-loading operation is free.

proposed_after_items.title: Quantum bounded-expectation guarantee and query cost
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $g:X\to[a,b]$ be exactly encoded with $a\le b$, let $V$ be the coherent sampler of [[def-qa-29-coherent-sampler]], and let $\mu=\sum_xp_xg(x)$. If $a=b$, the algorithm [[alg-qa-29-quantum-expectation-estimation]] returns $a=\mu$ exactly. If $a<b$, then for rational $0<\varepsilon\le b-a$ and $0<\delta<1$ it returns $\widetilde\mu$ with $|\widetilde\mu-\mu|\le\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-\delta$. Writing $q=(\mu-a)/(b-a)$ and $M$ for its QA13 phase-register size, the median output also obeys
$$|\widetilde\mu-\mu|\le(b-a)\left(\frac{2\pi\sqrt{q(1-q)}}{M}+\frac{\pi^2}{M^2}\right)$$
with probability at least $1-\delta$ in either declared QA13 access mode. For $a<b$, in repeated controlled-$Q$ access it uses exactly $r(M-1)$ controlled-Grover calls, where $M$ and $r$ are the current QA13 median-interface parameters. In this mode its controlled-sampler/reflection query count is $O\bigl((b-a)\varepsilon^{-1}(1+\ln(1/\delta))\bigr)$ for all $0<\delta<1$, and $O\bigl((b-a)\varepsilon^{-1}\ln(1/\delta)\bigr)$ when $0<\delta\le1/2$. If $a=b$, the algorithm returns $a$ exactly with no quantum query.

For $a<b$, in supplied controlled-power access it instead uses exactly $rm$ controlled-power queries, where $M=2^m$; sum their separately declared costs over all $r$ runs. No $M-1$ constituent-call expansion is inferred for a supplied power.

The query bound is an oracle statement. Every controlled or inverse sampler call, good-state reflection, initial-state reflection, rotation, arithmetic operation, state preparation, and classical order-statistic computation retains its separately supplied cost.

proposed_after_items.title: Dyadic positive-mean estimator under an L2 bound
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $h$ be a nonnegative finite-valued output of a coherent sampler, $s=\|h\|_2=(\mathbb E[h^2])^{1/2}$, and let $a,\rho_1$ be rational with $0<a<1/2$ and $0<\rho_1<1$. Let $\operatorname{PositiveMean}(h,a,\rho_1)$ be the subroutine defined in [[alg-qa-29-variance-aware-monte-carlo]]. Its output $u$ satisfies
$$|u-\mathbb E[h]|\le a(1+s)^2$$
with probability at least $1-\rho_1$. For $k=\lceil\log_2(1/a)\rceil$, its calls use
$$O\bigl(k\ln(k+1)(1+\ln(1/\rho_1))\bigr)$$
prepared output-state copies and
$$O\bigl(a^{-1}k^{3/2}\ln(k+1)(1+\ln(1/\rho_1))\bigr)$$
uses of the supplied state reflection when its binned QAE calls use repeated controlled-$Q$ access. The accuracy and prepared-copy bounds also hold in supplied controlled-power access; in that mode sum the separately declared power-query costs rather than infer this reflection count. All input access, band comparison, value arithmetic, controlled rotation, and finite-precision costs remain separately charged.

proposed_after_items.title: Variance-aware quantum Monte Carlo guarantee
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $v$ be the finite-valued real output of a coherent sampler with $\operatorname{Var}(v)\le\sigma^2$ for a known rational $\sigma\ge0$, and let rational $\varepsilon>0$. For each rational $0<\rho<1$, the algorithm [[alg-qa-29-variance-aware-monte-carlo]] returns $\widetilde\mu$ with $|\widetilde\mu-\mathbb E[v]|\le\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-\rho$. If $\sigma=0$, it returns the exact mean after one output preparation. For $\sigma>0$, put $z=\sigma/\varepsilon$ and $L=\max(2,z)$. In the exact coherent-access model, its resource counts are
$$O\!\left((1+\ln(1/\rho))\ln L\,\ln\ln(e^e+L)\right)$$
output-state preparations and
$$O\!\left((1+\ln(1/\rho))L(\ln L)^{3/2}\ln\ln(e^e+L)\right)$$
uses of the supplied state reflection in repeated controlled-$Q$ access, up to universal constants. Accuracy and the preparation bound hold in either declared access mode; in supplied controlled-power access sum the separately declared power costs instead of applying this reflection bound. Each state reflection is implemented through the supplied sampler and its inverse; these bounds do not turn variance alone into coherent access. A finite-gate approximation needs a separate certified error analysis before it can inherit this theorem.

proposed_after_items.title: Coherent query-to-circuit cost translation
proposed_after_items.statement:
For a QA29 execution, group its complete value-rotated sampler preparations into the distinct supplied unitaries $A_j$, and let $N_j$ be the number of fresh standalone preparations of $A_j$ and $Q_j$ the number of controlled Grover rounds using it. Also let $V_t$ range over the supplied unrotated sampler preparations used for coarse measurements, with $N_t^0$ such fresh preparations. If each controlled Grover round for $A_j$ is the explicit product of one controlled $A_j$ call, one controlled $A_j^\dagger$ call, one controlled initial-state reflection, one controlled good-state reflection, and its control phase, then the exact primitive-call cost is
$$\sum_jN_jC_{A_j,\rm prep}+\sum_tN_t^0C_{V_t,\rm prep}+\sum_jQ_j(C_{A_j,c}+C_{A_j^\dagger,c}+C_{S_{0,j},c}+C_{S_{{\rm good},j},c}+C_{{\rm phase},j}),$$
where every $C$ is the declared cost of that operation. The preparation counts exclude the controlled $A_j$ and $A_j^\dagger$ occurrences inside Grover rounds, which are already included in the $Q_j$ terms. With a single $A_q$, no unrotated coarse preparations, and $N_{\rm prep}=N_q$, this reduces to the homogeneous formula $N_{\rm prep}C_{A_q,\rm prep}+Q(C_{A_q,c}+C_{A_q^\dagger,c}+C_{S_0,c}+C_{S_{\rm good},c}+C_{\rm phase})$. Value decoding, band comparisons, reversible arithmetic, controlled rotations, uncomputation, phase estimation, ancilla workspace, circuit description, and classical output/median computations add their own declared gate, width, bit, or oracle costs. If a complete reflection is instead supplied as a named oracle, charge that oracle's declared cost separately and do not also expand it into its components. No bare query bound becomes a gate bound without these implementations.

items.title: Trace of a product of Hermitian matrices is real
items.statement: For Hermitian matrices $A,B\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $n\ge0$, the trace $\operatorname{tr}(AB)$ is real.
