proposed_after_items.title: A finite-grid quantum subgradient from approximate values

references.title: van Apeldoorn, Gilyen, Gribling, de Wolf, Convex optimization using quantum oracles, Lemmas 14–21 and Theorem 23

proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $1\le d\le n$, let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, and let $f:C\to\mathbb R$ be convex. Let $r_1,L>0$ and suppose $f$ is $L$-Lipschitz on a neighborhood of $[-2r_1,2r_1]^d\subset C$, with every point there having a subgradient in $\mathbb R^d$ of norm at most $L$. Let $0<\rho\le1/3$, $\rho_0=99\rho/100$, $0<\delta\le nr_1L/\rho_0$, and $r_2=\sqrt{\delta r_1\rho_0/(nL)}$. A deterministic clean value oracle approximates $f$ to error at most $\delta$ on the finite query grids.

Choose a finite uniform grid of cell centers of $[-r_1,r_1]^d$, with $2^b$ cells per coordinate and mesh $h_0=2r_1/2^b\le(\rho/1000)r_2^2/(8n^2r_1)$. Sample one center $z$ uniformly using $b$ independent fair bits per coordinate, and keep it fixed across all subsequent runs. Put $a=2r_2/n$, $B=La$, $m=\max\{5,\lceil\log_2(B/(28\pi\delta))\rceil\}$, $M=2^m$, and $B_*=28\pi\delta M$. On each independent run prepare the uniform product grid $u_i=(j_i+1/2)/M-1/2$, apply phase $\exp(2\pi iM\widetilde f(z+au)/(3B_*))$ with clean uncomputation, apply the negative-sign QFT to each coordinate, and decode signed integers $y_i$ as $3B_*y_i/(aM)$. Use $N=\lceil18\ln(1000n/\rho)+3\rceil$ independent runs and coordinate medians. A total implemented-phase operator error at most $1/1000$ per run is permitted.

With probability at least $1-\rho$, the resulting vector $v\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfies, simultaneously for every $y\in C$,
$$f(y)\ge f(0)+\langle v,y\rangle-(23n)^2\sqrt{\frac{\delta L}{\rho_0r_1}}\|y\|-2L\sqrt n\,r_1.$$
The number of value-oracle and inverse calls is $O(\log(n/\rho))$. Random bits, phases, QFT gates, arithmetic, and output costs are separate.

Let $p_M$ be the probability that all work flags are zero. Let $p_0$ be the corresponding probability when $M=0$. Then $p_0>0$ and
$$\frac{p_M}{p_0}=1+\frac12\operatorname{tr}(M\rho_G).$$

proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $B(x,t)=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:\|z-x\|_2\le t\}$ and let $B(K,t)=\bigcup_{x\in K}B(x,t)$ for $t\ge0$; $B(K,-t)$ denotes the inward erosion consisting of points whose radius-$t$ ball is contained in $K$. The deterministic weak-membership oracle $\mathrm{MEM}_{\varepsilon,0}(K)$ is queried at a finite-precision point $y$ and must correctly assert either $y\in B(K,\varepsilon)$ or $y\notin B(K,-\varepsilon)$. In the overlap it may return either valid assertion. The coherent interface is a supplied reversible Boolean unitary with a fixed deterministic completion on every encoded input, together with its inverse and any controlled forms used.

A weak separation oracle $\mathrm{SEP}_{\eta,\rho}(K)$, queried at $y$, with probability at least $1-\rho$, either asserts $y\in B(K,\eta)$ or asserts $y\notin B(K,-\eta)$ and returns a unit vector $g$ satisfying $\langle g,z\rangle\le\langle g,y\rangle+\eta$ for every $z\in B(K,-\eta)$. The membership-to-separation algorithm is promised only on the query domain in its theorem; no unique answer is required in the boundary bands. A finite unit-normal encoding may be a nonzero rational vector v with the normalization g=v/||v|| interpreted exactly; rational bisection supplies an upper norm bound N between ||v|| and2||v|| when a classical reduction requires rational halfspaces. Radius, point, unit-normal and offset encodings and all query/inverse/gate/bit costs are part of the contract.

proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $B(0,r)\subseteq K\subseteq B(0,R)$ be a closed convex body in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$. In any rotated coordinates set $C=\{y:\exists t,(y,t)\in K\}$ and $h(y)=\min\{t:(y,t)\in K\}$. Every interior point of $C$ has a subgradient, and every such subgradient at a point in the interior of this ball has norm at most $L$.

Hence binary search on $[-R,-r/2]$, returning its final upper endpoint when its width is at most $\delta/3$, approximates $h(y)$ within $\delta$ if $\varepsilon\le r\delta/(3R)$. It uses $O(1+\log(R/\delta))$ membership queries and has a clean coherent implementation using the same order of queries and inverse queries.

proposed_after_items.title: Sparse-oracle quantum SDP algorithm
proposed_after_items.statement:
Input finite binary Hermitian matrices $A_1,\ldots,A_m,C$ and rational $b,R,r,\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon>0$, $m\ge1$, $A_1=I$, $b_1=R\ge0$, $\|A_j\|,\|C\|\le1$, a nonempty primal, and an attained optimal dual of $\ell_1$ norm at most $r\ge1$. Supply the total finite sparse XOR location/value interfaces of [[def-qa-30-sdp-sparse-oracle-model]], the costed reference preparation $\Phi_n$, and declared finite reversible arithmetic, controlled evolution, inverses, reflections and synthesis budgets. The output is a classical sparse dual list or explicit `FAIL`; the confidence target is rational $0<\delta<1$ (use $\delta=1/3$). Every memory, QRAM, reference, arithmetic and output cost is recorded. The separate resource theorem substitutes actual sparse-evolution implementations; no matrix function or sparse-sum oracle is implicit.

**Boundary branches.** In dimension zero return the zero dual vector. For $R=0$ or $\varepsilon\ge2R$ return $e_1$. These branches precede all divisions by $R$. Otherwise put $e=\varepsilon/8$, $L=\lceil\log_2(16R/\varepsilon)\rceil+2$, $w=r+1$, and
$$\ell=\ln(\max(2,n)),\quad \theta=e/(24Rr),\quad T=\lceil36w^2R^2\ell/e^2\rceil,\quad\eta=\sqrt{\ell/T}.$$
Computable-real constants such as $\eta$ are not exact value-oracle outputs: choose certified finite rational enclosures and round common scalar coefficients to the precision allocated to each decoded Hermitian sum and its simulated evolutions. Integer cutoffs use certified upper enclosures, so a conservative larger $T$ is allowed with the same $\eta=\sqrt{\ell/T}$. No equality comparison with a transcendental number is required. The ideal densities and regret argument use the displayed real parameters; every decoded-matrix error is included in the finite block-error and whole-circuit hybrid budgets below.

**Derived sparse access.** At round $t$, store the previous two-sparse rational lists and form $S_{t-1}=\sum_{u<t}M_u$, $M_u=(\sum_jy_{u,j}A_j-C)/w$. To answer a row query, enumerate all constituent support lists and the identity column, sort their finite column labels, merge duplicates and retain every distinct union column, including columns whose combined value is zero. Pad with distinct labels. Never test a real sum for exact zero. Round common real scalar coefficients with certified total norm error and compute exact finite decoded entry sums; this preserves Hermiticity and transposed support lists. The sorted-support construction of [[lem-qa-25-sorted-xor-sparse-access-isometries]] allows these listed zeros and constructs the clean block access. Actual row scanning, sorting, value arithmetic and inverse/control calls are charged. Allocate decoded-matrix error before each evolution so its Duhamel error $|u|\|H-\widetilde H\|$ and all simulation errors meet the allocated circuit slot budget. The clean-subspace hybrid in [[lem-qa-25-clean-subspace-unitary-hybrid]] applies to the actual finite implementations. A QRAM profile supplies its address/memory unitary and its construction/update costs explicitly.

**Frozen round factory.** At the start of each round, choose the exact finite Hermitian decoded $\widehat L_t$ with $\|\widehat L_t-\eta S_{t-1}\|\le\delta_t\le\min(1/8,e_f/100)$. Run the finite ShiftMin construction of [[lem-qa-30-spectral-minimum-shift]] on $\widehat L_t$ with its certified norm bound, measure its rational lower shift once and freeze both $\widehat G=\widehat L_t-(\widetilde\lambda-3/2)I$ and the target $G=\eta S_{t-1}-(\widetilde\lambda-3/2)I$, their norm bounds, Fourier lists, normalization and all precisions. The minimum-eigenvalue variational bound transfers the shift margin to the target: both minima lie in $[1,2]$. Implement the decoded block, including its at-most-$e_f/200$ positive-exponential perturbation against the target in the final block-error budget. Execute steps 2–3 of [[alg-qa-30-sdp-gibbs-purification]] with these frozen matrices and shift to build the unmeasured Gibbs block; do not repeat its shift-measurement step. For each observable $A$, build the finite Fourier block for $F_A=\frac12\sqrt{I+A/2}$ with $x_0=0,r=1,\Delta=1/2,B=1$ and coefficients $a_k=\frac12\binom{1/2}{k}2^{-k}$. Use $e_f\le\min(1/2,\theta/(100000n))$ and the SAME $B_A^+=B_G^+=1+e_f/8$ in numerator and baseline. The baseline block is $I/(2B_A^+)$.

**Trace label.** Compose the frozen Gibbs block and observable block on the first half of $\Phi_n$, with distinct work registers. Estimate the two actual all-zero probabilities with [[alg-qa-relative-probability-estimation]], floor $1/(1024n)$ and relative tolerance $\theta/36$. Return $2(\widehat q_A/\widehat q_0-1)$ rounded with error at most $\theta/4$ and clipped to $[-1,1]$; a zero denominator on a bad path returns the fixed label zero. Use its finite worst-case cap and the supplied `efficient-grid` fixed-precision rounding mode. For an indexed trace sampler preserve the uniform index, all AE/QPE targets, comparison bits, stop flags, coins, rounded values and history; defer internal measurements and pad stopped branches by identities. Its inverse is the reverse of this entire circuit. No inverse of a normalized postselected state is used. All coherent division, comparison, rounding and history are quantum gates and work, separately charged. [[thm-qa-30-flagged-trace-error-and-cost]] supplies the conditional accuracy and probability floors.

**Diagonal mode.** When every input is diagonal, the caller may select the scalar flag implementation instead of Fourier evolution. Evaluate the finite decoded round energy $\widehat L_t(i)$ using the stored sum of at most $2t+1$ diagonal values. Round to absolute error at most $1/8$, retain the uniform index, run the same capped robust minimum, measure its label $s$ once, and freeze $\widehat g_i=\widehat L_t(i)-s+3/2$. Its confidence uses the round's shift budget. Set the common coefficient approximation error $\delta_t\le\min(1/8,\mu/100)$, $\mu\le\theta/(100000n)$. On the shift good event target and decoded minima are in $[1,2]$. For observable entry $a_i$, prepare a scalar flag with probability within $\mu$ of $(1+a_i/2)e^{-g_i}/4$, using the finite decoded energy; the baseline uses $a_i=0$ and the same shift. Compute the exponential as follows. Put $B=\lceil\log_2(32/\mu)\rceil$ by rational doubling comparisons. For $\widehat g_i\ge B$ use zero. Otherwise double an integer $h$ from two until $3^B B^h/h!\le\mu/64$, then evaluate its exact rational Taylor polynomial through degree $h-1$ and round once. Clip to $[0,1]$. To implement the flag, bisect an angle interval $[0,\pi/2]$ using fixed absolute-$\mu/32$ Taylor enclosures of its midpoint $\sin^2$; stop on comparison overlap or after the fixed $O(\log(1/\mu))$ width cap, then implement the finite encoded angle by binary-controlled rotations with its allocated synthesis error. Retain/uncompute all arithmetic as stipulated for the full inverse. The factorial test passes by $h=O(\log^2(1/\mu))$; the cost theorem proves this schedule and its ratio/error budget. Use the same RelProb floor, relative tolerance, coherent history, score oracle and outer loop as in general mode. This diagonal factory replaces the spectral/Fourier factory; its arithmetic costs remain explicitly charged.

**Two-sparse round oracle.** First measure a scalar trace label $\widetilde c$ for $C$. Put $c'=\widetilde c-w\theta$. Execute the explicit rational region, membership, determinant-based angular order, interpolation and scale recovery in the proof of [[lem-qa-30-two-sparse-estimated-oracle]]. If $\alpha\ge0,c'\le0$, return zero. Otherwise run [[alg-qa-30-capped-generalized-minimum]] twice with $N=m$ on the two score orders of that lemma. Both orders assign score zero to every point inside its region; outside points use the oppositely oriented angular orders, compared by rational half-plane and determinant tests. No arctangent equality test or preliminary search miss is needed. If either selected point lies in the region, return its scaled one-coordinate vector. Otherwise intersect its selected pair's segment with the closed rational halfspaces and recover its positive scale by the lemma's explicit formulas. If the segment interval is empty return `EMPTY`. If successful return its rational weights, merging repeated indices. `EMPTY` is a bounded-error complete-oracle response: on the joint good event it implies $\alpha<\mathrm{OPT}$. A low-level failure with no proved contract returns `FAIL` instead.

**Threshold$(\alpha,e,\delta_{call})$.** Initialize $S_0=0$. Set $\beta=\delta_{call}/(10T)$. For $t=1,\ldots,T$:

1. Build the frozen round factory with shift failure at most $\beta$ and scalar $C$ trace failure at most $\beta$.
2. Let $Q_{min}$ be the deterministic sampler-call cap of one generalized minimum at confidence $\beta/2$. Give each indexed trace label bad probability at most $\nu\le(\beta/(16Q_{min}))^2$, by allocating its relative-estimation and implementation errors accordingly. Retain its history and fixed-index access as above. Allocate any remaining whole-minimum implementation hybrid error within its $\beta$ failure budget. Run both minima at total failure at most $\beta$ each. These are the good-label/cleaning hypotheses of [[thm-qa-30-generalized-minimum-guarantee]], rather than a union bound over unmeasured labels.
3. On `EMPTY` return `HIGHER`. On a successful weight list store $y_t$, compute $M_t$, and update its sparse list. An absent access certificate or other unsupported numerical failure returns `FAIL`.

After $T$ successful rounds return `LOWER` with the exact rational sparse list $\bar y=(e/R)e_1+T^{-1}\sum_ty_t$. Retain its finite rational coefficients; no feasibility-preserving rounding is inferred. The oracle's conditional bad probability is at most $\delta_{call}$ by the adaptive union bound. Its `HIGHER` implication and `LOWER` reserve margin are [[lem-qa-30-mmw-to-sdp-feasibility]].

**Outer search.** Set $lo=-R$, $hi=R$, $\delta_{call}=\delta/(L+1)$. Call Threshold at $R+e$ and store its `LOWER` vector; any other outcome returns `FAIL`. For at most $L$ midpoint calls, stop when $hi-lo\le\varepsilon/2$. At $\alpha=(lo+hi)/2$, on `LOWER` store its vector and put $hi=\min(hi,\alpha+e)$; on `HIGHER` put $lo=\max(lo,\alpha-e)$; on `FAIL` return `FAIL`. Return the stored vector, or `FAIL` if the fixed cap is exhausted before the stopping test. The invariant and finite cap are proved in [[thm-qa-30-sdp-binary-search-correctness]]; no tolerance refinement is needed on a good path. Check finite rational nonnegativity and objective arithmetic before output; PSD feasibility is supplied by the proved MMW reserve, without a free dense spectral checker.

Confidence budgets are predictable functions of finite prior histories. The first-bad-call union bound covers the adaptive search. Capped search/statistical errors belong to their proved bad events; unproved access or arithmetic failures do not certify infeasibility. Output contains at most $2T+1$ nonzero coordinates after merging, and no dense primal matrix is produced.

For arbitrary $n$, the reference price is repeated $\widetilde O(\sqrt{nm}\max(1,Rr/\varepsilon)^3)$ times per threshold run, rather than incurred once.

Let $G=\langle g\rangle$ have known exact order $q\ge2$, let $x=g^a$, and let $\delta=p/v$ be supplied as binary positive integers $p<v$. Write $K$ for the sum of their bit lengths. Each independent Fourier sample succeeds with probability $\varphi(q)/q\ge1/(1+\log_2q)$. Put $L=\lceil\log_2q\rceil$, let $D$ be the least integer $d\ge0$ with $2^d\delta\ge1$, and set $t=(1+L)D$. Let $w$ be the supplied group-element encoding width. $$
O\!\left((L^2C_G+Lw+L^3)(1+\ln(1/\delta))\right).

O\!\left(K^2+(L^2T_G+L^4)(1+\ln(1/\delta))\right).
$$

items.title: Fourier sample from a generalized-dihedral reflection coset state
items.statement:
Write $A=\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$ additively, $N\ge2$, and identify its generalized-dihedral group with $A\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ under
$$
(a,b)(a',b')=(a+(-1)^b a',\,b+b'\bmod2).
$$
Let $H_s=\{(0,0),(s,1)\}$ and let a total encoded function $F$ be constant on each left coset of $H_s$ and distinct on different left cosets. Start in the uniform state on the $2N$ group elements, evaluate the coherent XOR oracle for $F$ into a zero output register, discard that register, apply the positive-sign $\operatorname{QFT}_N$ to the first coordinate, and measure that coordinate. The measured $k\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$ is uniform. Conditional on $k$, the remaining qubit is, up to a global phase,
$$
|\psi_k\rangle=\frac{|0\rangle+\exp(2\pi i ks/N)|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}.
$$

The coordinate readout uses the Lüders projective instrument for the projections $\Pi_k=|k\rangle\langle k|\otimes I_2$. The stated conditional qubit is the post-measurement state after discarding the measured coordinate.

items.title: Finite abelian hidden-shift promise
Finite cyclic discrete-logarithm problem and costed encoding
Hidden shift as generalized-dihedral hidden subgroup
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite abelian group in explicit additive coordinates, and let $f,g:A\to S$ satisfy the hidden-shift promise of [[def-qa-finite-abelian-hidden-shift-problem]]: both maps are injective and there is a unique $s\in A$ such that $f(a)=g(a+s)$ for every $a$. Write $D_A=A\rtimes\mathbb Z_2$ with
$$
(a,b)(a',b')=(a+(-1)^b a',b+b'\bmod2),
$$
and define $F(a,0)=f(a)$ and $F(a,1)=g(a)$. Then $F$ is constant exactly on the left cosets of the order-two subgroup $H_s=\{(0,0),(s,1)\}=\langle(s,1)\rangle$. The subgroup determines the shift uniquely: $H_s=H_t$ implies $s=t$.

If a coherent XOR oracle for this $F$ is directly supplied, one $F$-oracle query implements one value query. From only coherent XOR oracles for $f$ and $g$, the $F$-XOR operation can be implemented with four calls total (two to compute the values into scratch registers and two to uncompute them), plus the controlled output XOR; no controlled call to either oracle is assumed. All gate, workspace, and named-oracle query costs remain separately charged.
items.axiom_use: None; all groups, functions, and encodings are finite.

items.title: Power-of-two dihedral hidden-subgroup sieve
items.statement:
Input an integer $n\ge1$, $N=2^n$, and either (i) a coherent XOR oracle $O_F$ for a total encoded function $F:D_N\to S$ that is constant on each left coset of the unknown reflection subgroup $H_s=\langle yx^s\rangle$ and takes distinct values on different left cosets, or (ii) a finite cyclic hidden-shift instance on $A=\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$ together with its reflection oracle constructed by [[thm-qa-hidden-shift-generalized-dihedral-reduction]]. Use coordinates $(a,b)\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ with multiplication $(a,b)(a',b')=(a+(-1)^b a',b+b')$ and fix $x=(-1,0)$ and $y=(0,1)$; then $yx^s=(s,1)$. Charge each supplied or constructed oracle call according to its interface.

Every projective readout below is implemented by the Lüders instrument of its stated projections. Charge each supplied measurement or instrument implementation under its declared interface.

For $n\le5$, query all group elements (at most $2N\le64$ values of $F$) and return the unique $s$ for which $F(0,0)=F(s,1)$. For $n\ge6$, set $m=\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$ once and retain this $m$ through all recursive calls. The following procedure is run at modulus $2^r$, starting with $r=n$:

1. If $r\le5$, use the direct-query base case. Otherwise set $t_r=\lceil(r-1)/m\rceil$ and create a list $L_0$ of $M=3\cdot2^{3m}$ independent coset samples: prepare the uniform group state with Hadamards on its $r+1$ coordinate bits, evaluate $O_F$, discard the function-output register, apply the positive-sign $\operatorname{QFT}_{2^r}$ to the cyclic coordinate and measure that coordinate. Store the measured label $k$ and retain its conditional qubit $|\psi_k\rangle=(|0\rangle+e^{2\pi i k s/2^r}|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$.
2. For each $j=0,\ldots,t_r-1$, put $w_j=\min(m,r-1-mj)$. The current labels are divisible by $2^{mj}$. Bucket them by the $w_j$ bits of $k/2^{mj}$ immediately above those trailing zeroes, using only the lower $r-1$ bits of $k$. In each bucket, preserve current list order, pair consecutive entries, and leave the last entry unmatched if the bucket has odd size; this is a maximum-cardinality disjoint matching. For each pair, apply the CNOT pair combiner and measure its second qubit with the Lüders instrument. Retain only outcome $1$; the retained state has label $k-\ell\pmod {2^r}$. Discard unmatched states and outcome-$0$ states. The next list consists of the retained states.
3. The widths sum to $r-1$, so every final label is $0$ or $2^{r-1}$. If a state with label $2^{r-1}$ occurs, measure its qubit in the $\{|+\rangle,| -\rangle\}$ basis. Outcome $+$ means $s$ is even; outcome $-$ means $s$ is odd. If the target label is absent, return FAIL.
4. For even $s$, put $r'=r-1$, $x'=x^2$, $y'=y$, and $s'=s/2$. Identify child coordinates with $K_0=\langle x^2,y\rangle$ by
$$\phi_0:\mathbb Z/2^{r'}\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z\longrightarrow\mathbb Z/2^r\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z, \qquad \phi_0(a',b')=(2a',b')\pmod {2^r}.$$
Use the child oracle $F_0=F\circ\phi_0$ and run this procedure at modulus $2^{r'}$. A coherent $F_0$ query is implemented by appending a fresh clean low address bit $0$ to the $r'$ bits of $a'$, retaining $b'$, and making one parent $O_F$ call.

   For odd $s$, put $r'=r-1$, $x'=x^2$, $y'=yx$, and $s'=(s-1)/2$. Identify child coordinates with $K_1=\langle x^2,yx\rangle$ by
$$\phi_1:\mathbb Z/2^{r'}\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z\longrightarrow\mathbb Z/2^r\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z, \qquad \phi_1(a',b')=(2a'+b',b')\pmod {2^r}.$$
Use $F_1=F\circ\phi_1$ and recurse at modulus $2^{r'}$. To implement a coherent $F_1$ query, append a fresh clean low address bit $z=0$, copy $b'$ to $z$ by CNOT, make one parent $O_F$ call on the ambient address $(a',z,b')$, and uncopy $z$ by the same CNOT. Thus each child hiding-oracle query uses one parent $F$ query; the odd embedding adds two ordinary CNOT gates per query, and the even embedding adds none beyond the clean address wire. Return $2s'$ in the even branch and $2s'+1$ in the odd branch.

   Before the recursive call, discard the current sample, pair, output, and label registers after recording the parity branch; carry only the classical branch result and recursion parameters. The child call reuses this workspace.

The exact sampling-state law and pair-combination identity are in [[lem-qa-dihedral-coset-state-fourier-law]] and [[lem-qa-dihedral-sieve-pair-combination]]. The correctness, error, and resource claims for this locally specified shortened-final-width version are proved in [[thm-qa-dihedral-sieve-scope]]. The procedure is only specified for power-of-two cyclic orders; no arbitrary-$N$ or arbitrary finite-abelian extension is asserted.

items.title: Clean reversible controlled multiplication by a cyclic constant
items.statement:
Let $G=\langle g\rangle$ have order $q\ge2$, let $c\in G$, and let valid fixed-length codes occupy a subset $V\subseteq\{0,1\}^w$. Suppose total Boolean circuits are supplied for functions $h_c,h_{c^{-1}}:\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}^w\to\{0,1\}^w$, where
$$h_c(b,z)=\begin{cases}z,&b=0,\\\operatorname{enc}(u c),&b=1,\ z=\operatorname{enc}(u)\in V,\\z,&b=1,\ z\notin V,\end{cases}.$$
For each fixed control $b$, the maps $z\mapsto h_c(b,z)$ and $z\mapsto h_{c^{-1}}(b,z)$ are inverse permutations; the full controlled permutation preserves $b$.
Then reversible embedding supplies a clean-ancilla circuit that acts on a control bit and accumulator by
$$
|b,z,0_{\mathrm{work}}\rangle\longmapsto |b,h_c(b,z),0_{\mathrm{work}}\rangle.
$$
If the two Boolean circuits have at most $S$ non-input nodes and $E$ port uses each, the construction uses at most $12S+8E+5w$ elementary gates and at most $2(S+E)+w$ clean work wires. The gate charge counts each supplied $X$, CNOT, and Toffoli as one gate; no cost for constructing the Boolean descriptions is inferred.

items.title: Kuperberg dihedral hidden-subgroup scope and resource claim
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and $N=2^n$. Let $F:D_N\to S$ be a total encoded function that is constant on each left coset of $H_s=\langle yx^s\rangle$ and takes distinct values on different left cosets, accessed by a coherent XOR oracle either directly or through [[thm-qa-hidden-shift-generalized-dihedral-reduction]]. Equivalently, $F(u)=F(v)$ exactly when $uH_s=vH_s$, as required by [[alg-qa-dihedral-hidden-subgroup-sieve]]. Use the Lüders instruments specified there for the projective readouts. For $n\le5$ the direct branch succeeds exactly with at most $64$ $F$ queries. For $n\ge6$, put $m=\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$ and $M=3\cdot2^{3m}$. The locally specified shortened-final-width sieve has failure probability at most
$$\min\{1,nm\exp(-2^{m/3-1})\}.$$
It uses at most $nM+64$ named $F$-oracle queries, $O(n^3M)$ ideal gates for sieve control and recursive coordinate maps, $O(n^2m^2M)$ classical bit operations for label sorting and list processing, $O(M+n+w_F+a_F)$ quantum workspace, and $O(nM)$ bits to store all active labels. Here $w_F$ is the output-register width and $a_F$ is additional workspace for the supplied or constructed $F$ implementation. The $O(n^3M)$ gate count excludes the implementation of the named $F$ interface itself. An explicit $F$ circuit using $G_F(n)$ gates per call adds $O((nM+64)G_F(n))$ gates. If $F$ is constructed from only the two coherent XOR oracles for a hidden-shift pair, each call uses four $f/g$ oracle calls and adds $O(w_F)$ ordinary gates for controlled output selection; add $O((nM+64)w_F)$ selector gates, and charge any explicit circuits implementing $f$ and $g$ separately.

Since $m=\Theta(\sqrt n)$, the named $F$-query count, sieve gate count, and classical label-processing count are $2^{O(\sqrt n)}=2^{O(\sqrt{\log_2 N})}$ up to polynomial factors in $n$. The total workspace and any oracle-implementation gate costs retain the explicit interface-dependent terms above. The theorem is confined to power-of-two cyclic orders and supplied exact interfaces. It proves no polynomial-time claim, no arbitrary-$N$ version, and no algorithm for arbitrary finite abelian hidden shift.

items.title: Costed coherent evaluation of cyclic group powers
items.statement:
Inputs are a valid instance from [[def-qa-finite-cyclic-discrete-logarithm-problem]], exponent registers $u,v\in\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, and one of these access profiles:

1. a supplied coherent XOR oracle for $f(u,v)=g^u x^v$; initialize a fresh output target to $0^w$, invoke the oracle once, and return its output (the zero target need not be the encoding of the group identity); or
2. explicit reversible group-operation circuits, or separately charged named controlled-multiplication operations with the same complete-register action, for each classically specified constant and its inverse. Initialize a fresh accumulator to $\operatorname{enc}(e)$, the code of the group identity. Precompute $g_j=g^{2^j}$ and $x_j=x^{2^j}$ for $0\le j<L$, where $L=\lceil\log_2q\rceil$, by repeated squaring. For $j=0,\ldots,L-1$, use the bit $u_j$ to apply the clean controlled multiplication by $g_j$ to the accumulator, and use $v_j$ to apply the clean controlled multiplication by $x_j$. The procedure is the circuit of [[lem-qa-controlled-cyclic-multiplication-clean]] applied at each control bit.

In profile 2, return the accumulator as the function value. The exponent registers are unchanged, all work and temporary target wires are returned to their declared initial states, and each direct oracle invocation or group-operation invocation is charged under its separately declared access profile. If only an uncontrolled black-box group operation is supplied, return UNSUPPORTED_ACCESS: it does not provide a controlled call.

To supply the total coherent XOR oracle required by the hidden-subgroup sampler, profile 2 is wrapped as follows. Prepare its $w$-bit accumulator from zero to $\operatorname{enc}(e)$ with at most $w$ Pauli-$X$ gates, execute the $2L$ controlled multiplications, copy the resulting $w$-bit value by CNOT into an arbitrary target $y$, then reverse the evaluation using the separately supplied inverse-constant controlled multiplications. Finally undo the initial $X$ gates. This implements $|u,v,y\rangle\mapsto|u,v,y\oplus\operatorname{enc}(g^ux^v)\rangle$ on valid exponent codes and restores every auxiliary wire to zero. The supplied total controlled operations also define its action on invalid exponent codes; these values are the declared Boolean extension. The wrapper uses $4L$ controlled multiplications and at most $3w$ extra $X$/CNOT gates; preparation, output copying, and inverse calls are charged.

items.title: Correctness and clean-work cost of cyclic power evaluation
items.statement: For every valid encoded cyclic-group input $(G,g,x,q)$ with $q\ge2$ and every $u,v\in\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, the explicit-circuit branch of [[alg-qa-cyclic-group-power-evaluation]] writes the encoding of $g^u x^v$ into the accumulator, leaves the exponent registers unchanged, and returns every clean work and temporary target register to zero. If $L=\lceil\log_2 q\rceil$ and each controlled multiplication by a known constant has gate cost at most $C_G$, the circuit uses $2L$ controlled multiplications and $O(LC_G)$ gates per evaluation, in addition to the separately charged classical precomputation. The compute-XOR-uncompute wrapper in that algorithm implements the full target-XOR action on valid exponent codes, with its declared total extension elsewhere. If each forward and inverse-constant controlled multiplication costs at most $C_G$, that wrapper uses $4L$ such calls and at most $3w$ additional $X$/CNOT gates, hence $O(LC_G+w)$ gates, and restores its auxiliary registers to zero.

Let $w$ be the supplied group-element encoding width. A direct coherent function-oracle profile uses at most $O(L(1+\ln(1/\delta)))$ function queries and separately uses $O(L(1+\ln(1/\delta)))$ ordinary multiplication/equality operations for classical verification. If $f$ is implemented by controlled group multiplications, there are $O(L^2(1+\ln(1/\delta)))$ controlled-multiplication calls and the same order of ordinary multiplication/equality calls for verification. If the explicitly supplied reversible multiplication, equality, and both forward and inverse-constant controlled-multiplication circuits each cost at most $C_G$ gates and the supplied exact uniform preparation and product QFT cost $O(L^2)$ ideal gates, the total ideal gate count is
$$
O\!\left((L^2C_G+Lw+L^3)(1+\ln(1/\delta))\right).
$$
If one classical multiplication or equality operation on the encoding costs at most $T_G$ bit operations and modular inverses use the schoolbook extended-Euclidean algorithm, the classical bit cost of confidence preprocessing, arithmetic and verification is
$$
O\!\left(K^2+(L^2T_G+L^4)(1+\ln(1/\delta))\right).
$$
All query, gate, and classical bit bounds are conditional on the stated supplied interfaces. The exact binary QFT is counted in the ideal-gate model; no finite-set compilation cost or generic efficient group encoding is asserted.

proposed_after_items.title: Fourier sample from a generalized-dihedral reflection coset state
proposed_after_items.statement:
Write $A=\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$ additively, $N\ge2$, and identify its generalized-dihedral group with $A\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ under
$$
(a,b)(a',b')=(a+(-1)^b a',\,b+b'\bmod2).
$$
Let $H_s=\{(0,0),(s,1)\}$ and let a total encoded function $F$ be constant on each left coset of $H_s$ and distinct on different left cosets. Start in the uniform state on the $2N$ group elements, evaluate the coherent XOR oracle for $F$ into a zero output register, discard that register, apply the positive-sign $\operatorname{QFT}_N$ to the first coordinate, and measure that coordinate. The measured $k\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$ is uniform. Conditional on $k$, the remaining qubit is, up to a global phase,
$$
|\psi_k\rangle=\frac{|0\rangle+\exp(2\pi i ks/N)|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}.
$$

The coordinate readout uses the Lüders projective instrument for the projections $\Pi_k=|k\rangle\langle k|\otimes I_2$. The stated conditional qubit is the post-measurement state after discarding the measured coordinate.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; all registers and sums are finite.

proposed_after_items.title: Finite abelian hidden-shift promise
Finite cyclic discrete-logarithm problem and costed encoding
Hidden shift as generalized-dihedral hidden subgroup
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite abelian group in explicit additive coordinates, and let $f,g:A\to S$ satisfy the hidden-shift promise of [[def-qa-finite-abelian-hidden-shift-problem]]: both maps are injective and there is a unique $s\in A$ such that $f(a)=g(a+s)$ for every $a$. Write $D_A=A\rtimes\mathbb Z_2$ with
$$
(a,b)(a',b')=(a+(-1)^b a',b+b'\bmod2),
$$
and define $F(a,0)=f(a)$ and $F(a,1)=g(a)$. Then $F$ is constant exactly on the left cosets of the order-two subgroup $H_s=\{(0,0),(s,1)\}=\langle(s,1)\rangle$. The subgroup determines the shift uniquely: $H_s=H_t$ implies $s=t$.

If a coherent XOR oracle for this $F$ is directly supplied, one $F$-oracle query implements one value query. From only coherent XOR oracles for $f$ and $g$, the $F$-XOR operation can be implemented with four calls total (two to compute the values into scratch registers and two to uncompute them), plus the controlled output XOR; no controlled call to either oracle is assumed. All gate, workspace, and named-oracle query costs remain separately charged.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; all groups, functions, and encodings are finite.

proposed_after_items.title: Power-of-two dihedral hidden-subgroup sieve
proposed_after_items.statement:
Input an integer $n\ge1$, $N=2^n$, and either (i) a coherent XOR oracle $O_F$ for a total encoded function $F:D_N\to S$ that is constant on each left coset of the unknown reflection subgroup $H_s=\langle yx^s\rangle$ and takes distinct values on different left cosets, or (ii) a finite cyclic hidden-shift instance on $A=\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$ together with its reflection oracle constructed by [[thm-qa-hidden-shift-generalized-dihedral-reduction]]. Use coordinates $(a,b)\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ with multiplication $(a,b)(a',b')=(a+(-1)^b a',b+b')$ and fix $x=(-1,0)$ and $y=(0,1)$; then $yx^s=(s,1)$. Charge each supplied or constructed oracle call according to its interface.

Every projective readout below is implemented by the Lüders instrument of its stated projections. Charge each supplied measurement or instrument implementation under its declared interface.

For $n\le5$, query all group elements (at most $2N\le64$ values of $F$) and return the unique $s$ for which $F(0,0)=F(s,1)$. For $n\ge6$, set $m=\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$ once and retain this $m$ through all recursive calls. The following procedure is run at modulus $2^r$, starting with $r=n$:

1. If $r\le5$, use the direct-query base case. Otherwise set $t_r=\lceil(r-1)/m\rceil$ and create a list $L_0$ of $M=3\cdot2^{3m}$ independent coset samples: prepare the uniform group state with Hadamards on its $r+1$ coordinate bits, evaluate $O_F$, discard the function-output register, apply the positive-sign $\operatorname{QFT}_{2^r}$ to the cyclic coordinate and measure that coordinate. Store the measured label $k$ and retain its conditional qubit $|\psi_k\rangle=(|0\rangle+e^{2\pi i k s/2^r}|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$.
2. For each $j=0,\ldots,t_r-1$, put $w_j=\min(m,r-1-mj)$. The current labels are divisible by $2^{mj}$. Bucket them by the $w_j$ bits of $k/2^{mj}$ immediately above those trailing zeroes, using only the lower $r-1$ bits of $k$. In each bucket, preserve current list order, pair consecutive entries, and leave the last entry unmatched if the bucket has odd size; this is a maximum-cardinality disjoint matching. For each pair, apply the CNOT pair combiner and measure its second qubit with the Lüders instrument. Retain only outcome $1$; the retained state has label $k-\ell\pmod {2^r}$. Discard unmatched states and outcome-$0$ states. The next list consists of the retained states.
3. The widths sum to $r-1$, so every final label is $0$ or $2^{r-1}$. If a state with label $2^{r-1}$ occurs, measure its qubit in the $\{|+\rangle,| -\rangle\}$ basis. Outcome $+$ means $s$ is even; outcome $-$ means $s$ is odd. If the target label is absent, return FAIL.
4. For even $s$, put $r'=r-1$, $x'=x^2$, $y'=y$, and $s'=s/2$. Identify child coordinates with $K_0=\langle x^2,y\rangle$ by
$$\phi_0:\mathbb Z/2^{r'}\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z\longrightarrow\mathbb Z/2^r\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z, \qquad \phi_0(a',b')=(2a',b')\pmod {2^r}.$$
Use the child oracle $F_0=F\circ\phi_0$ and run this procedure at modulus $2^{r'}$. A coherent $F_0$ query is implemented by appending a fresh clean low address bit $0$ to the $r'$ bits of $a'$, retaining $b'$, and making one parent $O_F$ call.

   For odd $s$, put $r'=r-1$, $x'=x^2$, $y'=yx$, and $s'=(s-1)/2$. Identify child coordinates with $K_1=\langle x^2,yx\rangle$ by
$$\phi_1:\mathbb Z/2^{r'}\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z\longrightarrow\mathbb Z/2^r\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z, \qquad \phi_1(a',b')=(2a'+b',b')\pmod {2^r}.$$
Use $F_1=F\circ\phi_1$ and recurse at modulus $2^{r'}$. To implement a coherent $F_1$ query, append a fresh clean low address bit $z=0$, copy $b'$ to $z$ by CNOT, make one parent $O_F$ call on the ambient address $(a',z,b')$, and uncopy $z$ by the same CNOT. Thus each child hiding-oracle query uses one parent $F$ query; the odd embedding adds two ordinary CNOT gates per query, and the even embedding adds none beyond the clean address wire. Return $2s'$ in the even branch and $2s'+1$ in the odd branch.

   Before the recursive call, discard the current sample, pair, output, and label registers after recording the parity branch; carry only the classical branch result and recursion parameters. The child call reuses this workspace.

The exact sampling-state law and pair-combination identity are in [[lem-qa-dihedral-coset-state-fourier-law]] and [[lem-qa-dihedral-sieve-pair-combination]]. The correctness, error, and resource claims for this locally specified shortened-final-width version are proved in [[thm-qa-dihedral-sieve-scope]]. The procedure is only specified for power-of-two cyclic orders; no arbitrary-$N$ or arbitrary finite-abelian extension is asserted.

proposed_after_items.title: Clean reversible controlled multiplication by a cyclic constant
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $G=\langle g\rangle$ have order $q\ge2$, let $c\in G$, and let valid fixed-length codes occupy a subset $V\subseteq\{0,1\}^w$. Suppose total Boolean circuits are supplied for functions $h_c,h_{c^{-1}}:\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}^w\to\{0,1\}^w$, where
$$h_c(b,z)=\begin{cases}z,&b=0,\\\operatorname{enc}(u c),&b=1,\ z=\operatorname{enc}(u)\in V,\\z,&b=1,\ z\notin V,\end{cases}.$$
For each fixed control $b$, the maps $z\mapsto h_c(b,z)$ and $z\mapsto h_{c^{-1}}(b,z)$ are inverse permutations; the full controlled permutation preserves $b$.
Then reversible embedding supplies a clean-ancilla circuit that acts on a control bit and accumulator by
$$
|b,z,0_{\mathrm{work}}\rangle\longmapsto |b,h_c(b,z),0_{\mathrm{work}}\rangle.
$$
If the two Boolean circuits have at most $S$ non-input nodes and $E$ port uses each, the construction uses at most $12S+8E+5w$ elementary gates and at most $2(S+E)+w$ clean work wires. The gate charge counts each supplied $X$, CNOT, and Toffoli as one gate; no cost for constructing the Boolean descriptions is inferred.

proposed_after_items.title: Kuperberg dihedral hidden-subgroup scope and resource claim
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and $N=2^n$. Let $F:D_N\to S$ be a total encoded function that is constant on each left coset of $H_s=\langle yx^s\rangle$ and takes distinct values on different left cosets, accessed by a coherent XOR oracle either directly or through [[thm-qa-hidden-shift-generalized-dihedral-reduction]]. Equivalently, $F(u)=F(v)$ exactly when $uH_s=vH_s$, as required by [[alg-qa-dihedral-hidden-subgroup-sieve]]. Use the Lüders instruments specified there for the projective readouts. For $n\le5$ the direct branch succeeds exactly with at most $64$ $F$ queries. For $n\ge6$, put $m=\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$ and $M=3\cdot2^{3m}$. The locally specified shortened-final-width sieve has failure probability at most
$$\min\{1,nm\exp(-2^{m/3-1})\}.$$
It uses at most $nM+64$ named $F$-oracle queries, $O(n^3M)$ ideal gates for sieve control and recursive coordinate maps, $O(n^2m^2M)$ classical bit operations for label sorting and list processing, $O(M+n+w_F+a_F)$ quantum workspace, and $O(nM)$ bits to store all active labels. Here $w_F$ is the output-register width and $a_F$ is additional workspace for the supplied or constructed $F$ implementation. The $O(n^3M)$ gate count excludes the implementation of the named $F$ interface itself. An explicit $F$ circuit using $G_F(n)$ gates per call adds $O((nM+64)G_F(n))$ gates. If $F$ is constructed from only the two coherent XOR oracles for a hidden-shift pair, each call uses four $f/g$ oracle calls and adds $O(w_F)$ ordinary gates for controlled output selection; add $O((nM+64)w_F)$ selector gates, and charge any explicit circuits implementing $f$ and $g$ separately.

Since $m=\Theta(\sqrt n)$, the named $F$-query count, sieve gate count, and classical label-processing count are $2^{O(\sqrt n)}=2^{O(\sqrt{\log_2 N})}$ up to polynomial factors in $n$. The total workspace and any oracle-implementation gate costs retain the explicit interface-dependent terms above. The theorem is confined to power-of-two cyclic orders and supplied exact interfaces. It proves no polynomial-time claim, no arbitrary-$N$ version, and no algorithm for arbitrary finite abelian hidden shift.

proposed_after_items.title: Costed coherent evaluation of cyclic group powers
proposed_after_items.statement:
Inputs are a valid instance from [[def-qa-finite-cyclic-discrete-logarithm-problem]], exponent registers $u,v\in\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, and one of these access profiles:

1. a supplied coherent XOR oracle for $f(u,v)=g^u x^v$; initialize a fresh output target to $0^w$, invoke the oracle once, and return its output (the zero target need not be the encoding of the group identity); or
2. explicit reversible group-operation circuits, or separately charged named controlled-multiplication operations with the same complete-register action, for each classically specified constant and its inverse. Initialize a fresh accumulator to $\operatorname{enc}(e)$, the code of the group identity. Precompute $g_j=g^{2^j}$ and $x_j=x^{2^j}$ for $0\le j<L$, where $L=\lceil\log_2q\rceil$, by repeated squaring. For $j=0,\ldots,L-1$, use the bit $u_j$ to apply the clean controlled multiplication by $g_j$ to the accumulator, and use $v_j$ to apply the clean controlled multiplication by $x_j$. The procedure is the circuit of [[lem-qa-controlled-cyclic-multiplication-clean]] applied at each control bit.

In profile 2, return the accumulator as the function value. The exponent registers are unchanged, all work and temporary target wires are returned to their declared initial states, and each direct oracle invocation or group-operation invocation is charged under its separately declared access profile. If only an uncontrolled black-box group operation is supplied, return UNSUPPORTED_ACCESS: it does not provide a controlled call.

To supply the total coherent XOR oracle required by the hidden-subgroup sampler, profile 2 is wrapped as follows. Prepare its $w$-bit accumulator from zero to $\operatorname{enc}(e)$ with at most $w$ Pauli-$X$ gates, execute the $2L$ controlled multiplications, copy the resulting $w$-bit value by CNOT into an arbitrary target $y$, then reverse the evaluation using the separately supplied inverse-constant controlled multiplications. Finally undo the initial $X$ gates. This implements $|u,v,y\rangle\mapsto|u,v,y\oplus\operatorname{enc}(g^ux^v)\rangle$ on valid exponent codes and restores every auxiliary wire to zero. The supplied total controlled operations also define its action on invalid exponent codes; these values are the declared Boolean extension. The wrapper uses $4L$ controlled multiplications and at most $3w$ extra $X$/CNOT gates; preparation, output copying, and inverse calls are charged.

proposed_after_items.title: Correctness and clean-work cost of cyclic power evaluation
proposed_after_items.statement: For every valid encoded cyclic-group input $(G,g,x,q)$ with $q\ge2$ and every $u,v\in\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, the explicit-circuit branch of [[alg-qa-cyclic-group-power-evaluation]] writes the encoding of $g^u x^v$ into the accumulator, leaves the exponent registers unchanged, and returns every clean work and temporary target register to zero. If $L=\lceil\log_2 q\rceil$ and each controlled multiplication by a known constant has gate cost at most $C_G$, the circuit uses $2L$ controlled multiplications and $O(LC_G)$ gates per evaluation, in addition to the separately charged classical precomputation. The compute-XOR-uncompute wrapper in that algorithm implements the full target-XOR action on valid exponent codes, with its declared total extension elsewhere. If each forward and inverse-constant controlled multiplication costs at most $C_G$, that wrapper uses $4L$ such calls and at most $3w$ additional $X$/CNOT gates, hence $O(LC_G+w)$ gates, and restores its auxiliary registers to zero.
proposed_after_items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite binary expansions and group-power identities.

proposed_after_items.title: Finite cyclic discrete logarithm by Fourier sampling
proposed_after_items.statement:
Input a promised instance $(G,g,x,q)$ from [[def-qa-finite-cyclic-discrete-logarithm-problem]] and a rational confidence target $\delta=p/v$ supplied as binary positive integers $p<v$, together with supplied exact uniform-state preparation and product-QFT circuits for $\mathbb Z_q^2$, including their full-register extensions and declared costs as required by [[alg-qa-finite-abelian-hidden-subgroup-sample]]. If the direct coherent $f$ oracle is unavailable, first check that the supplied interfaces support profile 2 of [[alg-qa-cyclic-group-power-evaluation]], including classical repeated squaring and the forward and inverse-constant controlled multiplications. If they do not, return `UNSUPPORTED_ACCESS` before sampling. Otherwise construct that profile's explicit compute-XOR-uncompute oracle and precompute its repeated-squaring constants once for all samples.
Let $L=\lceil\log_2q\rceil$, computed as the bit length of $q-1$. Let $D$ be the least integer $d\ge0$ with $2^d\delta\ge1$, found by testing $d=0,1,\ldots$ using exact rational comparisons, and set $t=(1+L)D$.
Repeat the following $t$ times, with fresh registers and independent measurements:

1. Use [[alg-qa-finite-abelian-hidden-subgroup-sample]] once on $\mathbb Z_q\times\mathbb Z_q$ with hiding function $f(u,v)=g^ux^v$, obtaining a character label $(c,d)$.
2. Use [[alg-qa-euclidean-modular-inverse]] on $(q,c)$. If it returns `NO_INVERSE`, discard this sample and continue; otherwise its output is $c^{-1}\pmod q$.
3. Set $\widetilde a=d\,c^{-1}\pmod q$.
4. Compute $g^{\widetilde a}$ by binary repeated squaring using the supplied multiplication interface, then compare it with $x$ using the equality interface. Return $\widetilde a$ only if they agree.

If no iteration returns a verified value, return FAIL. A direct coherent oracle for $f$ costs one $f$ query per sample only when explicitly supplied; on the supported fallback branch, charge the controlled group operations, gates, and classical precomputation of [[alg-qa-cyclic-group-power-evaluation]]. The algorithm does not infer controlled access from an uncontrolled oracle.

proposed_after_items.title: Finite cyclic discrete-log correctness, success and costs
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $G=\langle g\rangle$ have known exact order $q\ge2$, let $x=g^a$, and let $\delta=p/v$ be supplied as binary positive integers $p<v$. Write $K$ for the sum of their bit lengths. For an access profile of [[alg-qa-finite-cyclic-discrete-logarithm]] supplying either the direct coherent $f$ oracle or the complete supported power-evaluation fallback, every returned exponent is verified and equals the unique $a\in\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$. If neither is supplied, the procedure returns `UNSUPPORTED_ACCESS` before sampling; the following sampling, success and cost guarantees concern the supported profiles. Each independent Fourier sample succeeds with probability $\varphi(q)/q\ge1/(1+\log_2q)$. Put $L=\lceil\log_2q\rceil$, let $D$ be the least integer $d\ge0$ with $2^d\delta\ge1$, and set $t=(1+L)D$. With $t$ samples, the probability of returning the exact answer is at least $1-\delta$.

Let $w$ be the supplied group-element encoding width. $$
O\!\left((L^2C_G+Lw+L^3)(1+\ln(1/\delta))\right).
$$
If one classical multiplication or equality operation on the encoding costs at most $T_G$ bit operations and modular inverses use the schoolbook extended-Euclidean algorithm, the classical bit cost of confidence preprocessing, arithmetic and verification is
$$
O\!\left(K^2+(L^2T_G+L^4)(1+\ln(1/\delta))\right).
$$
All query, gate, and classical bit bounds are conditional on the stated supplied interfaces. The exact binary QFT is counted in the ideal-gate model; no finite-set compilation cost or generic efficient group encoding is asserted.

statement.before:
Input: an integer $n\ge1$ and oracle access to a promised function $f:V_n\to V_n$ from [[def-qa-32-simon-decision-oracle-promise]]. Set $m=n+2$. For each of $m$ independent runs, initialize two ordered $n$-qubit registers $X,Y$ to $|0^n\rangle|0^n\rangle$, apply $H^{\otimes n}$ to $X$, and query the coherent XOR oracle $U_f$ once on $X,Y$. Apply the computational-basis instrument on $Y$ from [[lem-qa-32-simon-function-register-instrument]], record and discard its classical outcome, apply $H^{\otimes n}$ again to $X$, and measure $X$ in the computational basis using the same instrument. Record the resulting $y_j\in V_n$.

Form the $m\times n$ binary matrix with rows $y_1,\ldots,y_m$. Set the next pivot row to $r=1$ and scan columns $j=1,\ldots,n$ from left to right. In column $j$, search rows $r,\ldots,m$ for the first row with a $1$ in that column. If there is no such row, leave the column without a pivot and continue to the next column. Otherwise swap that row with row $r$, XOR row $r$ into every other row with a $1$ in column $j$, and increase $r$ by one. Accept (declare injective) exactly when the number of pivots is $n$.

This procedure uses exactly $n+2$ oracle queries, $2n(n+2)$ ordinary Hadamard gates, two finite measurement readouts per run, and $O(n^3)$ classical bit operations for elimination. A query is charged separately from an implementation of $f$ by [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. It makes no gate-time separation claim.

items.title: PromiseBPP
items.statement:
Let $\Pi=(Y,N)$ be a promise problem, so $Y,N\subseteq\{0,1\}^*$ are disjoint ([[def-promise-problem]]). We say $\Pi$ belongs to $\mathrm{PromiseBPP}$ if there are one fixed probabilistic Turing machine $M$ and one positive integer polynomial $p$ such that every random branch halts within $p(|x|)$ transitions and

$$ \Pr[M(x)\text{ accepts}]\ge \frac23\quad(x\in Y),\qquad \Pr[M(x)\text{ accepts}]\le \frac13\quad(x\in N). $$

The probability is over the uniform finite tape $\{0,1\}^{p(|x|)}$ of independent fair bits; after the machine halts, unused suffix bits are ignored, as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. The pair has no correctness requirement outside $Y\cup N$. For total promise pairs this is the ordinary BPP acceptance convention of [[def-rp-corp-zpp-bpp-and-pp-classes]].

references.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, Section IV.1
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 13, Section 13.2

items.title: Indexed uniform circuits convert to polynomial-time full lists
items.statement: Let $(C_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a polynomial-size Boolean circuit family generated in the indexed-gate, logspace sense of [[def-logspace-uniform-circuit-family]]. Assume a fixed polynomial $q$ bounds the number of non-input nodes of $C_n$ by $q(n)$. There is one deterministic polynomial-time machine which, on unary input $1^n$, writes a complete self-delimiting topological gate list for $C_n$, including its input count, all node records and its designated output. The resulting list describes the same circuit and therefore computes the same Boolean function.

items.title: Computational-basis instruments and conditional states on two registers
items.statement:
Let $A,B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional registers with ordered orthonormal bases $(e_a)_{a\in\Lambda}$ and $(g_b)_{b\in\Gamma}$. Define $P_a e_{a'}=\delta_{a,a'}e_a$ and $Q_b g_{b'}=\delta_{b,b'}g_b$; tensor products of these maps use [[def-qc-tensor-map]]. The maps

$$ \mathcal I_a(R)=(P_a\otimes I_B)R(P_a\otimes I_B),\qquad \mathcal J_b(R)=(I_A\otimes Q_b)R(I_A\otimes Q_b) $$

form finite instruments on $A\otimes B$. If $\psi=\sum_{a,b}c_{a,b}e_a\otimes g_b$ is a unit vector, then their outcome probabilities are

$$ p_A(a)=\sum_b|c_{a,b}|^2,\qquad p_B(b)=\sum_a|c_{a,b}|^2. $$

items.title: EQP on promise problems in the QC14 model
items.statement:
A promise problem $\Pi=(Y,N)$ belongs to $\mathrm{EQP}$ in the QC14 model if there is a full-list uniform family $(C_n)_{n\ge0}$ and a polynomial-time total acceptance predicate $A_n$ as in [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]], [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]], and [[def-qc-quantum-acceptance-probability]], using the exact gate and cost conventions of [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]] and [[def-qc-clifford-t-gate-library]], such that

$$ p_{C_{|x|}}(x)=1\quad(x\in Y),\qquad p_{C_{|x|}}(x)=0\quad(x\in N). $$

No condition is imposed on $x\notin Y\cup N$ ([[def-promise-problem]]). The finite output law is normalized by [[thm-qc-output-acceptance-law-normalizes]].

items.title: ZQP on promise problems with bounded failure
items.statement:
In this page, $\mathrm{ZQP}$ denotes the following bounded-failure zero-error promise class. All output strings receive one of the three labels, so the remaining probability is the allowed failure label $?$; the output law is normalized by [[thm-qc-output-acceptance-law-normalizes]]. items.title: Boolean circuits compile exactly into the QC14 gate alphabet
items.statement:
Let a finite Boolean DAG in the basis of [[def-boolean-circuit-size-depth-fanin-and-basis]] have $n$ ordered input bits, $m$ ordered output ports, $S$ non-input nodes and $E$ input-port uses counted with multiplicity. There is a deterministic compiler which, from its explicit topological list, emits a valid QC14 circuit over exactly $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ with the first $n$ wires as data, $m$ zero-initialized target wires, at most $S+E$ clean value wires and one additional clean scratch wire. $$ |x,y,0^{S+E+1}\rangle\longmapsto |x,y\oplus f(x),0^{S+E+1}\rangle, $$

items.title: BQP to PP and PSPACE proof obligations in the exact QC14 basis
items.statement:
## Remarks

The established containments $\mathrm{BQP}\subseteq\mathrm{PP}$ and $\mathrm{BQP}\subseteq\mathrm{PSPACE}$ remain proof obligations for the exact QC14 gate alphabet $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$, whose entries lie in $\mathbb Q(\zeta_8)=\mathbb Q(i,\sqrt2)$ ([[def-qc-bqp-promise-class]], [[def-qc-clifford-t-gate-library]]). The PP route must encode amplitudes and acceptance weights over this number field, prove the required GapP closure, and compare against the strict $1/2$ threshold. The BQP thresholds $2/3$ and $1/3$ differ by $1/3$; each is at distance $1/6$ from $1/2$ (equivalently, $2p-1$ has margin at least $1/3$). A rational path count cannot simply replace the exact $\mathbb Q(\zeta_8)$ computation, since the probabilities can contain $\sqrt2$. The PSPACE route needs exact-field or certified-precision recursive evaluation with explicit bit-length and space bounds for each arithmetic and threshold step. The source containment arguments are context, not local proof suppliers; no containment item is claimed here.

items.title: Simon injectivity decision promise with XOR-oracle access
items.statement:
Fix $n\ge1$ and put $V_n=\{0,1\}^n$, with coordinatewise addition $\oplus$ over $\mathbb F_2$ and cardinality $N=2^n$. For $s,y\in V_n$, define the dot product $s\cdot y=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}s_jy_j\pmod 2$. A table code consists of a unary header $1^n0$ followed by the $n$-bit words $f(x)$ in lexicographic order of $x\in V_n$; this identifies function instances with binary strings as in [[def-promise-problem]], [[def-finite-field-and-its-order]], and [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]].

The YES promise set $Y_n$ consists of table codes of injective maps $f:V_n\to V_n$. The NO promise set $N_n$ consists of codes for which there is a nonzero $s\in V_n$ such that, for every $x,y\in V_n$,

$$ f(x)=f(y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y=x\ \text{or}\ y=x\oplus s. $$

The sets are disjoint: every NO function has a collision between the distinct inputs $x$ and $x\oplus s$. Its mask is unique, since two different nonzero masks would give a third distinct input in the same fiber. Classical query access returns $f(x)$ at a chosen address. Quantum query access is the coherent XOR oracle $U_f|x,z\rangle=|x,z\oplus f(x)\rangle$ of [[def-qc-coherent-function-oracle]], which is unitary and involutive by [[thm-qc-reversible-xor-oracle-unitary]]. Each call is one query; query charges remain separate from ordinary gate costs by [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. In the query model the table is not supplied as gate data; the table code fixes the promised function only.

items.title: Simon promise decision by sampled rank
items.statement:
Input: an integer $n\ge1$ and oracle access to a promised function $f:V_n\to V_n$ from [[def-qa-32-simon-decision-oracle-promise]]. Set $m=n+2$. For each of $m$ independent runs, initialize two ordered $n$-qubit registers $X,Y$ to $|0^n\rangle|0^n\rangle$, apply $H^{\otimes n}$ to $X$, and query the coherent XOR oracle $U_f$ once on $X,Y$. Apply the computational-basis instrument on $Y$ from [[lem-qa-32-simon-function-register-instrument]], record and discard its classical outcome, apply $H^{\otimes n}$ again to $X$, and measure $X$ in the computational basis using the same instrument. Record the resulting $y_j\in V_n$.

Form the $m\times n$ binary matrix with rows $y_1,\ldots,y_m$. Set the next pivot row to $r=1$ and scan columns $j=1,\ldots,n$ from left to right. In column $j$, search rows $r,\ldots,m$ for the first row with a $1$ in that column. If there is no such row, leave the column without a pivot and continue to the next column. Otherwise swap that row with row $r$, XOR row $r$ into every other row with a $1$ in column $j$, and increase $r$ by one. Accept (declare injective) exactly when the number of pivots is $n$.

This procedure uses exactly $n+2$ oracle queries, $2n(n+2)$ ordinary Hadamard gates, two finite measurement readouts per run, and $O(n^3)$ classical bit operations for elimination. A query is charged separately from an implementation of $f$ by [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]. It makes no gate-time separation claim.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, Chapter 3, Section 3.2
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, Chapter 1, Section 1.6

items.title: Classical randomized Simon decision requires square-root-many queries
items.statement: Let $N=2^n$ with $n\ge4$. A classical randomized adaptive algorithm that, given only classical query access $x\mapsto f(x)$ to the Simon decision promise of [[def-qa-32-simon-decision-oracle-promise]], must decide injective versus nonzero-mask two-to-one with worst-case error at most $1/3$ requires $\Omega(\sqrt N)=\Omega(2^{n/2})$ queries. Ordinary classical computation between queries is unrestricted.

items.title: Simon rank test correctness and linear query cost
items.statement:
For every $n\ge1$, the sample in [[alg-qa-32-simon-query-rank-test]] is uniform on $V_n$ when $f$ is YES, and uniform on $s^\perp=\{y:s\cdot y=0\}$ when $f$ is NO with mask $s\ne0$. The rank test rejects every NO instance. On YES its error probability is at most

It uses exactly $n+2$ queries and $O(n^3)$ classical bit operations.

proposed_after_items.title: PromiseBPP
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $\Pi=(Y,N)$ be a promise problem, so $Y,N\subseteq\{0,1\}^*$ are disjoint ([[def-promise-problem]]). We say $\Pi$ belongs to $\mathrm{PromiseBPP}$ if there are one fixed probabilistic Turing machine $M$ and one positive integer polynomial $p$ such that every random branch halts within $p(|x|)$ transitions and

$$ \Pr[M(x)\text{ accepts}]\ge \frac23\quad(x\in Y),\qquad \Pr[M(x)\text{ accepts}]\le \frac13\quad(x\in N). $$

The probability is over the uniform finite tape $\{0,1\}^{p(|x|)}$ of independent fair bits; after the machine halts, unused suffix bits are ignored, as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. The pair has no correctness requirement outside $Y\cup N$. For total promise pairs this is the ordinary BPP acceptance convention of [[def-rp-corp-zpp-bpp-and-pp-classes]].

The resulting list describes the same circuit and therefore computes the same Boolean function.

items.statement: Fix a nonnegative integer $q$ and dimension $D=2^q$, independent of input length. Given a $D\times D$ unitary whose entries have polynomial-time Cauchy names from a finite description and a rational $0<\eta<1/2$, a deterministic polynomial-time procedure outputs a circuit on its $q$ data wires, with a constant number of clean ancillas returned to zero, for which there is a unit scalar $\lambda$ with $\|V-\lambda U\|\le\eta$. The procedure has polynomial bit cost and polynomial gate count in the description length and $1/\eta$. Scalar phase is immaterial only for this unconditional circuit. The construction uses complex Givens elimination with robust pivoting, a constant-width decomposition into unconditional one-qubit $SU(2)$ rotations and CNOT gates, and the finite-precision compiler of [[thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-bit-complexity]]. Its exact reversible-control subconstruction gives Toffoli from $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ by the parity-phase identity in the proof.
items.axiom_use: None; the decomposition is a finite constructive matrix algorithm.

items.statement:
Let a QMA verifier have completeness $c$ and soundness $s$ with $0\le s<c\le1$, and put $\gamma=c-s$. For $0<\delta<1$, choose an integer

$$r\ge 2\gamma^{-2}\ln(1/\delta).$$

Then the parallel verifier of [[alg-qa-33-qma-parallel-majority-amplification]] has completeness at least $1-\delta$ and soundness at most $\delta$. On a NO input its soundness bound holds for every joint $r$-block witness state, including entangled states. The repetition uses $r$ witness blocks and $r$ verifier copies, so choosing the least integer $r$ satisfying the bound gives polynomial size when $\gamma^{-1}$ and $\ln(1/\delta)$ are polynomially bounded. The probability bounds hold for every larger $r$ as well.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite tensor products, finite POVMs, and a choice-free operator moment bound.

statement.after:
Let $x\in\mathbb R^n$ be nonzero with exact norm, ℓ2 sample access, and entry-query access, and let $y\in\mathbb R^n$ have entry-query access and known norm. For $0<\epsilon\le1$, a positive integer $m\ge16/\epsilon^2$, and a positive integer $r$ with $2^{-r}\le\delta<1$, there is a finite estimator using the lower median of $r$ block means, with $mr$ samples from $x$ and at most $mr$ entry queries to each of $x$ and $y$, such that
$$\mathbb P\left(|\widehat\mu-\langle x,y\rangle|>\epsilon\|x\|_2\|y\|_2\right)\le\delta.$$
If $y=0$, return $0$ without sampling. All sample and entry-query costs are charged.

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ have the row/column entry-query and ℓ2-sampling access of [[def-qa-34-l2-sample-query-access]], let $F=\|A\|_F>0$, and fix a row $i$ with $\|D_{i,*}\|_2>0$. Here $D$ is the ModFKV matrix description from [[alg-qa-34-modfkv-low-rank-description]] and its success event is specified by [[thm-qa-34-modfkv-low-rank-approximation]]. Assume
$$0<\sigma\le F,\qquad 0<\epsilon\le\tfrac14\sqrt{\sigma/F},\qquad \epsilon^2\le\eta\le1,\qquad 0<\delta<1.$$
Assume countable choice and dependent choice, and model the finite sketch history together with the countably many potential fresh row-sample calls in the adaptive refinement by the joint product probability law supplied by [[thm-countable-product-of-probability-spaces]]. After a finite row-refinement stop, the capped rejection sampler uses its finite conditional law; the joint execution law is the countable mixture over finite stopping histories together with any residual nontermination event, on which no rejection call occurs.
There is a Tang recommendation procedure whose sketch succeeds unconditionally with probability at least $1-\delta/3$. For every fixed successful description having $D_{i,*}\ne0$, its conditional probability of a successful row estimate and an accepted sample is at least $1-2\delta/3$. Thus the unconditional probability of a nonzero realized target row together with failure of these guarantees is at most $\delta$. If the nonzero-row promise holds almost surely, this implies overall success probability at least $1-\delta$. For every fixed successful sketch and successful row estimate, the law of the accepted classical sample is within total variation $\epsilon$ (where $d_{\rm TV}(p,q)=\tfrac12\sum_a|p(a)-q(a)|$ as in [[def-qa-34-end-to-end-error-contract]]) of the normalized squared-entry distribution of $D_{i,*}$. A capped sampling failure returns FAIL; no conditional distribution is assigned to a zero target row. The nonzero-row hypothesis is a promise on the realized description, not an assumed ability to compute its full row norm. The failure bound is unconditional; it is not a claim that conditioning on a nonzero realized row preserves ModFKV's confidence. At constant precision its query and arithmetic-time bounds are respectively
$$\widetilde O\!\left(\frac{F^{18}}{\sigma^{18}\epsilon^8\eta^4}\right),\qquad \widetilde O\!\left(\frac{F^{24}}{\sigma^{24}\epsilon^{12}\eta^6}\right).$$
For the final $\epsilon$ total-variation guarantee, the finite row refinement below adds a query and arithmetic-time factor $\widetilde O(\|A_{i,*}\|_2^2/\|D_{i,*}\|_2^2)$. These bounds hold on the successful event; refinement terminates almost surely for every realized description satisfying the nonzero-row promise. Hidden logarithms, access-structure preprocessing, arithmetic precision, and the cost of writing the returned sample remain charged. The result is conditional on this exact input model and does not output $D$ as a full matrix or a full classical amplitude list.

items.title: Finite distributions, entropy, divergence, and stochastic matrices
items.statement:
For a finite nonempty set identified with $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, a **probability vector** is $p=(p_i)_{i=1}^k$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$; it is the outcome-weight vector of a finite probability space ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). Its Shannon entropy in natural units is
$$H(p):=-\sum_{i=1}^k p_i\ln p_i,$$
with $0\ln0:=0$. For probability vectors $p,q$, the relative entropy is
$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one. For $X\in[0,1]^m$, the dot product $pX^{\mathsf T}$ is the acceptance probability under distribution $p$.

These definitions use finite sets only; entropy is between $0$ and $\ln k$, as proved where needed below.

items.title: Finite communication problem and protocol model
items.statement:
A **finite communication problem** consists of nonempty finite input sets $X,Y$, disjoint sets $YES,NO\subseteq X\times Y$ with nonempty promise $P=YES\cup NO$, and a required output bit on promised pairs. This is the finite-relation generalization of a binary-string promise problem ([[def-promise-problem]]): choose fixed injective labels $c_X:X\to\{0,1\}^*$ and $c_Y:Y\to\{0,1\}^*$, and encode a pair by
$$e(x,y):=1^{|c_X(x)|}0\,c_X(x)c_Y(y).$$
The unary length prefix makes $e$ injective, so $e(YES)$ and $e(NO)$ are disjoint subsets of $\{0,1\}^*$. This encoding only formalizes the relation; it is not a transmitted message or part of communication cost unless a protocol explicitly sends it. A protocol specifies who receives each input, the message schedule and number of rounds, each message alphabet or finite-dimensional register ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]), the local maps that produce messages, the referee's finite POVM ([[def-qc-povm-and-outcome-law]]) and output rule, and any shared randomness or entanglement. A quantum message state is a density operator, meaning nonnegative with trace one ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). Its worst-case error is the supremum of the probability of a wrong output over promised input pairs; its communication cost is the maximum total number of transmitted bits or qubits on any promised input. Local computation, referee computation, and shared resources are separately declared and are not silently included in that communication count.

In a simultaneous-message protocol (SMP), Alice and Bob each send one message to a referee without seeing the other's message. For classical private-coin SMP with no shared resource, conditional on inputs $x,y$ the two messages are independent, so their joint law is a product of their individual message distributions. For quantum SMP with no shared entanglement or randomness, the received state is a product of the two locally prepared density operators. These factorization properties are part of the stated resource model.
proof_obligations: Specify worst-case promised-input error and separate communicated bits/qubits from local work and shared resources.

items.title: Equality communication problem
items.statement: For $n\ge1$, the **Equality promise problem** has $X=Y=\{0,1\}^n$, YES set $\{(x,x):x\in\{0,1\}^n\}$ and NO set $\{(x,y):x\ne y\}$. The required output is $1$ on YES and $0$ on NO. This is a total promise problem, and a bounded-error protocol must meet its error bound on every pair.
proof_obligations: Use the total promise and fixed output convention.

items.title: Code-based quantum fingerprint
items.statement:
For $n\ge1$ and $N\ge1$, let $E:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^N$ be a binary code map. Define its relative distance by
$$\delta(E):=\frac1N\min_{x\ne y}d_H(E(x),E(y)),$$
where $d_H(u,v):=|\{i<N:u_i\ne v_i\}|$ and the minimum is over distinct inputs. Thus duplicate codewords are allowed and give relative distance $0$, and $\delta(E)\in[0,1]$; the minimum is over a nonempty finite set because $n\ge1$. For every such map, with no positive-distance assumption, let $m=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ and use the ordered computational basis of the $m$-qubit index register, padding unused indices by zero amplitude. The **fingerprint state** of $x$ is
$$|h_x\rangle:=\frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}|i\rangle|E_i(x)\rangle,$$
where $E_i(x)$ is bit $i$ of $E(x)$, indexed from $0$ to $N-1$. It is a vector in the $(m+1)$-qubit index-and-data register. The following theorem proves it is normalized and computes its overlap. This is a state definition; it makes no uniformity or encoder-time claim.

items.title: Constant private-coin error reduction by repetition
items.statement: If a private-coin simultaneous-message Equality protocol has worst-case error at most 1/3 and each sender sends at most c bits, then for any fixed odd t independent repetitions followed by majority have error at most exp(−t/48) and each sender sends at most t(c+1) bits under a fixed-length encoding.
proof_obligations: State finite message padding and independence of private random tapes across repetitions.

items.statement: In an SMP Equality protocol on n≥2 bits with worst-case error at most 1/3, no shared randomness or entanglement, and fixed q-qubit messages, each sender must transmit Ω(log n) qubits. For fixed Bob input y, the referee’s equality POVM separates ρ_y from each ρ_x, x≠y, by trace distance at least 1/3; packing d×d density matrices in trace distance yields 2ⁿ≤(26d^(3/2))^(d²), d=2^q, and hence q=Ω(log n).
proof_obligations: Handle complex Hermitian coordinates, entry bounds, trace-distance mesh, the two senders, and the fixed message-dimension convention.

items.title: Simultaneous-message equality by quantum fingerprints
items.statement:
**Inputs:** Integers $n\ge1$, $N\ge1$, and $r\ge1$; a fixed binary code map $E:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^N$ known to both senders and the referee; and inputs $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$. The parties use no shared randomness or shared entanglement. State preparation and local computation are permitted and are not included in the communicated-qubit count.

**Output:** A bit $b\in\{0,1\}$, where $b=1$ means the referee declares $x=y$ and $b=0$ means the referee declares $x\ne y$.

Set $m=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ and $L=m+1$. Alice prepares $r$ copies of the fingerprint state $|h_x\rangle$ and sends the $r$ registers, each with $L$ qubits, to the referee. Bob prepares and sends $r$ copies of $|h_y\rangle$ in the same way. The referee groups the received registers as pairs $(A_j,B_j)$ in increasing order $j=1,\ldots,r$. For each pair, the referee appends a fresh control qubit $|0\rangle$, applies the Hadamard gate $H=2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$, then applies one Fredkin gate to each of the $L$ corresponding pairs of message wires, using this fresh control qubit as the gate's control. The referee applies $H$ again and measures the control in the computational basis. If any test returns $1$, stop the loop and output $b=0$. If all $r$ tests return $0$, output $b=1$. Thus each sender transmits exactly $rL$ qubits, and the referee uses at most $rL$ Fredkin gates and $2r$ Hadamard gates.
proof_obligations: Expand the H-controlled-swap-H state and count transmitted wires and Fredkin gates; pad the index by zero amplitudes when N is not a power of two.

items.title: Fingerprint swap-test error and communication cost
items.statement:
Let $n,N\ge1$ and let $E:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^N$ have relative distance $\delta(E)=\delta\in(0,1]$. Equal inputs yield antisymmetric probability $0$; unequal inputs yield $p\ge p_0=[1-(1-\delta)^2]/2=\delta-\delta^2/2>0$. For $0<\epsilon<1$, set
$$r=\left\lceil\frac{\ln(1/\epsilon)}{-\ln(1-p_0)}\right\rceil.$$
The bounded loop in [[alg-qa-35-swap-test-fingerprint]] halts after at most $r$ tests. On $r$ fresh pairs, declaring unequal iff any anti outcome occurs gives worst-case error at most $\epsilon$, with $r(\lceil\log_2N\rceil+1)$ qubits sent by each party. If $N\le Cn$ and $C,\delta$ are fixed, this is $O((1+\log n)(1+\log(1/\epsilon)))$ qubits per sender, conditional on a supplied code with those parameters.
proof_obligations: Keep δ>0 and ε∈(0,1); handle δ=1; distinguish a supplied efficient code from the nonuniform existence result.

proposed_after_items.title: Finite distributions, entropy, divergence, and stochastic matrices
proposed_after_items.statement:
For a finite nonempty set identified with $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, a **probability vector** is $p=(p_i)_{i=1}^k$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$; it is the outcome-weight vector of a finite probability space ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). Its Shannon entropy in natural units is
$$H(p):=-\sum_{i=1}^k p_i\ln p_i,$$
with $0\ln0:=0$. For probability vectors $p,q$, the relative entropy is
$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one. For $X\in[0,1]^m$, the dot product $pX^{\mathsf T}$ is the acceptance probability under distribution $p$.

These definitions use finite sets only; entropy is between $0$ and $\ln k$, as proved where needed below.

proposed_after_items.title: Symmetric and antisymmetric swap-test measurement
proposed_after_items.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. On $H\otimes H$ define the **swap** $F$ by $F(u\otimes v)=v\otimes u$ and linear extension. Define the symmetric and antisymmetric effects
$$P_+=(I+F)/2,\qquad P_-=(I-F)/2.$$
The “equal” outcome corresponds to $P_+$ and “unequal” to $P_-$. When $H\ne\{0\}$, the following theorem proves well-definedness as a two-outcome projective measurement and calculates its pure-product law. For $H=\{0\}$ the operators are still defined, but no density input or measurement interpretation under the cited nonzero-space convention is asserted.

proposed_after_items.title: Finite communication problem and protocol model
proposed_after_items.statement:
A **finite communication problem** consists of nonempty finite input sets $X,Y$, disjoint sets $YES,NO\subseteq X\times Y$ with nonempty promise $P=YES\cup NO$, and a required output bit on promised pairs. This is the finite-relation generalization of a binary-string promise problem ([[def-promise-problem]]): choose fixed injective labels $c_X:X\to\{0,1\}^*$ and $c_Y:Y\to\{0,1\}^*$, and encode a pair by
$$e(x,y):=1^{|c_X(x)|}0\,c_X(x)c_Y(y).$$
The unary length prefix makes $e$ injective, so $e(YES)$ and $e(NO)$ are disjoint subsets of $\{0,1\}^*$. This encoding only formalizes the relation; it is not a transmitted message or part of communication cost unless a protocol explicitly sends it. A protocol specifies who receives each input, the message schedule and number of rounds, each message alphabet or finite-dimensional register ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]), the local maps that produce messages, the referee's finite POVM ([[def-qc-povm-and-outcome-law]]) and output rule, and any shared randomness or entanglement. A quantum message state is a density operator, meaning nonnegative with trace one ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). Its worst-case error is the supremum of the probability of a wrong output over promised input pairs; its communication cost is the maximum total number of transmitted bits or qubits on any promised input. Local computation, referee computation, and shared resources are separately declared and are not silently included in that communication count.

In a simultaneous-message protocol (SMP), Alice and Bob each send one message to a referee without seeing the other's message. For classical private-coin SMP with no shared resource, conditional on inputs $x,y$ the two messages are independent, so their joint law is a product of their individual message distributions. For quantum SMP with no shared entanglement or randomness, the received state is a product of the two locally prepared density operators. These factorization properties are part of the stated resource model.
proof_obligations: Specify worst-case promised-input error and separate communicated bits/qubits from local work and shared resources.
